描述_EN: batik patterned cloths are worn by both men and women in java, the kain panjang being the skirt or waist cloth worn by men. batik is the name given in indonesia to the process of applying resist-dyed patterns to cloth. colour combinations of blue and white, red and white, and red and blue, as found in this example, which was probably made in cirebon, were common in batik cloths from the northern coastal area which had always been subject to considerable influence from external trade, both from the east (china) and the west (india). the main centres of production were the areas around the sultanates of surakarta and jogyakarta or yogyakarta in central java, and the coastal areas of cirebon, indramayu, pekalongan and lasem in the north and the area around garut in western java.

描述_EN: cizhou wares were utilitarian at their time of production and were made in relatively large numbers. this vase is made in a shape known as meiping (prunus vase), although it was most likely used to store alcohol. this vase is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the term cizhou encapsulates a range of wares made in several regions of northern china, often consisting of a course stoneware body covered with a white slip (a thin layer of wet clay), and then decorated with a bold design in a contrasting colour.

描述_EN: cartier-bresson helped develop the street photography style that has influenced generations of photographers that followed. he documented the liberation of paris, the collapse of the nationalist regime in china, gandhi's funeral and the partitioning of berlin. he sought to capture the 'everyday' in his photographs and took great interest in recording human activity. he wrote, "for me the camera is a sketch book, an instrument of intuition and spontaneity, the master of the instant which, in visual terms, questions and decides simultaneously. it is by economy of means that one arrives at simplicity of expression." as a reporter and co-founder of the magnum photography agency, cartier-bresson accepted his responsibility to supply information to a world in a hurry. in order to 'give a meaning' to the world, one has to feel involved in what one frames through the viewfinder. the victoria and albert museum has over 440 photographs by henri cartier-bresson (1908-2004), a french photographer who is considered to be one of the fathers of photojournalism and masters of candid photography. this attitude requires concentration, discipline of mind, sensitivity, and a sense of geometry.
描述_ZN: 卡蒂埃-布列松帮助发展了街头摄影风格，影响了后来的几代摄影家。 他记录了巴黎的解放、中国民族主义政权的崩溃、甘地的葬礼和柏林的分治。 他试图在他的照片中捕捉 "日常"，并对记录人类活动表现出极大兴趣。 他写道："对我来说，相机是一本素描书，是直觉和自发性的工具，是瞬间的主人，在视觉方面，它同时质疑和决定。 它是通过经济手段来达到简单的表达。"作为一名记者和Magnum摄影机构的创始人之一，卡地亚-布列松接受了他的责任，向这个匆忙的世界提供信息。 为了给世界 "赋予意义"，一个人必须感觉参与到他通过取景器拍摄的东西中。 维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有超过440张亨利-卡蒂尔-布列松（1908-2004）的照片，这位法国摄影师被认为是新闻摄影之父和坦率摄影的大师之一。 这种态度需要集中精力、心智的约束、敏感和几何感。

描述_EN: cartier-bresson helped develop the street photography style that has influenced generations of photographers that followed. he documented the liberation of paris, the collapse of the nationalist regime in china, gandhi's funeral and the partitioning of berlin. he sought to capture the 'everyday' in his photographs and took great interest in recording human activity. he wrote, "for me the camera is a sketch book, an instrument of intuition and spontaneity, the master of the instant which, in visual terms, questions and decides simultaneously. it is by economy of means that one arrives at simplicity of expression." as a reporter and co-founder of the magnum photography agency, cartier-bresson accepted his responsibility to supply information to a world in a hurry. in order to 'give a meaning' to the world, one has to feel involved in what one frames through the viewfinder. the victoria and albert museum has over 440 photographs by henri cartier-bresson (1908-2004), a french photographer who is considered to be one of the fathers of photojournalism and masters of candid photography. this attitude requires concentration, discipline of mind, sensitivity, and a sense of geometry.
描述_ZN: 卡蒂埃-布列松帮助发展了街头摄影风格，影响了后来的几代摄影家。 他记录了巴黎的解放、中国民族主义政权的崩溃、甘地的葬礼和柏林的分治。 他试图在他的照片中捕捉 "日常"，并对记录人类活动表现出极大兴趣。 他写道："对我来说，相机是一本素描书，是直觉和自发性的工具，是瞬间的主人，在视觉方面，它同时质疑和决定。 它是通过经济手段来达到简单的表达。"作为一名记者和Magnum摄影机构的创始人之一，卡地亚-布列松接受了他的责任，向这个匆忙的世界提供信息。 为了给世界 "赋予意义"，一个人必须感觉参与到他通过取景器拍摄的东西中。 维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有超过440张亨利-卡蒂尔-布列松（1908-2004）的照片，这位法国摄影师被认为是新闻摄影之父和坦率摄影的大师之一。 这种态度需要集中精力、心智的约束、敏感和几何感。

描述_EN: after 1949, with the founding of the people’s republic, he settled in beijing and became director of the new central academy of fine arts and chairman of the national artists’ association. on returning to china, xu became a powerful force for the introduction of western art through his teaching, writing and exhibitions; his influence was rivalled only by liu haisu and lin fengmian. the work was made in summer 1944, shortly before the artist had a medical operation. horse is xu's favourite subject matter. it was given by him to miss ellen wilkinson (1891-1947), a prominent member of the labour cabinet in clement attlee's government. it was given to the v&a by her sister, miss ann wilkinson, after her death. xu beihong (1895-1953) was an important early pioneer in the introduction of western art to china and in the adaptation of it to chinese character. xu was born in a village in yixing, jiangsu province. in the period from 1919 to 1927, he studied at the ecole des beaux-arts in paris, acquiring a solid foundation in the western academic tradition. he studied painting in his hometown and shanghai before having an opportunity to go to europe. this painting reflects the artist's principal artistic concern, namely, to bring together the western academic tradition of painting and chinese aesthetics through ink techniques. as one of the most acclaimed painters and educators in modern china, he influenced the development of 20th-century chinese painting.

描述_EN: by the 1940s, under the influence of western tailoring, the dress had become tailored to be much more form-fitting (and fashionable). the use of synthetic silk reflects also the modernisation of technology in dress production. on its own, the qipao is itself a modernised form of the dress worn by manchu and han women of the qing dynasty (1644-1911). during the republican period (1911-1949), the qipao was promoted as the dress of modern china, identifiably 'chinese' on the one hand, and moving away from 'feudal' associations with the imperial past. in its earlier form, the modern qipao was relatively loose and comfortable, a symbol of simplicity and frugality. this dress is also padded with a thicker lining, so may have been made to be worn during cooler seasons. the cut of this dress is narrowed at the waist, and a hidden side zip allows the dress to fit the frame more closely.
描述_ZN: 到了1940年代，在西方裁缝的影响下，这种衣服变得更加合身（和时尚）。 合成丝的使用也反映了礼服生产中技术的现代化。 就其本身而言，旗袍本身是清朝（1644-1911年）满汉妇女所穿服装的一种现代形式。 在共和国时期（1911-1949），旗袍被宣传为现代中国的服装，一方面可以识别为 "中国人"，另一方面也摆脱了与帝国时代的 "封建 "联系。 在其早期形式中，现代旗袍是相对宽松和舒适的，是简单和节俭的象征。 这件衣服也是用厚衬垫的，所以可能是为了在凉爽的季节穿的。 这条裙子的剪裁在腰部收窄，隐藏的侧边拉链使裙子更贴合框架。

描述_ZN: Green-glazed, incised, single-handled jug, Northern dynasty, 21.3 cm high, mouth 11 cm in diameter, foot 12 cm in diameter, the mouth of the jug with a rim, short neck, sloping shoulders, and bulging belly, supported by a solid pie-shaped foot. The vertical tether is symmetrically placed on both sides of the shoulder, with a short tubular stream on the other side and a curved handle on the side opposite the stream. The form is full and rounded. The body is heavy and off-white. Inside and outside the pot are glazed, glaze green, glaze layer transparent, glaze glass feeling is strong, glaze open fine fragment pattern.　　The entire body of the pot is decorated with incised flowers, and the decoration is divided into three layers, with the shoulders and the lower part of the belly with the supine and overlapping lotus petal patterns respectively, and with the lingzhi pattern between the supine and overlapping lotus petal patterns, separated by the string pattern between the patterns. The pattern is clearly layered and skillfully decorated.　　After Buddhism was introduced to China in the Eastern Han Dynasty, it tended to flourish during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, which was reflected in the decoration of porcelain, where lotus, lotus petal, and lonicera motifs were very popular, with distinctive features of the period.　　This object was donated by Mr. Chen Wanli, a researcher at the National Palace Museum and a world-renowned ceramic expert in modern times. The ceramics donated by Mr. Chen have enriched the collection of the National Palace Museum, and some of the objects are preferred exhibits in successive ceramic displays at the National Palace Museum.

描述_ZN: Earthenware white tiger tile, Han Dynasty, 19.3 cm in diameter.　　The White Tiger is the deity in charge of the West, and together with the Green Dragon, Vermilion Bird, and Xuanwu, they form the Four Gods (also called the Four Spirits). 描述_ZN: There are ten stone drums, made of granite, about 90 cm high and 60 cm in diameter.　　The stone drums are named after the drum-shaped stone on which the text is carved in seal script. The stone is engraved with ten poems describing the hunting trips in big seal script, so it is also called "Hunting Jie". The poems are all in four lines, which are similar to the poem "Che Tackle" in "Shi Jing Xiao Ya". It is the earliest surviving set of stone inscriptions in China. Since the Tang Dynasty, Wei Yingyi and Han Yu made the "Song of the Stone Drum" to express the chapter, and then it became a big phenomenon in the world. The age of the stone drum has been said to be Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn Period, Warring States, Qin Dynasty, Han Dynasty, Jin Dynasty, Northern Wei, Western Wei, Northern Zhou and so on. Later, after examination and research by jinshi scholars from various aspects such as its content, script and calligraphic style, it was identified as a relic of the Qin Dynasty. The exact date has not yet been agreed upon, but among those who claim that it is a relic of the Qin Dynasty, there are also sayings such as Duke Wen of Qin, Duke Mu of Qin, Duke Xiang of Qin, and Duke Xian of Qin.　　The stone drums were found in the early Tang Dynasty in Tianxing, Shaanxi Province (now Fengxiang, Shaanxi Province). After that, it was moved to Tokyo (now Kaifeng) in the Song Dynasty, and when the Jin Dynasty broke the Song Dynasty, it was moved to Yanjing (now Beijing). After several migrations, the text was much worn out and damaged. Tokyo was filled with gold, and then removed after transporting Yanjing. One of the drums has no characters.　　Some of the characters in the stone drum script are the same as those in the pre-Han script. It is also called the Great Seal Script, which is said to have been made by the Emperor Shih Zhou during the reign of King Xuan of Zhou. It was popular in the Qin Dynasty during the Spring and Autumn Period, and was further simplified and linearized in the process. The calligraphy of this stone drum script is so simple and ancient that Kang Youwei of the Qing Dynasty said, "It is like a gold inlay on the ground or a group of clouds of grass. The seal script of some calligraphers in the Qing dynasty was mostly based on this.　　The topos of the stone drum script in the Forbidden City include the topos of the early Ming Dynasty, which was collected by Sun Kehong in the Ming Dynasty and is a famous book in China.　　It was recorded in Li Jifu's "Yuanhe County Map" in Tang Dynasty, Ouyang Xiu's "Ji Gu Lu" in Song Dynasty, Zhao Mingcheng's "Jin Shi Lu" and Zheng Qiao's "Shi Gu Wen Kao".

描述_ZN: Scroll of "Hibiscus and Golden Rooster", painted by Zhao Ji, Emperor Huizong of the Northern Song Dynasty, on silk, with color. 81.5 cm in length and 53.6 cm in width.　　As a separate painting discipline, Song dynasty flower and bird paintings had reached a high level of artistry in terms of both painting technique and expression, and "Hibiscus and Brocade Rooster" is one of the finest. This painting is a flower and bird painting depicting a golden autumn scene. In the picture, the hibiscus is in full bloom, gently trembling in the wind, and the butterflies are chasing and playing with each other, attracting the pheasants that fall on the branches to gaze back and stare. On the upper right side of this painting, Zhao Ji of Emperor Huizong of Song Dynasty inscribed in a lean gold font, "Autumn is strong and resists frost. It has been known to have all five virtues, and is more at ease than the eider duck", with the inscription "Xuanhedian imperial system and calligraphy" on the lower right and "One person in the world" in cursive script. Chicken in China has always been "virtuous bird", "Han Shi Wai Zhuan" contains: "the chicken has five virtues: head wearing a crown, also; foot fighting distance, also; enemy in front, dare to fight, also brave; see the food to call, also benevolent; guard the night not lost, also letter", can be seen in both civil and military, benevolent and brave, faithful and dedicated, It is no wonder that the emperor of the generation with the greatest talent also left the poem "Known to be full of five virtues, ease is better than eider ducks", revealing the praise for the noble character of ease, thus reflecting the humanistic meaning of Chinese flower and bird painting.　　In the works of Zhao Ji, the artistic style is very different from that of the simple and elegant ones, such as "Hibiscus and Pheasant" and "Mountain Bird with Plum Blossoms" (in the collection of the National Palace Museum, Taipei), and the simple and awkward ones such as "Willow Crow" (in the collection of the Shanghai Museum) and "Bird with Loquat and Mountain". Through a comparative analysis of brush and ink styles, Mr. Xu Bangda points out that the former is not by Zhao Ji, but by the painter of the Academy, while the latter is his own handwriting, a view shared by most art historical researchers. In addition, the extant record of the Southern Song court's collection of paintings in volume 3 of the "Southern Song Pavilion Continued Records" includes this painting in the category of "imperial inscriptions" alongside "imperial paintings," suggesting that the "Hibiscus and Golden Rooster" is merely a poem inscribed by Zhao Ji himself.

描述_ZN: Song Stepping" scroll, Southern Song Dynasty, by Ma Yuan, on silk, color, 192.5 cm long, 111 cm wide.　　"It is a very old custom in the countryside of southern China that when the villagers have worked hard for a year and finally have a good harvest, the whole village, men, women and children, step to the beat, sing and dance, celebrating the harvest and thanking nature for its bounty, just as happily and lively as the New Year festival.　　On the surface, the painting looks like a landscape painting showing the natural landscape, but in reality it is a customary painting depicting human life. The author, Ma Yuan, has arranged a few pointillist figures in the picture so that the theme of the painting can be fully displayed. Instead of depicting the whole picture of the countryside singing scene, the painter has chosen a few very representative figures of the villagers: a middle-aged villager, who has drunk a few bowls of wine out of joy, stumbles, staggers and is drunk, but the gourd holding the wine is not forgotten and is still properly carried on his shoulder; an old man with a white beard, who has also drunk a lot of wine, has one hand on a crutch and the other hand raised high, with his feet off the ground and his hands dancing. Feet off the ground, hands dancing, unusual excitement. Their demeanor is not in line with their age, so they seem particularly comical and ridiculous. After depicting the adults, Ma Yuan felt that it was not enough to express the joyful and indulgent atmosphere, so he specially arranged two young children, male and female, in the lower left corner of the painting, who turn around and stare at their elders with astonished eyes, why is the usual parental bullying and majesty gone? The older girl, who also covered her mouth with her hand, was secretly laughing. These two groups of characters echo each other and set each other off, pushing the joyful and happy mood of the "song" to the extreme. However, if we look closely at the picture, the author has only drawn six people, but he has managed to render the atmosphere so well. From these six villagers, one can fully feel the singing, the beat of the ground and the laughter coming from the whole village. Ma Yuan's artistic expression of "taking one for ten" and "seeing the big with the small" is really brilliant.　　A few figures occupy a small place in the picture, but they are the most striking. The lines of the figures are strong and vigorous, and their dynamics are lively and interesting, all showing Ma Yuan's extraordinary skills.　　Ma Yuan's method of painting the mountains and rocks is also extremely distinctive. He used the side sweep of the brush to express the steepness of the mountains and the texture of the hard rocks, which are as if they were split by a giant axe. Ma Yuan also innovated in the composition of his paintings. He liked to concentrate the rocks in the picture on a certain corner to form a contrast between reality and fiction, which gave him the name "Ma Yijiao," although this feature is not very obvious in this work. Ma Yuan also had his own habit of painting trees. He often drew the branches of the trees diagonally downward, so some people summarized it into four words: "dragging branches and Ma Yuan".　　On the top of Ma Yuan's painting "Stepping on a Song", there is a five-line poem, which was copied from a poem by Wang Anshi of the Northern Song Dynasty by Emperor Ningzong of the Southern Song Dynasty. The poem reads, "The rain is clear, the sun is shining, the city is beautiful, the people are happy in the year of plenty, and the song is on the monastery." This is the Southern Song emperor's wish for a peaceful and prosperous world, and the painter Ma Yuan, who served the court, painted with this poem as the title.

描述_ZN: The Fisherman's Father" scroll, Yuan, by Wu Zhen, on silk, ink and brush, 84.7 cm long, 29.7 cm wide.　　In ancient China, fishing, woodcutting, farming, and reading were often considered idealized lifestyles by literati and scholars, and were often used as themes for literary works to express the author's desire to escape from the world, with the material of "fishing and seclusion" being the most common. During the Yuan Dynasty, Han literati had no way to enter society and their social status plummeted, and this was especially true for the Jiangnan scholars. As a result, "fishermen and hermits" appeared more frequently in paintings, among which Wu Zhen's "Fishermen and Fathers" is the most typical. Wu Zhen was good at landscape painting with the theme of "fishermen and hermits", and there are several copies of "Fisherman's Father", of which this is one of the more representative ones. The picture depicts the scenery of the south of the Yangtze River, with trees on a flat hill and a fisherman's father driving a boat to escape between the bend of the lake and the color of the water. The ink is pale and moist, and the rocks, trees, branches and leaves are all used in alternating shades of ink to show the hierarchical relationship and highlight the main objects. The varied brushwork, chafing and dabbing, all show the author's superb brush control. The secluded and quiet mood of the lake and mountains leaps off the paper, giving a sense of being far away from the mundane. Wu Zhen's "Fisherman's Father" is mostly matched by the powerful and dashing cursive script "Fisherman's Father Group", which complements poetry, calligraphy and painting. The poem, calligraphy, and painting complement each other well. For example, in this picture, it reads: "The frost and fading maple leaves are blurred. A thousand feet of waves, four gills of perch, and a gourd of wine in a poetry tube." 描述_ZN: The Five Mountains, Ming dynasty, painted by Song Xu, on silk, 24.9 cm long, 75.9 cm wide.　　Shiqu Baoji Sequel, recorded in the Qianqing Palace, the eight seals of the whole Five Mountains, is the general name of the five famous mountains in China, referring to Mount Tai in the east, Mount Hua in the west, Mount Songshan in the middle, Mount Heng in the north, and Mount Heng in the south. The Five Mountains originated from the ancient Chinese worship of mountains and rivers, and were associated with the worship of mountain gods by the king of the country. The painting depicts the natural beauty of the five mountains, such as the sunny view of the sun, the clear autumn of Taihua, the two colors of the rushing peaks, the snowy Hengsei, and the two rooms of the mountain, using the technique of contrast between the light and the strong, the real and the imaginary to make the picture clear. In the composition, the artist uses the traditional flat and distant composition method, with the scenery near large and far small, near real and far virtual, with a strong sense of depth and distance. The brushwork is rough, elegant, and strong, with the sober and pale style of Shen Zhou's later paintings.　　The painting is recorded in the "Continued Compilation of Painting Treasures".

Wang Sash is famous for his paintings of bamboo and rocks in landscapes, and his paintings of bamboo are especially "pioneering" in the Ming Dynasty. This painting is an inheritance from the Yuan Dynasty, but with new ideas. The bamboo leaves are drawn with round and strong strokes, and the branches are drawn with a straight and wide brush, and the leaves are naturally skimmed out with the hand to reflect the front and side of the leaves and the back, as well as the look of the leaves. The dryness and intensity of the ink and the size and sparseness of the brushstrokes are used to express the sense of space and three-dimensionality of the bamboo clusters. The brushwork is skillful and simple, and the shapes are vivid and realistic, with a refreshing charm.　　According to legend, there is a story about Wang Sash's bamboo painting. When he was in Beijing, he heard the beautiful sound of the xiao at night, so he painted a piece of bamboo on his own initiative and visited the xiao player the next day to present it to him in person. He was a big businessman and was so happy to see this that he immediately sent Wang Sash a generous gift and asked him to paint another one. Wang Sash laughed and said, "I visit for the sound of the xiao, you to xiao material, you vulgar son also." So he tore up the previous painting and returned the gift. This kind of arrogant and solitary character is naturally revealed in Wang Sash's ink and bamboo paintings, which have become a reflection of his personality.　　This painting is inscribed with the following inscription: "Written by Wang Fang on the 9th day of the xinsi year of the year of the Chinese calendar and sent to the Zen master outside of the dust." 描述_ZN: Scroll of "The Mountains and the Rain", Ming, by Zhang Lu, on silk, color, 147 cm long and 105 cm wide.　　The title of the painting, "Mountains and Rain Desire to Come," was added by later generations according to the content of the picture, but it is aptly used for this painting. The painting depicts a deep ravine, a spring, a stream, a misty cloud, and a swaying tree branch, a scene of impending rain and sudden changes in the storm. The whole painting is splashed with large brush strokes, dense with moisture, unrestrained with brushes, and full of ink and wash. The mountain peaks are formed with large horizontal dots, and the outer contours show irregular dog-tooth-like curves. The bold brushwork appropriately depicts the natural scenery of the stormy weather in a particular environment. The distant mountains are lightly painted with light ink, giving the impression that there are mountains beyond the mountains. At the foot of the mountain, the artist leaves a large blank space without a single brush stroke, and the dazzling clouds open up the spatial distance. The author uses the brush to paint the leaves in a messy way, making the branches and leaves swaying in the wind and rain vivid and charming. The whole picture, except for the figures, almost omits lines and is distinguished by the rendering of large blocks of ink.

描述_ZN: Scroll of Hibiscus Goose, Ming, Sun Long, on silk, color, 159.3 cm long and 84.1 cm wide.　　The painting is unmarked. Inscriptions: "孫隆圖書", "金川侍御" and "開國忠拇侯孫".　　The picture depicts a large goose looking forward with its head held high, standing sideways under the hibiscus and lake rocks by the grass side of a pond. The hibiscus flowers and leaves are painted with the method of dotting and then outlining, with ink and color interspersed. The Taihu Lake stone is rendered with the boneless method. The goose is both unboned and outlined, with light ink lines outlining the outline and feathers, light ink rendering the flowers, and vermilion brown ochre filling in the muzzle and palm, with a rigid shape and fine brushwork. The whole painting does not stick to the details, but starts from the whole and focuses on the vivid demeanor of the white goose and hibiscus.　　In terms of painting method, the author integrates the painting with the form, the boneless and the outline, the ink and the light color, and harmoniously unifies them in the painting. The origin of this painting method should be the development and variation of the ink and wash painting technique of flowers and birds since Song and Yuan, and it is a creation of Sun Long, which opens up a new style of painting flowers and birds. This painting is his best surviving work.

Inscription: "Zizhong" in vermilion.　　The picture depicts a young man bowing to an old man, while the old man raises his hand and points in reply, hence the title of this painting. Cui Zizhong's figure painting is innovative based on the traditional brushwork of Gu Kaizhi, Lu Tanwei, Yan Liben and Wu Daozi. He paid attention to the portrayal of characters' expressions, and in his "Washing Elephant", "Hidden Cloud" and "Fishing Family" in the collection of the National Palace Museum, he was able to accurately paint the characteristics of characters with different identities. In this painting, his humble expression when the young man asks questions and the confident and calm demeanor of the old man are both vividly conveyed. The rounded and delicate brushwork of the clothing pattern, the trembling lines, and the gnarled folds highlight the soft texture of the clothing material and its movement with the wind. The branches and leaves of the trees are filled in with double lines, and the brushwork is meticulous and decorative.

The case has Huangting Zun has wine, and the place with less storm is home. Xuanzai complements the picture." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions of "Song Eun's review", "Gala in Xin's", "Yi Jin Zhai seal" and "Huang XI Zi".　　The composition of the painting takes the potential of the corners, with hills and ravines, jungles, huts and villages, winding mountain paths and open water. A flat boat slowly coming, relaxed and comfortable. The brushwork and ink are light, and the chalking and dyeing are exquisite.　　In the second panel, the title of the painting reads: "The water of Nanling is long and lingering, the wind is tight and the clouds are busy, and it wants to change into autumn. The wind is tight and the clouds are full of autumn. It is a lonely place for a guest's heart, who has red sleeves leaning on a high building. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions of "Song Eun's review" and "Jiang Shang Wai Shi".　　The wide water surface divides the picture into distant and near scenes, with rocks and trees on the near side and reeds moving with the wind, while the man in the building looks at the mountains across the river from afar, seeing only green hills and green islands, and clouds and smoke flowing. The whole picture is about the brushwork, mostly painted with a medium sharpness, the mountains and rocks are chapped in a complicated but not chaotic way, and the rules are self-existing. The coloring is pure and elegant, not too rich and beautiful, which better expresses the literati's interest.　　The third opening, this panel is inscribed: "Imitating half of Beiyuan's mountain and stream travel. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Dong Qichang". Inscriptions of "Jiang Shang Wai Shi" and "Song Eminent Review".　　The picture represents the scene of the towering boulders in the mountains and ten thousand trees competing for beauty, and the thick texture of the mountains and rocks is painted with different shades of ink, and the strokes are connected with each other, using both dryness and wetness, with the flavor of Dong Yuan in the Fifth Dynasty.　　　　　　The fourth panel is inscribed: "The air clears the surface of the earth and the clouds converge at the end of the sky. The waves of the cave are beginning, and the leaves of the wood are slightly removed. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions of "Gala Chongguang Seal", "Jiang Shang Wai Shi" and "Song Eminent Review".　　A few trees are on the near bank, while the flat slope and gentle hills in the distance are hidden by green hills. The mountains are dotted with horizontal strokes of moss, resembling the charm of Xiaomi (Mi Youren). The picture presents a quiet and elegant atmosphere, and the composition is sparse, with the brushwork of Ni Zan.　　In the fifth panel, the painting is inscribed, "Imitating the brushwork of Beiyuan. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Seal of Dong Qichang". Inscriptions: "Reviewed by Song eminent" and "Jiang Shangguang".　　In the picture, the path is winding, trees are scattered, and several huts are vaguely revealed among the rocks. The rocks are mostly chiseled with long strokes, and the branches of the trees are sketched with strokes, and the leaves are dyed with ink dots. The brushwork does not seek to work in detail, but to seek the innocent interest.　　The sixth panel is inscribed: "The sea breeze keeps blowing, and the moon shines on the river (this word is removed by dots). Xuanzai." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions: "Jiang Shang Wai Shi" and "Song Eminent Review".　　The painting is a partial interception of a landscape, with beautiful green peaks and waterfalls hanging upside down, which makes people feel relaxed and happy.　　In the seventh panel, this panel is inscribed: "Imitating the brushwork of Huang Zijiu's giant scroll landscape in the collection of Bachelor Hua of Liangxi. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Seal of Dong Qichang". Inscriptions: "Reviewed by Song eminent" and "Jiang Shangguang".　　The forms are drawn with light ink lines, and the mountains and rivers are written with fine and moist lines, while the recumbent brush with moss dots and the pistachio chap are used by Huang Gongwang in the Yuan Dynasty. The pine trees are both thick and light, with a distinction between near and far. This huge brushwork is not constrained in the small painting format, Dong's random brushwork has a natural interest.　　For the study of painting, Dong Qichang believed that one should first take the ancients as teachers, copy their paintings carefully, and integrate their brushwork techniques and layouts and compositions in one's mind, so as to gain the interest of the ancients' brushwork and ink, and from this seven-page album, one can appreciate Dong's brushwork and ink skills. The female prostitutes accompanying them are either mechanically accompanying the music on the board, or sitting with their sleeves distractedly, forming a sharp contrast with the concentrated expressions of the patrons. According to Tang Yin's ink mark on the painting, "Li Nunu's song and dance is inscribed by Tang Yin of Wu Men, late in March of Hongzhi Kuihai, when Li Nunu was ten years old," it is clear that the dancer in the circle is Li Nunu, who was ten years old but had been a prostitute for several years. The Ming Dynasty was a period of prosperity for the brothel industry. In view of the prosperity of the culture of green houses, many talented and disillusioned painters, such as Wu Wei and Tang Yin, drank and drank with prostitutes, trying to get rid of the depression of disillusionment and the burden of ethics through traveling with prostitutes, and gaining psychological balance and spiritual relaxation. Tang Yin engraved the seal of "the first genius in Jiangnan" and created this picture by Wu Wei to show his cynical outlook on life with the glory of visiting prostitutes.　　This painting was made when Wu Wei was 45 years old. 描述_ZN: The Book of Stories of People, Ming, Qiu Ying, silk, color, 41.4 cm in length and 33.8 cm in width per opening.　　The book has ten openings, the contents of which are drawn from historical stories, fables and legends, anecdotes of literati and poetic allegories, specifically, Zilu asks for the Jin, Ming Concubine Goes to the Cypress, Guifei Diao Makeup, South China Autumn Water, Blowing a Cock and Attracting a Phoenix, High Mountains and Flowing Water, Bamboo Courtyard Pin Gu, Pine Forest Six Escapees, Xunyang Pipa, Catching Willow Flowers, and so on. These subjects were often depicted by painters in history, but Qiu Ying injected his own talent and skills in the conception, image shaping and ink expression of his works, showing a distinctive individual style.　　The works are clearly themed and cleverly conceived, with not only specific and clear details of the characters' activities, but also attention to the setting and atmosphere, making each page highly ornamental. For example, the page of "Your Concubine's Makeup" is centered on Yang Guifei's early morning bun in the mirror at the Duanzheng Building of the Huaqing Palace, with the courtesans playing music, picking flowers and carrying a pipa in one scene, concentrating on her love of peonies, her love of hairpin flowers, her good music and her good dressing, and also reflecting her luxurious and happy life in general. Another example is the page of "High Mountain and Flowing Water", which is based on the story of Boya drumming his zither. While depicting the specific plot of Yu Boya playing his zither in a pavilion and Zhong Ziqi picking up the steps to meet his soulmate, the quiet and secluded environment of a high mountain waterfall and a pine forest with flowing water is set up to express the musical content of high mountain and flowing water imaginatively and to set off the elegant sentiments of the characters. It creates a perfect situation of intermingling scenes.　　This album uses the heavy-color brush method. The characters are delicately depicted, the literati are elegant and graceful, and the ladies are dignified and beautiful. The architectural vessels are neat and fine, and the mountains, rocks, and trees have their own forms. The brushwork is meticulous but not stagnant, smooth and natural, rigid and soft. The colors are brilliant and harmonious, and the overall tone is harmonious and elegant. The work has the artistic effect of elegance and vulgarity, and is Qiu Ying's innovation and development of the painting method of painting with heavy brush in the Tang and Song dynasties.

描述_ZN: Fan Page with Flowers and Insects, Qing dynasty, painted by Yu Shen, on paper with color, 19.3 cm in length and 56 cm in width.　　The fan page is inscribed with the following inscription: "I touched on the interest in the dense foliage, and dotted the grass and insects from the dense leaves. Inscriptions of "Yu" and "Save" in vermilion, and "Yixing" in vermilion at the head.　　This work is a sketch of a small-scale painting in color, depicting dragonflies, grasshoppers, praying mantis, ladybugs and other insects enjoying themselves among flowers and plants. Yu is a painter who pays attention to life drawing and believes that the most vivid and touching paintings are the ones that touch the scenery, and that only by taking heaven and earth as his teacher can he create a masterpiece. For this reason, he engraved the chapters of "The Heart of Heaven" and "Spring Rain" to express his intention of "touching the heart of life at the right place". This painting is not a work of imperial command, but a gift from the author to a friend, so it was created entirely according to Yu's own wishes, making it the most authentic painting of Yu's artistic style. The artistic language of the whole painting is simple, from composition to brushwork and ink, without embellishment. The picture is colored with rich colors, forming a bright, clean and elegant tone against each other, and overflowing with the freshness of nature.

描述_ZN: Wisteria and Goldfish" scroll, painted by Xugu in the Qing dynasty, on paper with color, 125 cm in length and 66 cm in width.　　The picture depicts several goldfish swimming comfortably at the time when wisteria flowers are in full bloom. All of Xugu's paintings of wisteria and goldfish are titled "Golden Medallion with Purple Ribbon". The so-called "golden seal with purple ribbon" comes from the phrase "the ministerial state and the prime minister, both Qin officials, had golden seals and purple ribbons" in the Book of Han. These paintings are popular with the public for their auspicious symbolism of officialdom and prestige. The flowers and leaves of the wisteria in this painting are directly colored, and their fullness of moisture reveals their vivid vitality. The vines are expressed with intermittent and staccato sideways strokes, the strokes are broken but the air is continuous, forming an elegant rhythm of brushwork and ink. The form of the goldfish is simple and exaggerated, and although it is hastily made with red color, it is still moving and interesting. This painting shows the author's unique artistic charm with its clear and cool style.　　Signed: "Purple ribbon and gold seal. Written in honor of Lord Dianfu Fangbo. Xigu." The difference is that the main characters in Yinzhen plowing and weaving diagram such as farmers, sericulture women, etc. are the portraits of Yinzhen and his Fujin, which is only seen in the plowing and weaving diagram in successive generations. The picture survives 52 pages, of which 6 pages are undrafted derivative pages, and the remaining 46 pages are 23 pages each of plowing and weaving, each with a poem inscribed in Yinzhen's own handwriting and inscribed with two seals, "Prince Yong Bao" and "Broken Dust Jushi". Inscriptions: "Seal of Hu Huien" and "Seal of Meng Lun".　　This picture was created at the age of 52 in the 32nd year of the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing Dynasty (1693), following the brushwork of the master of Yuan Dynasty painting Huang Gongwang's masterpiece "Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains", which shows the painter's profound skills and high attainments in the management position, the opening and closing of the mountains and the use of ink and brush. In this imitation, he is comfortable with the use of chaffing, pointing and dyeing, and his technique is superb, especially in the use of ink and brush, the first brush and then ink, staining several times, from light to thick, gradually increasing, and finally to burnt ink to break awake, giving people a sense of heaviness. Mountains and scenery are thicker, more rigorous and more detailed than those painted by Huang Gongwang. Wang Yuanqi's painting style is very distinctive among the Four Kings, and he developed Dong Qichang's pursuit of abstract ink and brush forms with programmatic features. The purpose of his paintings was to entertain the senses, with a preference for the ideal, which is significantly different from Western painting's preference for realistic scenes.

描述_ZN: The booklet "Visiting the Stele at Dai Lu", Qing Dynasty, painted by Huang Yi, on paper, color, 17.4 cm per opening, 50.8 cm across.　　The name of the picture "Dai" refers to Mount Tai, located in the central part of Shandong Province. The book "visiting the monuments in Dai Lu" has 24 openings, depicting Huang Yi in the second year of the Qing Dynasty (1797) from Jining to visit the monuments in Mount Tai in the form of left text and right picture. According to the author's own inscription, some of the pages record the inscriptions on Mount Tai, such as "Daeding", "Kaiyuan Mill Cliff Tablet", "Shijing Valley", "Wangmu Pond", etc, "The other part records the inscriptions the author saw on his way to and from the site, such as "Daming Lake", "Mencius Temple", "Confucius Forest ", "Confucius Temple", "Dawenkou" and so on. In addition, the author also introduces the specific condition of the inscriptions in his inscriptions, providing information for future generations to study.　　Huang Yi devoted his life to the study of jinshi steles and tablets, and has searched around for the surviving broken steles and organized and recorded them in a more systematic way, which has played an active role in the development of traditional jinshiology in China. Unusually, he personally used a brush to record the process of each visit to ancient monuments in full, and drew many works, which were widely praised by artists of the time. One of these works is the booklet "Visiting Monuments in Dailu".　　Throughout the whole set, the author uses two Chinese painting techniques, ink and light violet, but presents a unified artistic style. Specifically, he pays attention to the interruptions and transitions of the lines, and mostly uses thick strokes and short lines to depict the scenery around the location of the inscriptions, making the scene simple and clear, with a secluded and quiet mood, and a bland and naive artistic interest.

描述_ZN: The scroll of "Statue of Ba Weizu", Qing Dynasty, by Min Zhen, on paper with color, 103.5 cm in length and 31.6 cm in width.　　This painting is inscribed by Yuan Huanshu with the title "Statue of Jundang Jushi," with inscriptions by Jinbeng, Dasheng, and Sisheng, and by Wu Yunsteam, with inscriptions by Han Tingxiu, Cheng Zhenjia, and seven others on the sides of the frame.　　On the picture, Ba Weizu is about 50 years old, wearing a green cedar and a red robe, sitting on a futon with yellow flowers on a blue background, with a peaceful posture, a thin face, hale and hearty eyes, but seemingly with a tired look, reminiscent of Gu Kaizhi's Vimalakirti "lightly frail, showing the appearance of sickness, hidden a few forgetfulness of speech", so it is clear that this picture was made when Ba was sick. The artist uses a realistic painting method, which is fine and realistic, and the faces of the figures are drawn from the "Bosun School", with fine brushwork, light coloring, and darker shading, so that the sense of concavity and convexity is evident. The artist's use of color expresses the character's individuality, with the cheekbones, cheeks, and eye sockets clearly described, and the clothing pattern is finely drawn with strong strokes, with a slight staccato in the turn, and with elaborate coloring, the picture is simple and elegant, focusing on a sense of unity of form and content as a whole, and the portrait under his brush is well represented in both form and spirit.

描述_ZN: Snow in the Sky Mountains, Qing Dynasty, by Hua Yan, on paper, color on canvas, 159.1 cm long and 52.8 cm wide.　　Hua Yan's figure paintings are characterized by their distinctive forms, which are distinguished by their distinctive personalities and intrinsic charm. The Snowy Mountains in the Sky is a representative work from his later years.　　Traveling to the frontier was one of Hua Yan's frequent subjects. The present painting depicts a poetic vision of the Tang people traveling to the frontier. In this painting, a single traveler, clad in a large red cloak and hiding a sword, walks slowly through the snow and ice with an old bactrian camel at the foot of the Tianshan Mountains. The sky is gray, the field is empty, the road is long and snow-capped. A lone goose skims the air, and the traveler and the old camel look up at the scene, which seems to have aroused a thousand thoughts of the wanderer. The painting is a blend of scenes and ambiguities. The composition of the painting is long and narrow, creating a visual effect of the sky and the sky, in order to set off the lonely inner world of the characters. The color scheme is elegant, and the matching of colors and the contrast of warm and cold tones are very elaborate. The figures and the old camel are realistically portrayed with exaggerated techniques, and the forward motion of the figures and the humane expression of the old camel make the theme more prominent. The work shows the artist's unique artistic conception and outstanding painting talent.　　The painting is self-referential: "Snow in the Tianshan Mountains. In the spring of Yihai, Xinluo Shanren wrote this in the Studio of the Sound of Talking, at the age of seventy or four." Inscription: "Huayan" at the bottom and "Empty Dust Poetry and Painting" at the lower right corner.

描述_ZN: Portrait of Dong Bangda, Yongzheng, Qing dynasty, painted by Tang Qianli, color on silk, 93.8 cm long, 68.4 cm wide.　　There is no biography of Tang Qianli in the history of painting. According to this figure and its self-title, it is known that his character Cheng Yuan was a native of Biling (present-day Changzhou, Jiangsu Province). He was active in the Kangxi and Yongzheng years of the Qing Dynasty. He was good at painting figures and landscapes.　　This painting is self-recognized as "written in the rain window in June of the summer of Yongzheng renchen. Tang Qianli of Biling". Inscriptions of "Tang", "Qianli" and "Cheng Yuan". There are poem inscriptions by Dong Bangda and Fu Zeng on the panel. The poem hall is inscribed with poems by four people, including Lu Qingyuan, Liang Dong, Ma Zeng and Zhou Peas.　　The picture depicts Dong Bangda sitting by a window in a cold house, holding a scroll. In terms of painting technique, the brushwork is delicate, and the characters' five senses are vividly portrayed and their demeanor is subtle. The background of trees, rocks, huts and streams is cold and secluded, and the depiction is real and natural, showing Dong Bangda's sentiment of studying hard in poverty. The painting was made in 1732, when Dong was 34 years old and had not yet been admitted to the imperial examinations.

描述_ZN: Axis of "Wu Rui Tu", Yongzheng, Qing dynasty, painted by Lang Shining, on silk with color, 140 cm long and 84 cm wide.　　This is a near-European still-life painting, with a celadon vase containing cattail leaves, pomegranate flowers, and marshmallow blossoms, a tray containing plums and cherries, and a few dumplings scattered about. The zongzi and the cattail in the picture suggest that the painting was painted for the Dragon Boat Festival, a traditional Chinese holiday. In terms of composition, the objects in the painting are clustered and scattered in a square triangular layout, giving a sense of stability to the human eye. The painting method uses shades of color and shadows to show the three-dimensionality of the flowers, fruits and vase, especially the "highlighting" technique on the shoulder of the vase, which is found in European paintings but not in Chinese paintings, so that the viewer can clearly appreciate the skills of Western oil painting. Although the picture is not dated, according to the archives of the Office of the Interior of the Qing Dynasty, it was painted in 1732, one of Lang Shining's early works in China.　　As an exotic visitor to China, the many missionaries who arrived in China in the late Ming and early Qing dynasties adopted the missionary strategy of blending Eastern and Western cultures and then implementing the doctrine in a gradual and progressive manner, and Lang Shining was undoubtedly a thorough practitioner. Although his technique of representing still life in this painting is derived from European oil paintings, its content reflects the customs of the Chinese people, which have been embodied in the essence of their culture for more than two thousand years. It was his eclectic technique of combining Chinese and foreign knowledge and his choice of subject matter to suit the interests of the Chinese emperors that made Lang Shining a Western painter who was highly appreciated and greatly used by the Yongzheng and Qianlong emperors, and to which he owes the survival of a large number of his paintings.　　Signed: "Painted by Lang Shining", with two seals, the inscriptions indistinct. 描述_ZN: Ruan Guangxian Entering the Hajj and Giving a Banquet, in the album Pingding the War in Annam, Qianlong, Qing dynasty, painted by an unknown artist, on paper, color, 55.6 cm long and 91.2 cm wide.　　The upper part of the painting is inscribed by the Qianlong emperor with the poem "Ruan Hui sent his nephew Ruan Guangxian to the court to give a banquet", and the inscription reads, "The imperial brush in mid-autumn of the Qianlong period." Inscriptions include "Guxi Tianzi's treasure", "Sanxitang Jingjian Seal", and "Yizi Sun". The year "Jiyou" is the 54th year of the Qianlong era (1789), when the Qianlong emperor was 79 years old.　　In the second half of the 18th century, war broke out in Annam (present-day Vietnam) due to regime change. The brothers Nguyen Van Ngoc and Nguyen Huy (later renamed Nguyen Quang Binh) of Qui Nhon Province led an army to overthrow the Le Dynasty and King Le Vicky left. In 1788, the mother and wife of the king of Annam asked the Qing court for help. In view of the fact that since 1666, when the Qing court crowned King Le Vicky as the king of Annam, the Le dynasty had paid tribute to the Qing court and was very obedient to the Qing court, the Qianlong Emperor decided to send troops to help Le and restore the rule of the Le dynasty in Annam. The Qianlong Emperor ordered Sun Shiyi, the governor of the two provinces, to lead the conquest and soon captured Xuanguang and Xinghua in Annam, and embraced Le Vicky to reassume the throne. However, the following year, when the Qing soldiers were celebrating the New Year festival, they were attacked by Ruan Hui's army, and the Qing soldiers responded hastily and lost their troops, and the city was regained. Although Nguyen Hue defeated the Qing army and destroyed the Le Dynasty, he knew that in order to stabilize the order and strengthen his rule, he had to be recognized and enthroned by the Qing Dynasty in order to gain legal status. In order to change the policy of the Qing court to "support Le and destroy Ruan", Ruan Hui kept seeking to improve the relationship with the Qing dynasty. Faced with Ruan Hui's persistent actions and the political situation in Annam, the Qianlong Emperor decided to change his policy towards Annam from Fuli to Ruan and crowned Ruan Hui as King of Annam.　　Qianlong emperor in order to commemorate the Qing army to Annan won several battles, while praising in the battle of Pingan South, Guangxi Governor Xu Shiheng, general Shang Wei Ping, Zhang Chaolong and other generals serve the court's heroic behavior, ordered the drawing of a "pacification of Annan war map" book (a total of 6). In addition to the battle maps showing the battles of the Shouchang River, the three different pillars of the right, the Shiqiu River, and the Fuliang River, there is also a picture depicting the arrival of Ruan Hui's nephew, Ruan Guangxian, at the summer resort in July 1789, where the Qianlong Emperor received Ruan Guangxian and his party at the grand opera house of the Qing Yin Pavilion, and ordered him to accompany the Mongolian princes and ministers of civil and military affairs to enjoy the opera. In the picture, the Qianlong Emperor is in full spirit, sitting on his knees, and in front of him are Ruan Guangxian and other ambassadors kneeling in a row wearing red robes. The composition of this painting is both realistic and vivid, depicting the strict hierarchical differences between the Emperor and his ministers, as well as the monarchical position of imperial power that the Emperor holds in the painting.

A total of nine works by Ai were included in the Shiqu Baoji, a collection book compiled by the Qing court. The painting level of Ai Qimeng was average compared to that of the Italian Lang Shining and the Frenchman Wang Zhicheng, but after the death of Lang Shining and Wang Zhicheng, Ai Qimeng became a European painter relied upon by the Qianlong Emperor.　　The painting is of a large horse of similar size to the real one, named "Baoji bay". "At this time, the original chief European painter at the court, Lang Shining, died in 1766, and another European painter, Wang Zhicheng, passed away in 1768, so Ai Qimeng naturally became the most important painter. Therefore, Ai Qimeng naturally became the main painter who specialized in European painting style, so some of the tasks of depicting tribute objects were taken up by Ai Qimeng, such as this large banner of "Baoji bay".　　"Baoji bay" is the name of the horse in the painting. In June of 1771, the Mongolian Turks, who were nomadic in the lower Volga River in Russia, returned to their ancestral homeland in the East after nearly a year of bullying and oppression by the local Russians, led by their tribal leaders, the Wobashi and the Cebek Dolji (Wobashi's son-in-law). For this reason, Emperor Qianlong was very happy and received the chief of the tribe to appease and reward them. The horse named "Baoji bay" was a tribute presented to the Qianlong Emperor by Zebek Dorji at this time. This "Baoji bay" was painted by order of the Qianlong Emperor.　　If we talk about the painting skills alone, Ai Qimeng's painting is not much outstanding, and its painting level is much lower than that of Lang Shining, who is also a court painter. But after all, as a court painter, Ai Qimeng has played a documentary role with his brush, leaving us with a piece of history that once took place, and its value cannot be judged solely on the basis of the skill of his painting.

Back then, Lin Qing of the Tianli Sect led an insurgent army to invade the Forbidden City when the Jiaqing Emperor was not in the palace (at the summer residence). When the palace was in a state of panic, Minning, who was 16 years old at the time, took the lead, raised his gun and shot at the rebels, and organized an effective resistance. He always kept the uprising army on the Qianqingmen Square outside the Qianqing Gate until the elite soldiers of the Eight Banners Jianrui Battalion arrived at the Forbidden City to relieve the siege. Minning's outstanding performance won him important leverage for his succession to the throne.　　The Daoguang emperor was at a critical moment in the turning point of history, but he "kept his usual but did not know his changes". During his 30-year reign, he abided by the ancestral system, was diligent in government, and was frugal. But the opium flowing from the southeast sea made him restless, and he finally resolved to strictly prohibit smoking. At the beginning of the 19th year of Daoguang (1839), the Daoguang Emperor appointed Lin Zexu as the Minister of the Imperial Household to combat smoking in Guangdong. The Tiger Gate Smoking Ban also caused tensions between China and Britain. In June 1840, the British expeditionary force reached the Chinese sea and the Opium War broke out. On August 29, 1842, the Qing government signed the Treaty of Nanjing, the first unequal treaty in modern Chinese history, with Britain, reducing China to a semi-colonial society. 　　This painting bears the seals of "Shen De Tang Bao", "Daoguang" and "Ri Jin Wu Jie".　　This picture was painted by a court painter and represents the court painting style of the late Qing Dynasty. It depicts the Emperor Daoguang and his princes and princesses having fun together in the Yuanmingyuan. In the painting, Emperor Daoguang is elegant, holding a snuff bottle, sitting in the pavilion of "Chengxin Zhengxue", looking kindly at his children playing. The fourth son of the emperor, Yi wisdom, who later became the Xianfeng emperor, and the sixth son of the emperor, Yi appeals, who later became the Prince Gong, were studying under the watchful eye of their father. The seventh son of the emperor, Yixuan, the eighth son of the emperor, and the ninth son of the emperor, Yixuan, are still young, and the seventh son of the emperor, Yixuan, is the grandfather of the later Xuantuan emperor, Puyi. The two princesses in the painting are Princess Shouan Gulun, the fourth daughter of the Daoguang Emperor, and Princess Shouen Gulun, the sixth daughter of the Daoguang Emperor.　　This picture has important historical value for studying the life of the late Qing Dynasty court.

描述_ZN: Scroll of "The Magpie in the Willow", modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 100 cm long and 61.5 cm wide.　　Self-titled: "In the spring of 1933, Beihong wrote this in congratulation of the completion of the new residence of Huaju Rendi at Lihang Middle School." Inscribed with a seal in vermilion underneath: "Sorrow". One seal of the collection is indistinct and illegible.　　Thirty-three years that refers to the Republic of 33 years (1944), Xu Beihong was 49 years old.　　In 1944, Xu Beihong suffered from hypertension and nephritis in Chongqing hospital for six months, the medical advice not to move the brush to do painting. As a result, the number of his creations dropped sharply that year. The present painting was painted by him at the beginning of the year at the invitation of a friend, and is very rare. Six magpies are perched on the branches of a willow tree, two of which are clinging to each other, whispering and attracting the other magpies to stop and watch.　　The picture is cleverly conceived, with the magpies either single or double, forming a "c" shape, with sparse or dense distances and high or low positions between them, making the picture rich in rhythmic changes and vividness. The painting is full of willow branches fluttering in the wind, which are outlined with a medium sharp brush, and the lines are thick and thin and elastic, showing the author's solid line drawing skills. 描述_ZN: A four-legged covered stove with green glaze from Changsha kilns, Song dynasty, 8.5 cm high, 8 cm in diameter, 8.3 cm from the foot.　　The lid is modelled after an ancient bronze vessel, with a converging mouth, straight belly and folded bottom, bearing four feet. The body is glazed with green glaze, glaze is less than the bottom, glaze green in yellow, elegant and soft, glaze surface has a small open pattern.　　This kind of furnace is also known as incense smoke, for incense use. Stove cover more for carved decoration, will be burned spices placed in the furnace, curling smoke from the hollow floating out, such as clouds and fog. Porcelain incense burner was first seen in the Eastern Wu, more popular in the Six Dynasties, more trays, stove body large, cover surface hollow, generous style. After the Tang Dynasty, the tray was changed to three-footed or five-footed, with small and dense hollowing.　　Changsha kiln, also known as Tongguan kiln, Wangcheng kiln and Wajiaping kiln, is known as Changsha kiln because it is under the jurisdiction of Changsha City. Founded in the Middle Tang Dynasty and flourished in the Late Tang and Five Dynasties, Changsha Kiln is a large folk porcelain kiln of great scale and skill. The decorative techniques of Changsha kiln porcelain include incised flowers, molded decals, sculptures and underglaze decorations, of which underglaze is the most famous. The coloring materials used are mainly green coloring with copper oxide as the coloring agent and brown coloring with iron oxide as the coloring agent. According to the painting technique, it can be divided into four kinds of underglaze brown color spot pattern, underglaze green color spot pattern, underglaze green color painting and underglaze brown green color painting.　　This vessel is neat and generous in shape, with heavy body and decorated with underglaze brown color on the lid surface, with different shades of glaze, which is highly decorative.

In the Tang Dynasty, there were six translations of the Vajra Sutra after it was introduced to China. When the Tang Emperor Wenzong Li Ang, Yang '0490', a native of Hongnong, abridged and compiled this sutra, called the "New Set of Vajra Sutra", which is known as the "Seven Translations". Yang wrote the preface and invited eight ministers, including Zheng Qin and Liu Gongquan, to inscribe the sutra praise, and put it on the stone with an eight-point book, which was installed in the Xingtang Temple in Shangdu (Chang'an). In July of the fourth year of Taihe (830), Yang Chenghe, Minister of Internal Affairs and Minister of Hongnong County, presented this "sutra" to the emperor with a certificate. In August, Emperor Wen compiled it into the "Collection of scriptures catalog", and thought that "the initial carving of the body of eight points, the reader many errors", ordered the set of Jin right general Wang Xizhi book republication, to Taihe six years (832 years) spring work completed. Li Shimin, Emperor Taizong of Tang, loved Wang Xizhi's calligraphy, so Wang became the most popular calligraphy style of the Tang generation. In the third year of Xianheng (672), Hongren, a Buddhist monk at Hongfu Temple in Chang'an, first adopted the method of "collecting characters" and carved the monument "Collecting Wang Xizhi's line script", which played a significant role in the popularization of Wang's calligraphy. It is 22.3 cm in length and 12.8 cm in width.　　This stele was erected in the eighth year of Yanxi (165), in clerical script, elegant and magnificent. It is "the most powerful of the Han eighths, the first of the Wei steles" (Wang Xisun, Qing Dynasty). The name of the calligrapher is seldom left on Han inscriptions, but this inscription has the name of "Shuzo Xinfeng Guo Xiangcha Shu" at the end. The inscription describes the rituals of the emperors of successive dynasties and the restoration of the Huayue Temple by Yuan Feng, the governor of Hongnong in the current dynasty.　　The original stele Song Ouyang Xiu "collection of ancient records", Zhao Mingcheng "Jinshilu" recorded. According to Yuan Luo Tianchao's "Class Compilation Chang'an Zhi" and Ming Guo Zongchang's "Jin Shi Shi Shi", it is presumed that the monument was destroyed in the late Song and early Yuan dynasties. There are four trustworthy copies: one is the Chang Yuan version, named after the Ming Dynasty Chang Yuan Wang Wensun collection. The second is the Huayin book, which was collected by the Huayin East Shiu Shang brothers and Guo Zongchang in the Ming Dynasty, also known as the Guanzhong book. Third is the four Ming Ben, Ming Dynasty Ningbo Fengxi Wan scroll building and Fan Qin Tianyi Pavilion collection, Ningbo is known as the four Ming. Four is the Shunde book, because of the Qing season Shunde Li Wentian was stored and named.　　The Huayin version is finely topologized with thick ink. The first to seventeenth lines of the original stele have more than one hundred characters of dancing, which is later than the Chang Yuan and Shun De Ben, about between Song and Yuan. More than 230 inscriptions and comments by Guo Zongchang, Wang Duo, Weng Fanggang, Ruan Yuan, etc. are present on the accompanying pages. Among them, Wang Hong wrote a postscript: "advocate the Han clerical when and Changli text from the same work of the same eight generations"; Zhu Yun postscript from the theory of six books to examine the structure of the inscriptions, to prove the progression of seal, official, regular; Zhu Xigeng postscript detailing the flow of the Huashan stele all toppings passed to the collection, all have high academic value.　　It is also recorded in the books such as Song Hong Shih's "Official Interpretation" and Qing Ruan Yuan's "Han Yanxi Xiyue Huashan Temple Tablet Examination".

描述_ZN: The Tablet of Divine Prophecy of Heaven, erected in 276, the first year of the reign of Wu Tianxi. In 264 A.D., Sun Hao succeeded to the throne of the Three Kingdoms of Wu, and the political situation became more and more dangerous due to his faintness and brutality. 276 A.D., the first year of the reign was changed to Tianxi, and this stone was carved in order to stabilize the people and create the public opinion that the prophecy of God was sent down from the sky, thinking that it was auspicious for Wu. It is said to be the book of the Emperor's elephant, but there is no solid evidence.　　The upper section of the stele is 21 lines long, with 5 characters, 1 line of 6 characters for "imperial decree" and 1 line of 7 characters for "Great Wu"; the middle section is 17 lines long, with 7 characters; the lower section is 10 lines long, with 3, 2 or 1 characters. The original stele was carved at Tianxi Temple in Jiangning (present-day Nanjing). In the sixth year of the Song Dynasty (1091), Hu Zong Shi moved the stele to the rear garden of the transfer department and then to the Jiangning Academy of Scripture, and in the tenth year of the Jiaqing Dynasty (1805), the school official Mao Zao printed the "Jade Sea" in March and the stone was destroyed by fire. The upper part of the original stone has the trek of Hu Zong Shi in the sixth year of Yuan You, the trek engraved by Shi Yu in the first year of Chongning (1102), the trek engraved by Geng Ding in the forty-third year of Jia Jing (1564), and the trek engraved by Weng Fang Gang in the lower part of the stone in the Qing Dynasty, "Beiping Weng Fang Gang Lai Guan".　　The calligraphy of the "Divine Prophecy Tablet of Heaven" was described by Kang Youwei as "amazing and magnificent". The calligrapher wrote the seal script with a clerical style, which is extremely square and heavy at the beginning, square at the turn and round at the inside, and pendulous at the bottom. Huang Boshi of the Song Dynasty said, "In Wu Dynasty, there was the Tian Fa Shen Prophecy Tablet, which was majestic in character if it was in seal script."　　This is the oldest known copy in the collection of the National Palace Museum of the Northern Song Dynasty. The character "Wu" of "Wu County" is slightly damaged at the mouth, while the character "County" is intact, but there are many other slightly damaged strokes. There are more than 200 seals of the Song Dynasty such as "Beihai Kaiguo Lu Xuan's seal" and "Yongbao Wannian".　　The Qing Wang Chang "Jin Shi Zui Jian", Wang Zhuang Hong "additions to the school of monuments," Zhang Yansheng "good book of monuments and posters" and other books recorded.

描述_ZN: Fan Style Monument", also known as "Fan Juqing Monument". It was erected in the first month of the third year of the Qinglong period (235) of the Three Kingdoms. The full text of the stele is recorded in Song Hong Shi's "The Interpretation of the Official Script", with 19 lines and 33 characters. The name of the stele is inscribed in four columns, 10 lines in the first and second columns, 11 lines in the third column, and 6 lines in the fourth column. The frontal seal script reads "The monument of Fan Fujun, the former governor of Lujiang" in 10 characters.　　The monument was originally located in Rencheng, Shandong Province, but was later moved to Jining Prefecture. After the Song Dynasty, the monument was broken and lost in the earth. In the forty-first year of Qianlong of Qing Dynasty (1776), Cui of Jiaozhou first got the remnants of the tablet in the water mouth of West Longmen Square of Jining State School, and Li Dongqi and Huang Yi carved the trek under the tablet. Qianlong fifty-two years (1787), Li Dongqi regained the original monument remnants in the state school palace under the halberd door, Huang Yi, Li Kezheng and carved trek in the monument yin. The stone is now stored in the Han monument group of Tieta Temple in Jining.　　The Fanshibi Monument is one of the famous monuments of the Three Kingdoms of Wei. The calligraphy of this stele retains many characteristics of the Eastern Han Dynasty official script. Li Dongqi wrote: "The stone is very ancient and I was surprised that it was a Han monument. When I wiped it, there were several names of people in clerical script. I dug and washed it, and it was the Fan Shih Stele."　　This is the Song topography of the stone in Huang Yi's collection before it was unearthed, and the inscription has more than 180 characters than the topography after it was unearthed. The paper and ink are antique and the characters are sufficient. Each page is 34 cm in length and 17 cm in width. The back panel is inscribed with Lu Wenshao and Weng Fanggang, and there are 34 Tibetan seals such as "Weng Fanggang" and "Qu Zhongsol".　　It is recorded in Zhao Mingcheng's "Jinshilu" in the Song Dynasty, Weng Fanggang's "Jinshilu of the Two Han Dynasties" in the Qing Dynasty, and Wang Chang's "Jinshilu Zuiji".

描述_ZN: Confucius Temple Monument", written and written by Yu Shinan in the Tang Dynasty, with the forehead written by Li Dan, the king of the Sangha. It was erected in the seventh year of Emperor Taizong's reign (633). The inscription is in regular script, with 35 lines and 64 characters. The height of the tablet is 400 cm and the width is 150 cm. The inscription records the establishment of Kong Delun, the 33rd grandson of Confucius, as the Marquis of Praise and the restoration of the Temple of Confucius in the 9th year of Wu De (626). According to legend, only a few dozen copies of this inscription were made and given to the ministers during the Zhenguan period, but the stone was destroyed by fire. In the third year of Wu Zhou Chang'an (703), Empress Wu ordered King Li Dan to re-carve and write the tablet, which was later destroyed by fire. There are two existing re-carvings: one is the early Song Dynasty Wang Yanchao re-carving, the monument in Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, commonly known as "Shaanxi Ben", "Shaanxi Ben" or "West Temple Hall"; one is said to be the Yuan Dynasty re-carving, the monument in Shandong It is said to have been re-carved during the Yuan and Yuan dynasties, and is located in Chengwu County, Shandong Province, commonly known as "Chengwu Ben" or "East Temple Hall". The former word is fatter, and the latter word is thinner.　　The topography is a white paper with a border cut and framed in white paper. A total of 17 and a half openings, each half opening 28.5 cm long, 16.3 cm across. At the end of the line, "The emperor's virtue and the Confucian breeze Yongxuan Jinshi" has not been danced. Inscribed with the signature of Jue'an, six paragraphs of postscript by Bao Shichen, Sun Xingyan, Song Baocun and Chen Qijun, and six paragraphs of observational markings by Yao Nai, Zhao Huaiyu, Wu Rongguang and Zhang Weiping, The Seal of the Temple Hall of Confucius" is inscribed with 31 seals, including "Kuan", "Ji Mu Fu", "Bao's Secret Play", "Shichen Xue Gu", and "Huaiyu Private Seal".　　The calligraphic style of the Confucius Temple Monument is handsome and rounded, with slightly longer and more beautiful characters, flat across and straight down, and with an expansive stroke. The calligraphy of this stele has been valued by calligraphers of the Jin Shi dynasty, who called it a masterpiece of the regular script of the Tang Dynasty, the ultimate rule of regular script. In the early Ming Dynasty, Zhang Shen commented on the stele: "The calligraphy and painting are unique to Zhong and Wang, and no one has been able to match them in thousands of years."　　It was recorded in the books of Song Ouyang Xiu's "The End of Jigu Lu" and Zhao Mingcheng's "Jin Shi Lu", and in the books of Qing Sun Chengze's "Geng Zi Pin Xia Ji" and Gu Yanwu's "Jin Shi Wen Ji".

描述_ZN: The "Qing Tuo Sui Shoushan Qiyan Daoist Temple Relic Tablet Book", carved in 604, with ink topography, 26 and a half pages cut and mounted. Each opening is 32 cm in length and 35 cm in width. Donated by Mr. Ma Heng.　　This stele is inscribed in seal script with the title "The Stele of the Relic Pagoda at Quyan Dojo, Shushan, Hedong County, Shanxi Province", erected in Yongji County, Shanxi Province. The inscription records that Emperor Wen of the Sui Dynasty ordered the whole country to build the pagoda by "distributing relics in eighty states", and was written by He Deren of Huiji. The regular script is very stable and rigorous, which is a pioneer of the Tang script. The material is covered with sand grains like fish roe, so it is commonly known as "Fish Roe Tablet". The top two dots of the word "monk" in "Gao Xing Ming Monk" still exist. On the back of the booklet, there is a postscript by Mr. Ma Heng on September 6, 1911, verifying that the stele was erected in December of the fourth year of Renshou of the Sui Dynasty (604), revising the error of "the second year of Renshou" in the Qing dynasty's Sun Xingyan's "Huanyu Visiting Monuments". The seal of the collection is inscribed as "Fanshuizhai Zangbi" and "Ma Hengshuping reads the stele".

描述_ZN: Song Mountain Three Queues", early Qing dynasty topography, combined with "Tai Muro Shique Inscription", "Shao Muro Shique Inscription" and "Kaimu Temple Shique Inscription". It is a white paper framed book, with thick ink topography, 7 and a half pages in total, decorated with brocade surface. Taimuro Que inscriptions" 2 openings, 14 lines per opening, 9 characters; "Shaomuro Que inscriptions" 3 and a half openings, 10 lines per opening, 6 characters; "Kaimu Temple Que inscriptions" 2 openings, 10 lines per opening, 4 characters. With Zhu Yi container inscription, collection of 2 seals.　　"Song Mountain Three Que" is the combined name of Tai Muro Stone Que, Shao Muro Stone Que and Kaimu Temple Stone Que, which are located in Song Mountain area of Henan Province and are the most ancient temple queues existing in China.　　Taimuro Stone Que is located in the Zhongyue Temple in Mt. The inscription was engraved in the fifth year of the first year of Emperor An of the Eastern Han Dynasty (118). The main text is written in 27 lines, with 9 characters in the third line and 10 characters in the third line. The front of the tablet is in seal script. Shaomuro Stone Que is located at the eastern foot of Shaomuro Mountain, west of Dengfeng County, Henan Province, and is a Shinto que in front of Shaomuro Shao Aunt Temple, carved in the second year of Emperor An's Yanguang (123) in the Eastern Han Dynasty. Its south side is engraved with an inscription in seal script, with 22 lines and 4 characters. The front of the tablet is in seal script. The stone queue of Kaimu Temple is also known as the stone queue of Qimu Temple, which was changed from "QI" to "KAI" to avoid the taboo of Emperor Jing of Han Dynasty Liu Qi. It is located in the north of Dengfeng County, Henan Province, under the Ban Ban Feng Peak, and is the temple of the gods of Qimu Temple, engraved in the second year of the Eastern Han Dynasty Emperor Yan Guang (123). Seal script 32 lines, no forehead. The inscriptions of "Song Mountain Three Queues" express the worship of the mountain gods.　　The font of "Tai Muro Shiqu" is wide and circumscribed, simple and elegant, with strong and majestic clerical style; the seal script of "Shaomuro Shiqu" is broad and simple, with a wang yang style; the calligraphy style of "Kaimu Temple Shiqu" is similar to that of "Shaomuro Shiqu", but the font is slightly smaller and the style is square and ancient. Shaomuro Stone Queue Inscription" and "Kaimu Temple Stone Queue Inscription" are among the top quality Han seal carving stones. Kang Youwei once said, "There are only two kinds of Han seal tablets left, such as "Shaomuro" and "Kaimu", which can be considered as the world's greatest treasure and the top instrument of seal script."　　The book of "Jinshifu", "Jinshifu Zuizhi Zuizhi", "Good Book of Stele and Poster", "Ma Ziyun, Shi Anchang, "Identification of Stele and Poster", etc. were recorded by Gu Yanwu in Qing Dynasty.

描述_ZN: The "Kong Biao Stele", ink topography of the whole paper stele Yang (the front and back of the stele are missing topography), mounted on a vertical axis. It measures 199 cm in length and 85.5 cm in width. It is written in 18 lines of official script, with 45 characters.　　Confucius Biao, with the character Yuan Shang, was the nineteenth grandson of Confucius and lived in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. At the beginning, he was promoted to the position of filial integrity, and was removed from the position of governor and Bo Chang Chang. Later, he served as a minister of the Shang Shu, a royal official, a governor of Boling, a minister of Xiapi, and a governor of Hedong. He resigned due to illness and retired. He died in the seventh month of the fourth year of Jianning in the Eastern Han Dynasty (171) at the age of 49. This monument was erected by 13 people, including Cui Lie, a former official (the title is on the shade of the monument) to praise his legacy. The original stone is now in the Confucius Temple in Qufu, Shandong Province.　　The inscription is simple and elegant, and can be regarded as a standard example of Eastern Han inscriptions. The inscription is written in the middle of a boundary grid, and the characters are small, but the spacing between characters and lines is extremely wide, making the layout clear and transparent. Yang Shoujing's "Hormone Feiqingge Review of Stele" says that his characters are "strong in strokes and strict in structure", which is the most definite comment. It has been listed as one of the most famous Han clerical works. It is a pity that the characters are more corroded and damaged.　　The character "Ying" in the fifth line and the character "Life" in the sixth line have been lost, but The word "life" in the sixth line of "Sitting at home without destiny" has been lost, but is still legible. In the sixth line, the word "cut" in the character "to cut the four evils" can be seen as "small" on the left. In the fourteenth line, the character "辯" is half of the character "辯", and the character "居" is visible in the remaining strokes. It must be an old topography from the middle and early Qing dynasty. Inscriptions of "Zhang Delong Jianzang Jinshi Script" and "Sanqu Zhang's Jinshi Shoukao" are on two sides.　　Song Ouyang Xiu's "The End of the Jigu Record", Ouyang Nian's "The Catalogue of the Jigu Record", Zhao Mingcheng's "Jinshilu", Hong Shi's "The Interpretation of Clerical Script", Chen Si's "Collection of Treasure Carvings", Ming Yang Shen's "Jinshilu Ancient Writings", Du Mu's "Jinlian Linlang", Qing Sun Chengze's "Gengzi Pin Xia Ji", Gu Yanwu's "Jinshilu Writings", Weng Fanggang's "Jinshilu Writings of the Two Han Dynasties", Qian Daxin's "The End of the Jinshilu Writings of Qian Yan Tang", Ruan Yuan's "Shanzuo Jinshilu Zhi", modern Wang Chang's The Jin Shi Zu Zu Zui Editorial", Fang Ruo's "Sui Pian" and other books.
