描述_EN: the finely modelled figure is of the compassionate bodhisattva avalokiteshvara, known in chinese as guanyin. although members of the imperial family were the most prestigious client for tiles, the largest customers by far were the numerous temple complexes all over china. here we see a very thick tile, constructed to provide a niche for the figure of the bodhisattva (an elevated being committed to attaining enlightenment), seated and holding a flask of ambrosia. at least as early as the song dynasty (960-1279), buddhist and daoist temples were using glazed tiles on all their exterior surfaces. originally it would have formed part of a wall of similar tiled images, for its unglazed back has raised ribs grooved to key into adjoining tiles.

描述_EN: this badge would have been worn on an overcoat for the court by an officer of the sixth rank, as indicated by use of egrets as a motif. this ming dynasty (1368-1644) rank badge is woven in the kesi tapestry technique, where colours are only woven on where the pattern requires, resulting in small gaps between woven patterns, giving the appearance of cut designs.

描述_EN: the horse was frequently one of a sequence of creatures shown on ridge tiles. the ming dynasty was a flourishing period for tile production. it is a bridge to the world of spirits and a platform for them to descend to earth. it is one of the beasts of the chinese zodiac. on roofs the most common decoration was tiling. in asia, the roof, by virtue of its position on a building, is deemed a point of communication between heaven and earth. chinese builders sought to harness auspicious spiritual forces and repel evil spirits with applied ornamentation freighted with symbolic meaning.
描述_ZN: 马经常是屋脊瓦片上显示的一连串生物之一。 明朝是一个瓦片生产的繁荣时期。 它是通向精神世界的桥梁，也是他们下凡的平台。 它是中国十二生肖中的一种动物。 在屋顶上，最常见的装饰是瓦片。 在亚洲，屋顶由于其在建筑物上的位置，被认为是天与地之间的沟通点。 中国的建筑家们试图用充满象征意义的装饰品来驾驭吉祥的精神力量和驱除邪恶的灵魂。

描述_EN: according to a number of later sources, the orchard factory was set up in the new capital, beijing, at the beginning of the ming dynasty in order to produce the finest carved lacquer. paintings reveal that folding chairs were used by ming emperors when on their travels.he might be hunting, inspecting territories or making sacrifices at the tombs of his ancestors. one of the most renowned of all imperial palace workshops was the orchard factory. this chair carries the mark of the xuande reign period (1426-35), although stylistically it would appear to date from rather later, towards the mid-16th century. the chair may be a product of that workshop. the chair is decorated with patterns of five-clawed dragons and lotus flowers. this folding armchair is among the museum's most important chinese treasures.
描述_ZN: 根据一些后来的资料，果园厂是在明朝初年在新首都北京设立的，目的是为了生产最好的雕漆。 画作显示，明朝皇帝在旅行时使用折叠椅。他可能是在打猎、视察领土或在祖先的坟墓前进行祭祀。 所有皇宫工坊中最著名的一个是果园工厂。 这把椅子带有宣德年间（1426-35）的标记，尽管从风格上看，它似乎是在更晚的时候，即16世纪中期。 这把椅子可能是那个工厂的产品。 这把椅子上装饰着五爪龙和莲花的图案。 这个折叠扶手椅是博物馆最重要的中国珍品之一。

描述_EN: a ‘bi’ is a flat circular slab of jade with a central hole. its function in prehistoric times remains unknown. however the ‘bi’ was made at least a thousand years before the ‘zhouli’ was written. an ancient chinese text entitled the ‘zhouli’ (‘rituals of zhou’) describes the ‘bi’ as a ceremonial object to sacrifice to heaven.
描述_ZN: "璧 "是一种扁平的圆形玉石板，中间有一个孔。 其在史前时代的功能仍然未知。 然而 "璧 "的制作时间至少比 "周礼 "的书写时间早一千年。 一篇名为《周礼》的中国古籍将 "璧 "描述为祭祀上天的礼器。

描述_EN: the height of cong varies drastically, ranging from 49 cm to a mere 3 cm. but long before writing was invented in china jade cong were used in a ritual context. tall cong are definitely more difficult to make than short ones. the outside walls are usually divided into sections by horizontal cuts in the four corners. a ‘cong’ is a jade cylinder that is square on the outside with a round perforation in the middle. an ancient chinese text called 'the rites of zhou' states that the cong was used to sacrifice to earth. recent archaeology in china has unearthed considerable quantity of cong from neolithic burial sites.
描述_ZN: 琮的高度差异很大，从49厘米到仅有3厘米不等。 但早在中国发明文字之前，玉琮就被用于祭祀。 高的铜钱肯定比短的更难制作。 外墙通常由四角的横切面分成若干部分。 一个 "琮 "是一个玉筒，外面是方形，中间有一个圆形的孔。 中国古籍《周礼》中说，琮是用来祭祀大地的。 最近在中国的考古工作中，从新石器时代的墓葬中发掘出了大量的玉琮。

描述_EN: kaolin clays were deposited earlier than loess: some 260 million years old, they were laid down when huge carboniferous forests flourished in north china. however, the firing range of neolithic kilns seldom exceeded 1,050°c, which means that the ewer was fired at much the same temperature as neolithic earthenwares, and the body has remained porous rather than become vitrified during firing. its form, with three bag-shaped legs, strap handle and spout, suggests it was a ewer in which water was boiled. the common raw material for neolithic chinese ceramics is loess, a wind-borne dust derived from igneous rocks (rocks formed from molten magma or lava), not kaolin-rich clays. the use of kaolin cays by the aboriginal potter could have been sheer coincidence, or it may have been deliberate, as the material had a superior resistance to the thermal shock that occurred, for example, when liquids were heated over a fire. made 1,000 years before writing was invented in china, there is no textual source to explain the function of this distinctive vessel. the great importance of this piece is that it is made from kaolin-rich clays, the same raw material used for porcelain, and had it been fired to a higher temperature it could be described as porcellaneous or as 'proto-porcelain'. this is because in northern china the latter was usually found beneath the loess and hence was more difficult to obtain. the mud on which these forests grew was of kaolin-rich sediments, washed by the rain from distant rocky highlands.
描述_ZN: 高岭土比黄土沉积得更早：大约有2.6亿年的历史，它们是在中国北方巨大的石炭纪森林盛行时沉积下来的。 然而，新石器时代窑炉的烧制范围很少超过1050°C，这意味着该陶器的烧制温度与新石器时代的陶器基本相同，器身在烧制过程中保持了多孔性而不是变成了玻璃。 它的形式，有三个袋状的腿，带状的手柄和水嘴，表明它是一个煮水的水壶。 新石器时代中国陶瓷的常见原料是黄土，一种从火成岩（由熔融岩浆或熔岩形成的岩石）中提取的随风飘散的尘埃，而不是富含高岭土的粘土。 原住民陶工使用高岭土可能完全是巧合，也可能是有意为之，因为这种材料对热冲击有很好的抵抗力，例如，当液体在火上加热时。 在中国发明文字之前的1000年制造的，没有任何文字资料可以解释这个独特的容器的功能。 这件作品的重要性在于它是由富含高岭土的粘土制成的，与瓷器的原料相同，如果它被烧到更高的温度，它可以被描述为瓷器或 "原瓷"。 这是因为在中国北方，后者通常被发现在黄土之下，因此更难获得。 这些森林生长的泥土是富含高岭土的沉积物，被来自遥远的岩石高地的雨水冲刷。

描述_EN: the inscription, situated on the back of the tile, would have been visible from the back of the temple, once the tile had been attached to the uppermost point of the roof. the architectural ornament has two large grooves on the sides of the plaque to secure it into position while the figure represents wei tuo, a buddhist deity commonly depicted as a warrior. to fund such an ornate buddhist ornament donations would have been received from the local monastic community. during the ming dynasty (1368-1644) tile production flourished. this fine example of the tilemaker's art, modelled with a standing figure in high relief, was designed for the main centre-piece on the roof ridge of a buddhist temple. kiln centres in china's northern provinces - hebei, for example - have been producing tiles from the 6th century to the present day.
描述_ZN: 碑文位于瓦片的背面，一旦瓦片被固定在屋顶的最上方，从寺庙的背面就可以看到。 建筑装饰品的两侧有两个大的凹槽，以固定它的位置，而人物代表韦陀，一个通常被描绘为战士的佛教神。 为了资助这样一个华丽的佛教装饰品，当地的僧侣们都会捐款。 在明朝（1368-1644）时期，瓦片生产蓬勃发展。 这是瓦匠艺术的一个很好的例子，以高浮雕的方式塑造了一个站立的人物，被设计为佛教寺庙屋脊上的主要中心部件。 中国北方省份的窑洞中心--例如河北--从6世纪到今天一直在生产瓦片。

描述_EN: but the text gives no description about the shape of the zhang. an ancient chinese text entitled the zhouli (rituals of zhou) describes a 'zhang' as a ceremonial object to sacrifice to the direction south. in the first few decades of the 20th century a fairly large number of jade blades with a curved end were excavated from neolithic sites, the present example being one of them. chinese archaeologists believe this type of blades is the zhang mentioned in the zhouli.
描述_ZN: 但该文本没有给出关于张的形状的描述。 一篇名为《周礼》的中国古籍将 "张 "描述为祭祀南方的礼器。 在20世纪的前几十年里，从新石器时代的遗址中发掘出了相当多的带有弧形末端的玉刃，本例就是其中之一。 中国考古学家认为这种类型的刀片就是《周礼》中提到的张。

描述_EN: the finished textiles were probably brought via chinese junks sailing to the philippines. judging from its shape, this fragment may have been taken from a roman catholic priest's chasuble. the crimson silk ground indicates that the vestment would probably have been worn on the feast day of a martyr. the repeat pattern of double-headed eagles over a stylised vase may have been intended to be an emblem adopted by the order of st augustine under hapsburg patronage. this vestment was probably woven in the east, in macau, for augustinian missionaries stationed in the philippines. the original emblem is the royal hapsburg eagles standing over a cardinal's hat (probably symbolising the authority of the crown and the church), which rests over the augustinian crest of a heart pierced with arrows.
描述_ZN: 成品纺织品可能是通过中国的船运到菲律宾的。 从它的形状来看，这块碎片可能是来自罗马天主教牧师的袍子。 深红色的丝绸地表明这件衣服可能是在殉道者的节日里穿的。 双头鹰在花瓶上的重复图案可能是圣奥古斯丁教团在哈布斯堡的赞助下采用的标志。 这件衣服可能是在东方的澳门为驻扎在菲律宾的奥古斯丁传教士编织的。 最初的徽记是哈布斯堡皇家老鹰站在红衣主教的帽子上（可能象征着王室和教会的权威），帽子放在奥古斯丁的心形徽章上，上面扎着箭。

描述_EN: the work is spuriously signed at the bottom right hand corner by li zhaodao (active during the tang dynasty, about ad 670-730) and bears suprious seals and inscriptions of some important connoisseurs, like ke jusi (1290-1343) and wen zhengming (1470-1559). ming collectors were likely to pay more attention to the authenticating inscriptions and seals on the painting rather than its style, and the forger probably took more care in imitating them than a real tang work. it depicts a gentleman accompanied by his servant approaching a cottage in the mountains to pay a visit to a friend. this large scale hanging scroll was probably painted in the second half of the 16th century or the first half of the 17th century at the end of the ming dynasty (1368-1644). the painting is clearly a product of the ming dynasty and the artist did not make any attempts to imitate a tang dynasty style.
描述_ZN: 该作品右下角有李昭道（活跃于唐代，约公元670-730年）的假签名，并有一些重要鉴赏家的印章和题词，如柯九思（1290-1343）和文征明（1470-1559）。 明朝的收藏家很可能更关注画上的鉴定铭文和印章，而不是它的风格，伪造者在模仿它们时可能比真正的唐代作品更谨慎。 它描绘了一位绅士在仆人的陪同下走近山中的小屋去拜访一位朋友。 这幅大型挂画可能是在16世纪下半叶或17世纪上半叶，在明朝末年（1368-1644）绘制的。 这幅画显然是明代的产物，画家没有试图模仿唐代的风格。

描述_ZN: 玉盘有各种不同的尺寸。 早期的玉盘通常没有雕刻的图案，就像这个例子。 这个圆盘会被认为是一个 "环"。 中国的语言学家习惯性地将中央有小孔的圆盘和中央有大孔的圆盘区分开来，即 "璧"，和 "璜"。 中国的玉盘生产始于新石器时代，一直持续到19世纪。

描述_EN: figures with turquoise and purple glazes were particularly popular; in this ming example, guan di is depicted in martial aspect, wearing full armour. in addition to large statues placed in city's temples, smaller wooden or porcelain images of guan di were made for worship. the figure would have been placed on an altar in a household or in a temple. guan di, the god of war, is one of the most important figures in chinese mythology and popular culture. with the name guan di, he was worshipped in temples and households as the daoist god of war and patron of honest merchants. his image comes from an historical figure, guan yu (about 161-220), a general who helped liu bei to establish the shu han dynasty in ad 221. after his death, he was venerated as a loyal and righteous figure, until he was given the title of an emperor in ad 1594.
描述_ZN: figures with turquoise and purple glazes were particularly popular; in this ming example, guan di is depicted in martial aspect, wearing full armour. 除了放置在城市寺庙中的大型雕像外，还制作了较小的木质或瓷质关帝像供人崇拜。 该雕像会被放置在家庭或寺庙的祭坛上。 关帝，战神，是中国神话和流行文化中最重要的人物之一。 他被称为关帝，在寺庙和家庭中被奉为道教的战神和诚实商人的守护者。 他的形象来自于一个历史人物，关羽（约161-220），一个帮助刘备在公元221年建立蜀汉王朝的将军。 他死后，被尊为忠义之士，直到公元1594年被封为皇帝。

描述_EN: the measure (dou) represents a container for wisdom and inspiration, but also holds an astronomical meaning: dou is the chinese name for the dipper, a part of the big dipper constellation. the god is often represented holding a writing brush in his right hand and a scroll or a tablet in his left hand; here, a trapezoidal grain measure is balanced in his upturning left foot. this bronze figure portraits kui xing, a daoist star-god connected with popular beliefs and astronomy. kui xing is the chief star in the big dipper constellation, but he is also called god of literature, and worshipped by candidates to the imperial examinations. dreaming of kui xing in the night before the exams was considered an auspicious sign.
描述_ZN: "斗 "代表着智慧和灵感的容器，同时也有天文意义："斗 "是北斗星的中文名称，是北斗星的一部分。 the god is often represented holding a writing brush in his right hand and a scroll or a tablet in his left hand; here, a trapezoidal grain measure is balanced in his upturning left foot. 此铜像为魁星，一个与大众信仰和天文学有关的道教星神。 魁星是北斗七星中的主星，但他也被称为文神，并被科举考试的考生所崇拜。 在考试前的晚上梦见魁星被认为是一个吉祥的征兆。

描述_EN: at the bottom left of the painting is the seal of an unidentified collector, reading: 'calligraphy and painting treasured in the collection of mr gao.' he specialised in landscape and flowers, and over the years he developed a highly distinctive style. typically he used 'boneless' ink washes to portrait flowers and plants in a descriptive manner, as demonstrated in this work. the same seal also appears in an album of flower paintings dated 1643, which might suggest that this scroll was produced around the same time, the year before the fall of the ming dynasty. xiang was born into a distinguished scholar-official family in jiaxing 嘉興, zhejiang province 浙江, and his grandfather was the great art collector xiang yuanbian 項元汴 (1525-1590). this hanging scroll, showing a bunch of flowers bound together with calamus, was painted by xiang shenmo 項聖謨 (1597-1658). the painting is signed on the right, above one of the many seals xiang used in his works.
描述_ZN: 画的左下方有一个身份不明的收藏家的印章，内容为 高先生收藏的书画作品"。 他擅长山水和花卉，多年来他形成了非常独特的风格。 通常他用 "无骨 "的水墨画来描述花草，正如这幅作品所展示的那样。 同样的印章也出现在1643年的花鸟画册中，这可能表明这幅卷轴是在同一时期，即明朝灭亡的前一年制作的。 祥生于浙江嘉兴的一个名门望族，他的祖父是伟大的艺术收藏家祥元汴（1525-1590）。 这幅挂轴表现的是用菖蒲捆绑的一束花，是项圣謨（1597-1658）所画。 这幅画的签名在右边，上面有他作品中使用的许多印章之一。

描述_EN: by contrast a 'zhuo' is a 'table with legs at the corners'. long rectangular tables were used as writing desks or set against a wall in order to display flowers or ornaments. both categories of chinese table had numerous uses and so cannot be classified by function. this type of table is known as 'an', meaning a table with in-set legs. this rectangular table of plain polished 'huali' wood has side panels of openwork carving and everted flanges at each end.
描述_ZN: 相比之下，"zhuo "是一种 "四角有腿的桌子"。 长方形的桌子被用作写字台或靠墙摆放，以便展示鲜花或装饰品。 这两类中国桌子都有很多用途，所以不能按功能分类。 这种类型的桌子被称为 "安"，意思是有固定腿的桌子。 这种长方形桌子由普通的抛光'华利'木料制成，侧面有镂空的雕刻，两端有常开的法兰盘。

描述_EN: the compact nature of the material comes from the way it is woven. blue background with a multicolored repeating design of interconnecting floral medallions within squares. it could also have been used as a furnishing fabric. it has a second set of warps (longitudinal threads) to bind the design-making wefts (transverse threads). in europe, the term lampas is used for such a weave. there is a selvedge at either side of the length. length of polychrome patterned silk. this term is difficult to translate into chinsese as traditionally textiles have been classified in other ways. the weight and style of the cloth make it suitable for decorating chinese-style book covers, and silk of this type is also used in several different ways on scroll paintings, albums of pictures and folding screens. the chinese term jin, an all-embracing name for any multi-coloured patterned cloth, would be the word used to describe this silk.
描述_ZN: 该材料的紧凑性来自于它的编织方式。 蓝色背景上有一个多色的重复设计，方块内有相互连接的花纹奖章。 它也可能被用作家具织物。 它有第二套经线（纵向线）来绑定设计的纬线（横向线）。 在欧洲，术语Lampas被用于这种编织。 在长度的两边有一个边角料。 长的多色花纹丝绸。 这个术语很难翻译成中文，因为传统上纺织品是以其他方式分类的。 这种布的重量和风格使它适合于装饰中国式的书皮，这种类型的丝绸也以几种不同的方式用于卷轴画、画册和折叠屏风。 中国的术语 "金"，是对任何多色花纹布的全称，将是用来描述这种丝绸的词。

描述_EN: (dated 1783?) buddhist silk thangka embroidered with a central figure of the buddhist divinity, avalokiteshvara. the figure has eight pairs of hands, two clasped in the attitude of mercy, the others holding respectively a praying wheel, a rosary, a lotus flower, a bow and arrow and a vase. behind are radiating hands with eyes, a double halo, a mountainous and wooded landscape and clouds. the latter, to the right, is an effigy of sakyamuni buddha with the hands raised in the attitude of preaching. yellow silk lining. the former, to the left, wears a peaked cap, and holds a vase in one hand, and a thunderbolt resting on a lotus in the other. above seated upon lotus pedestals and supported on clouds are six smaller figures, also with double halos, representing former manifestations of the same divinity. there are three narrow edging and a broad border of brocade all woven with close floral patterns in gold thread, dark blue, yellow, green and red silks. at the top are two gilt metal loops for suspension. in either corner of the foreground beneath are two figures seated upon mats, probably representing the dalai ("the vast") lama and the panchen (great doctor) lama, the two chief dignitaries of the tibetan worship.
描述_ZN: （日期为1783年？） 佛教丝质唐卡上绣有佛教神灵阿瓦洛蒂什瓦拉的中心图。 该图有八只手，两只手以慈悲的态度紧握，其他的手分别握着祈愿轮、念珠、莲花、弓箭和花瓶。 后面是带眼睛的放射状手，双光环，山林景观和云彩。 后者在右边，是一尊释迦牟尼佛的塑像，双手举起，作宣讲状。 黄色的丝绸衬里。 前者，在左边，戴着尖顶帽，一手拿着花瓶，另一只手拿着搁在莲花上的雷电。 上面是六个较小的人物，坐在莲花座上，支撑在云朵上，也有双光环，代表同一神灵以前的表现形式。 有三条窄边和一条宽边的锦缎，都是用金线、深蓝色、黄色、绿色和红色的丝绸织成的紧密花纹。 在顶部有两个镀金的金属环用于悬挂。 在前景的任何一角，有两个坐在垫子上的人物，可能是代表达赖（"广大"）喇嘛和班禅（伟大的医生）喇嘛，这是西藏崇拜的两位主要尊者。

描述_EN: the compact nature of the material comes from the way it is woven. blue background with a multicolored repeating design of interconnecting floral medallions within squares. it could also have been used as a furnishing fabric. it has a second set of warps (longitudinal threads) to bind the design-making wefts (transverse threads). in europe, the term lampas is used for such a weave. there is a selvedge at either side of the length. length of polychrome patterned silk. this term is difficult to translate into chinsese as traditionally textiles have been classified in other ways. the weight and style of the cloth make it suitable for decorating chinese-style book covers, and silk of this type is also used in several different ways on scroll paintings, albums of pictures and folding screens. the chinese term jin, an all-embracing name for any multi-coloured patterned cloth, would be the word used to describe this silk.
描述_ZN: 该材料的紧凑性来自于它的编织方式。 蓝色背景上有一个多色的重复设计，方块内有相互连接的花纹奖章。 它也可能被用作家具织物。 它有第二套经线（纵向线）来绑定设计的纬线（横向线）。 在欧洲，术语Lampas被用于这种编织。 在长度的两边有一个边角料。 长的多色花纹丝绸。 这个术语很难翻译成中文，因为传统上纺织品是以其他方式分类的。 这种布的重量和风格使它适合于装饰中国式的书皮，这种类型的丝绸也以几种不同的方式用于卷轴画、画册和折叠屏风。 中国的术语 "金"，是对任何多色花纹布的全称，将是用来描述这种丝绸的词。

描述_EN: the compact nature of the material comes from the way it is woven. blue background with a multicolored repeating design of interconnecting floral medallions within squares. it could also have been used as a furnishing fabric. it has a second set of warps (longitudinal threads) to bind the design-making wefts (transverse threads). in europe, the term lampas is used for such a weave. there is a selvedge at either side of the length. length of polychrome patterned silk. this term is difficult to translate into chinsese as traditionally textiles have been classified in other ways. the weight and style of the cloth make it suitable for decorating chinese-style book covers, and silk of this type is also used in several different ways on scroll paintings, albums of pictures and folding screens. the chinese term jin, an all-embracing name for any multi-coloured patterned cloth, would be the word used to describe this silk.
描述_ZN: 该材料的紧凑性来自于它的编织方式。 蓝色背景上有一个多色的重复设计，方块内有相互连接的花纹奖章。 它也可能被用作家具织物。 它有第二套经线（纵向线）来绑定设计的纬线（横向线）。 在欧洲，术语Lampas被用于这种编织。 在长度的两边有一个边角料。 长的多色花纹丝绸。 这个术语很难翻译成中文，因为传统上纺织品是以其他方式分类的。 这种布的重量和风格使它适合于装饰中国式的书皮，这种类型的丝绸也以几种不同的方式用于卷轴画、画册和折叠屏风。 中国的术语 "金"，是对任何多色花纹布的全称，将是用来描述这种丝绸的词。

描述_EN: the three sections on the lid all tell stories related to marriage, so the box was probably used in one of the crucial ceremonies leading up to a wedding. these included the exchange of horoscopes between the families of the bride and groom. astrological charts were important to ensure that the couple's destinies were linked together, for if the signs were unfavourable the marriage was unlikely to succeed. this oblong box is made of carved black lacquer on a red ground. this technique is strikingly reminiscent of the bold outlines of the book illustration that flourished at the time it was manufactured.
描述_ZN: 盖子上的三个部分都讲述了与婚姻有关的故事，所以这个盒子可能是在婚礼前的一个关键仪式上使用。 其中包括新郎和新娘家庭之间的星座交流。 占星图对于确保这对夫妇的命运联系在一起非常重要，因为如果星座不利，婚姻就不可能成功。 这个长方形盒子是由红底黑漆雕刻而成。 这种技术让人惊讶地联想到在制造它的时候，书本插图的大胆轮廓。

描述_ZN: 班特姆是印度尼西亚的一个港口，许多东亚货物通过这个港口运往欧洲。 精致的黄铜配件是西班牙或葡萄牙家具的风格。 它也成为了17和18世纪英国用于这种技术的名称。 这个漆木匣子的形式是欧洲式的。 这是一个 "bantam "作品的例子，是一种雕刻多色漆的技术。

描述_EN: the teapots are not usually glazed, but burnished and fired, and unlike the majority of chinese crafts, they can be signed by the potters. this teapot is an example of yixing ware produced at the beginning of the qing dynasty (1644-1910). the local clays in yixing have a high sand content and can be cream, red or warm brown. this example has an incised mark reading: 'made by hui mengchen in jingqi' (an old name for yixing). the yixing kilns, in the jangsu province of eastern china, have been known since the 16th century for their teapots.
描述_ZN: 茶壶通常不上釉，而是经过烧制，与大多数中国工艺品不同，它们可以由陶工签名。 此茶壶是清朝初年（1644-1910）生产的宜兴器的一个例子。 宜兴当地的粘土含沙量很高，可以是奶油色、红色或暖褐色。 这个例子有一个刻印的标记： 由惠孟臣在景岐制作"（宜兴的一个旧称）。 中国东部江苏省的宜兴窑，自16世纪以来就以其茶壶而闻名。

描述_EN: according to buddhist teachings, a bodhisattva is a deity on the path to reaching enlightenment. sea creatures swarm in the waves foaming over her bare feet. by this period (late ming) guanyin took on the aspect of an elegant lady in flowing robes. this graceful figure has been finely carved from rhinoceros horn and represents the 'compassionate' bodhisattva guanyin, also known as avalokiteshvara. here she is pouring from a bottle the sweet waters of salvation.
描述_ZN: 根据佛教教义，菩萨是通向开悟之路的神灵。 海洋生物蜂拥而至，在她的赤脚上冒着泡沫。 在这一时期（明末）观音菩萨呈现出一个身着飘逸长袍的优雅女士的形象。 这个优雅的形象是由犀牛角精雕细琢而成的，代表了 "慈悲 "的观世音菩萨，也被称为阿瓦洛蒂什瓦拉。 这里她正从瓶子里倒出救赎的甜水。

描述_EN: amitabha, the buddha of infinite light, is believed to dwell in the western paradise, a pure land where the faithful can be reborn. amitabha came to the v & a as one of a pair of figures, slightly under life-size. he wears floral ear jewellery. his throne is in the form of an open lotus flower, the upper row of petals pointing upwards towards amitabha. his companion figure is a lotus-bearing deity, probably the bodhisattva avalokiteshvara. his five-peaked crown encircles hair arranged in rows of tight curls, rising to a large protrusion or ushnisha, a sign of wisdom and enlightenment. he is sitting in the lotus position, soles of the feet upwards, with hands in the gesture of meditation and a facial expression of deep concentration.
描述_ZN: 阿弥陀佛，无量光菩萨，被认为居住在西方极乐世界，是信徒们可以转生的净土。 阿弥陀佛作为一对人物之一来到V&A，略低于真人大小。 他戴着花色的耳饰。 他的宝座是一朵开放的莲花，上面一排花瓣指向阿弥陀佛的方向。 他的同伴是一位手持莲花的神灵，可能是阿瓦洛蒂什瓦拉菩萨。 他的五峰冠环绕着一排排紧密卷曲的头发，上升到一个大的突起或ushnisha，是智慧和开悟的标志。 他坐于莲花座，脚底朝上，双手作禅定状，面部表情深沉专注。

描述_EN: images of bodhisattva were used in temples and shrines, and were particularly popular among devotees. this gilt bronze figure represents a bodhisattva, a holy being who has obtained the final enlightenment and has chosen to return to the world to help humanity. the inscription on this example dates the object to ad 534 and mentions a placed called tangxian in north china where this piece was probably made. it is a very rare example of devotional image from the eastern wei dynasty (534-577). only two other examples of this type survive from the period, one in the freer gallery in washington dc, the other in a private japanese collection.
描述_ZN: 菩萨的形象被用于寺庙和神社，在信徒中特别受欢迎。 这幅鎏金铜像代表了一个菩萨，一个获得最终觉悟并选择返回世界帮助人类的圣人。 这个例子上的铭文可以追溯到公元534年，并提到了中国北部一个叫唐县的地方，这件作品可能就是在那里制作的。 这是一个非常罕见的东魏时期（534-577）的虔诚形象的例子。 这一时期只有另外两个例子存世，一个在华盛顿特区的Freer画廊，另一个在日本的私人收藏中。

描述_EN: the 350 deities depicted represent the gods of the daoist pantheon, including the three purities, the three celestial worthies and the jade emperor. it would have rested on the shoulders of the daoist priest, and when he held up his arms, its decorative scheme would have been seen in all its glory by the onlookers. this sumptuous robe made for use in daoist religious ceremonies is embroidered with 350 deities and immortals. this is a 'robe of descent' - square in shape, sleeveless, with a round hole for the neck. originally, many of these personages had their names written beside them, but these have now largely worn away.
描述_ZN: 描绘的350个神灵代表了道教万神殿的神灵，包括三清、三仙和玉皇大帝。 它本来是放在道士的肩膀上的，当他举起手臂的时候，它的装饰方案就会被围观的人看到。 这件华美的袍子是为道教的宗教仪式而制作的，上面绣有350个神灵和仙人。 这是一件 "后裔长袍"--呈方形，无袖，颈部有一个圆孔。 最初，这些人物的旁边都写有他们的名字，但现在这些名字已经基本被磨掉了。

描述_EN: trade flourished along the famous silk road. the motif suggests that it was used for what the chinese considered that 'foreign' drink – wine made from grapes. the piece dates from the tang dynasty (618-907), an era when china was in close contact with the middle east and the west. this bowl is decorated with a moulded pattern of vines. the chinese people were fairly receptive to the customs and habits of other cultures, including drinking wine made from grapes as opposed to the traditional chinese wine made from rice.
描述_ZN: 贸易沿着著名的丝绸之路蓬勃发展。 这个图案表明它是用来盛放中国人认为的 "外国 "饮料--由葡萄制成的酒。 这件作品可以追溯到唐朝（618-907），一个中国与中东和西方紧密联系的时代。 这只碗上装饰着藤蔓的模样。 中国人相当容易接受其他文化的习俗和习惯，包括饮用葡萄酿制的葡萄酒，而不是传统的中国米酒。

描述_EN: this figure sculpted from stone represents the bodhissatva guanyin, an important buddhist deity, also known as the bodhissatva of compassion and avalokitesvara in sanskrit and who embodies the compassion of all buddhas. depictions of guanyin feature very widely in chinese material culture from the earliest times of buddhist worship in china in the late 2nd century ad. guanyin can be identified by the small figure of the amitaba buddha that sits in his crown. the lotus also represents the potential for attaining enlightenment. bodhisattvas (with museum no.a8-1913) are spiritually enlightened beings who help others attain enlightnment. here they each hold a lotus bud as a symbol of purity and goodness.
描述_ZN: 此石雕像代表菩提萨埵观音，是佛教的重要神灵，也被称为慈悲的菩提萨埵和梵文中的阿瓦罗基斯瓦拉，他体现了所有菩萨的慈悲。 从公元2世纪末中国最早的佛教崇拜时代开始，观音的形象就在中国的物质文化中广泛出现。 观音可以通过坐在他头顶上的阿弥陀佛的小像来识别。 莲子也代表着获得开悟的潜力。 菩萨（博物馆编号：A8-1913）是精神上开悟的众生，他们帮助别人达到开悟的程度。 在这里，他们每个人都拿着一朵莲花苞，象征着纯洁和善良。

描述_EN: it was set at the side of a road in southern shaanxi province in north china. many chinese buddhist artefacts were produced during a great period of expansion of the religion in china in the sixth century ad. a group of 26 buddhist believers paid for the column, which bears their names carved in rows. this four-sided limestone column is one of the v&a's foremost buddhist stone carvings. this was done, the inscription on the stone tells us, 'so that all wayfarers may gaze upon the radiant countenance, without having to turn aside their steps, and that travellers, resting themselves at this spot, may venerate the sacred images, not needing to take another path, that whether they are clergy or laity their hearts may be influenced, and whether they be monks and nuns or unordained, they may look upon this column with repectful eyes'. the main carved decoration is of the buddha on one side and of the religious debate between the bodhisattva manjusri (chinese name: wenshu), and the pious lay-believer vimalakirti (chinese name: weimojie).
描述_ZN: 它被放置在中国北方陕西省南部的一条公路边。 许多中国佛教文物是在公元六世纪该宗教在中国的大扩张时期产生的。 由26位佛教徒组成的团体为这根柱子支付了费用，柱子上刻着他们的名字，一排排的。 这根四边形的石灰石柱子是维也纳最重要的佛教石雕之一。 这样做，石头上的铭文告诉我们，"这样所有的路人都可以注视着光芒四射的面孔，而不必转身离开，旅行者在这个地方休息，可以敬仰圣像，而不必走另一条路，无论他们是神职人员还是俗人，他们的心都会受到影响，无论他们是僧人和尼姑还是没有受戒的人，都可以用恭敬的目光看着这个柱子。 主要的雕刻装饰是一边是菩萨，一边是文殊菩萨（中文名：文殊）和虔诚的信徒维摩诘（中文名：韦摩诘）之间的宗教辩论。

描述_EN: that the great wisdom and understanding of sakyamuni permeates all things like the scent of orchids. that the donors offer their praise. it expresses the donors' faith in the divine light that banishes bodies as if they were dirt. that its great beauty springs from the source of inspiration. it also expresses the wish that through the attainment of divine understanding one should pass into a state of calm and tranquil purity. it probably stood in a public place for passers-by to worship. it probably came from north china, from the borders of shaanxi and henan provinces. it is inscribed with the date of 544 ad and was paid for by five donors, three of them members of the same family. many chinese buddhist images and artefacts were produced during the great period of expansion of the religion in the sixth century ad, and this sculpture is one of the v&a's foremost buddhist stone carvings. on the face of the plinth, the long inscription states that the stele was carved as a memorial to one li hung-yen. this limestone carving of the buddha with two attendant bodhisattvas is typical in its style of late wei sculpture. that the stone was 'auspiciously carved' as a palace image so as to compare with that which is beyond compare. and, finally, that this sacrifice be as great as those of the past.
描述_ZN: 释迦牟尼的伟大智慧和理解像兰花的香味一样渗透到所有的事物中。 说明捐赠者提供了他们的赞美。 它表达了捐赠者对神圣之光的信仰，它驱逐了身体，就像它们是灰尘一样。 它的伟大之美来自灵感的源泉。 它还表达了这样的愿望：通过获得神圣的理解，人们应该进入一种平静和安宁的纯洁状态。 它可能矗立在一个公共场所，供过往的行人朝拜。 它可能来自中国北方，来自陕西省和河南省的边界。 它刻有公元544年的日期，由五个捐赠者支付，其中三个是同一家族的成员。 许多中国佛教的图像和工艺品是在公元六世纪该宗教的伟大扩张时期产生的，而这个雕塑是V&A最重要的佛教石雕之一。 在基座的表面，长长的铭文写道，这块石碑是为了纪念李洪彦而刻的。 这个石灰岩雕刻的菩萨和两个随从的菩萨是典型的晚期魏国雕塑风格。 这块石头被 "吉祥地雕刻 "为宫殿的形象，以便与那无法比拟的东西相比。 最后，希望这次祭祀能像过去的祭祀一样伟大。

描述_ZN: 他平静的表情和小个子使他非常平易近人，他的手势也是如此，张开的右手代表慷慨，举起的左手则代表无畏。 纤细、挺拔的躯干是中国北方雕塑的典型。 与其他菩萨一样，他有长长的头发，表明他对这个世界的持续依恋。 这个小的佛教人物代表了一个菩萨，一个为了帮助别人获得救赎而推迟自己的开悟的圣人。

描述_EN: compassionate guanyin has always been a favourite deity for chinese buddhists. in his left hand, guanyin holds a vase, said to relieve the thirst of his devotees. often known by the sanskrit name 'avalokitesvara', guanyin is said to have come from a ray of light emanating from the buddha amitabha. this typical representation shows him wearing a headdress incorporating the buddha amitabha, surrounded by a lotus halo (now damaged).
描述_ZN: 慈悲的观音菩萨一直是中国佛教徒喜爱的神灵。 他的左手拿着一个花瓶，据说是为了缓解信徒们的口渴。 通常以梵文名称 "阿瓦洛基斯瓦拉 "而闻名，据说观音来自于阿弥陀佛发出的一束光。 这幅典型的图画显示他戴着一个包含阿弥陀佛的头饰，周围有一个莲花光环（现已损坏）。

描述_EN: the poised calm of the buddhist deity guanyin (the chinese goddess of mercy) is contrasted with the liveliness of the little lion leaping up playfully. while it is very difficult to date small carvings of this type in steatite, it closely resembles white ceramic figures of guanyin from dehua (in fujian province), and hence possibly was made between about 1650 and 1750. this sculpture is a small masterpiece of serene composition.
描述_ZN: 佛教的观音菩萨（中国的慈悲女神）的沉着冷静与小狮子的活泼俏皮形成对比。 虽然很难确定这类硬玉小雕的年代，但它与福建德化的白陶观音非常相似，因此可能是在1650年至1750年间制作的。 这个雕塑是一个宁静构图的小杰作。

描述_EN: near the edges are huge guardian figures, chinese on the left and foreign on the right. above, musicians accompany the deceased on his journey to the afterlife. sogdians, natives of modern uzbekistan, travelled and traded in north china. they practised zoroastrianism, a fire-worshipping religion, and exposed their dead rather than cremating them. in the centre of the panel is a zoroastrian fire altar, flanked by half-human attendants. this slab supported a rectangular coffin platform, or funerary couch, made for a sogdian official.
描述_ZN: 靠近边缘的是巨大的守护者形象，左边是中国人，右边是外国人。 上面，音乐家们在死者的来世之旅中陪伴他。 索格达人，现代乌兹别克斯坦的土著，在中国北方旅行和贸易。 他们信奉拜火教，是一种火崇拜的宗教，他们将死者暴露在外面，而不是火化他们。 在画板的中央是一个拜火教的祭坛，两侧是半人的侍者。 这块板子支撑着一个长方形的棺材平台，或者说是殡仪馆的沙发，是为一个索格底亚官员制作的。

描述_EN: officials would have spent considerable time entertaining guests, such as the one who inspired this figure, from near and far. he sports a spectacularly well-groomed beard, a large pot-belly and a helmet-like hat. regular embassies seeking trade, peace, war and marriage alliances required hospitality. the dress, hat and features probably specified a particular foreign group.the man here is possibly a foreign dignitary. because of their position on a major trade route, silk road towns experienced a regular traffic of people passing through, many demanding attention from the local officials. many ethic groups can be identified in the tomb figures of the sui and tang dynasties. this glazed earthenware figure represents a foreign dignitary. this variety reflects the cosmopolitan flavour of life in towns along the silk road and in the capital, chang'an (present day xi'an). the chinese potters who modelled this type of figure clearly intended to show non-chinese.
描述_ZN: 官员们会花相当多的时间来招待来自远近的客人，比如这个人物的灵感。 他留着漂亮的胡子，有一个大肚子，戴着头盔似的帽子。 寻求贸易、和平、战争和婚姻联盟的定期使团需要受到款待。 衣着、帽子和特征可能指定了一个特定的外国群体，这里的人可能是一个外国政要。 由于处于主要贸易路线上，丝绸之路上的城镇经常有很多人经过，很多人要求当地官员关注。 在隋唐时期的墓葬人物中，可以发现许多种族群体。 这个釉面陶器形象代表了一位外国政要。 这种多样性反映了丝绸之路沿线城镇和首都长安（今西安）的世界性生活气息。 中国的陶艺家们为这种人物建模，显然是为了表现非中国人。

描述_EN: this ladle was probably used in preparation for drinking; a smaller, flatter type of spoon would have been used during the same period for food. by the beginning of the 7th century large quantities of silver pieces with exotic shapes and styles were imported along the silk road from iran and central asia to china. silver objects were not so highly coveted in china as in other ancient civilisations such as the roman or the parthian, but they became important luxury items for emperors and high-ranking officials during the tang dynasty (ad 618-960). chinese craftsmen often reproduced foreign shapes and acquired new manufacturing techniques from central asian silversmiths who had settled in chinese urban centres beginning in the mid 7th century.

描述_EN: the hairstyle and clothing of grave figures provide a fascinating insight into the fashion and taste of the time. the brocade design of clouds and floral scrolls on the silk robe was painted in pink, black, red and green with traces of gilding along the edges. about 60% of the original pigments is still visible on the surface. during the tang dynasty (ad 618-906) chinese graves were decorated with murals depicting scenes from court life, performances, or hunting activities, and were also enriched by a large variety of painted or glazed figures that were meant to assist or protect the deceased in the afterlife. in this example, the robe is characterised by a cape with a high collar and a v-shaped opening at the neck, long sleeves and frilled ends, from which the shoes emerge with their long, upturned toes. in this example, the figure was built using coils of clay which can still be seen inside, and smoothing the outside with a tool. this earthenware figure represents a richly dressed man, possibly a senior official or a courtier acting as a tomb guardian, and was placed in the tomb of a wealthy person. the whole body was painted with a white colour, and then a layer of pale pink was added to the flesh portions.
描述_ZN: 墓中人物的发型和服装提供了对当时的时尚和品味的迷人洞察力。 丝袍上的云纹和花纹图案用粉色、黑色、红色和绿色绘制，边缘有镀金的痕迹。 约60%的原始颜料在表面上仍然可见。 在唐代（公元618-906年），中国的坟墓被装饰以壁画，描绘宫廷生活、表演或狩猎活动的场景，同时也被大量的彩绘或釉面人物所充实，这些人物是为了在来世帮助或保护死者。 在这个例子中，长袍的特点是有一个高领的斗篷，颈部有一个V形的开口，长袖和流苏的末端，鞋子从里面露出长而上翘的脚趾。 在这个例子中，这个人物是用线圈粘土建造的，现在还可以看到里面的粘土，用工具把外面抹平。 这个陶塑代表了一个衣着华丽的人，可能是一个高级官员或作为护墓人的朝臣，被放置在一个富人的墓中。 整个身体被涂上白色，然后在肉的部分加上一层淡粉色。

描述_EN: the small figures of animals and birds cut out on the gold leaf represent the daoist belief of a paradise inhabited by human beings and animals who never grow old. mirrors in china were associated with daoist mysticism as well as being a functional object in the house. most ancient chinese mirrors are made of bronze and it is very rare to find one decorated with gold leaf.
描述_ZN: 在金箔上剪出的小动物和小鸟的形象代表了道家的信仰，即人类和动物居住的天堂，他们永远不会变老。 中国的镜子与道家的神秘主义有关，同时也是家里的一个实用物品。 中国古代的镜子大多是由青铜制成的，用金箔装饰的镜子是非常罕见的。

描述_EN: indeed the 'hufu' became the fashion in the 7th and early 8th century. it consisted of a tunic, loose trousers and high boots. like the men, the women also adopted the so-called 'foreigners’ dress' (‘hufu’) of their horse-riding neighbours. both men and women dressed in 'hufu' could be seen in the streets of the capital city chang'an. during the tang dynasty (618-907) both the men and women of the chinese aristocracy took to horse-riding.
描述_ZN: 事实上，"胡服 "在7世纪和8世纪初成为了一种时尚。 它包括一件外衣，宽松的裤子和高筒靴。 与男性一样，女性也采用了他们骑马的邻居的所谓 "洋人的衣服"（'胡服'）。 在首都长安的街道上可以看到穿着 "胡服 "的男女。 在唐朝（618-907），中国贵族的男人和女人都喜欢骑马。

描述_EN: it is possibly one of the 'kunlun boys' cited in historical records of the tang dynasty (ad 618-907), an ill-defined group from south-east asia, but not of chinese origin. this earthenware tomb figure represents a dark-skinned boy with curly hair, maybe a dancer. figures of this type were buried in graves to accompany the deceased in the afterlife.
描述_ZN: 它可能是唐朝（公元618-907年）历史记录中提到的 "昆仑童子 "之一，这是一个来自东南亚的不明确的群体，但不是中国的。 这个陶器墓的形象是一个皮肤黝黑、头发卷曲的男孩，可能是一个舞者。 这种类型的雕像被埋在坟墓里，陪伴死者来世。

描述_EN: the finial decoration is in openwork: on one pin, a lion roars amid leaf scrolls; on the other, a flying bird is seen against a cross-pattern. hairpins also became significantly larger, ranging from 20 to 35 cm (8 to 14 in.) in length. royal and aristocratic women wore buns of false hair decorated with an elaborate array of silver hairpins like these to dazzle and impress. the number of hairpins worn was also indicative of the wearer's social status. as women’s hairstyles became higher and more sophisticated, new types of hair accessories were developed to dress them. the tang dynasty marked the high point in the crafting of gold and silver hair ornaments, with both the technique and style showing the influence of persian and sasanian silverware. both motifs are surrounded by a border of half-palmettes, and further enhanced by the gilding of the pattern areas, a technique that also protects the silver surface from tarnishing. these two hairpins (zan) have been beaten into shape from sheet silver.
描述_ZN: the finial decoration is in openwork: on one pin, a lion roars amid leaf scrolls; on the other, a flying bird is seen against a cross-pattern. 发簪也明显变大，长度从20到35厘米（8到14英寸）不等。 皇室和贵族妇女戴着假发的发髻，上面装饰着像这样精致的银簪子，让人眼花缭乱，印象深刻。 佩戴的发卡数量也表明了佩戴者的社会地位。 随着妇女的发型变得更高、更精致，新类型的发饰也被开发出来，以装扮她们。 唐代标志着金银发饰制作的高潮，其技术和风格都显示了波斯和萨珊银器的影响。 这两个图案都被一个半掌状的边框所包围，并通过对图案区域的镀金来进一步加强，这种技术也能保护银器表面不被玷污。 这两支发簪（Zan）是用银片打成的。

描述_EN: the particular layout of the dragon motifs also marks it out from other garments in the v&a's collection. its decoration was undertaken on the loom as weaving techniques advanced, rather than being added later in the form of embroidery. it is front-fastening, whereas many other robes fasten to one side. this robe is unlike the other chinese women's garments in the museum, but we know from 18th-century pictorial sources that it was very fashionable at the time.
描述_ZN: 龙形图案的特殊布局也使它与V&A收藏的其他服装区别开来。 它的装饰是随着织造技术的发展在织机上进行的，而不是后来以刺绣的形式加入的。 它是正面扣的，而其他许多袍子都是扣在一边的。 这件袍子与博物馆中的其他中国妇女服装不同，但我们从18世纪的图片资料中得知，它在当时是非常时尚的。

描述_EN: silver objects became important luxury items for emperors and high-ranking officials during the tang dynasty (ad 618-960), but silver could also be used to enhance the appearance of objects. the animal and vine designs were popular motifs in the metalwork production of the silk road during the tang dynasty, and the granulation technique was frequently executed on silver products. in this eight-lobed bronze mirror, the back is covered with an elaborate embossed and chased silver decoration.
描述_ZN: 银器在唐代（公元618-960年）成为皇帝和高级官员的重要奢侈品，但银也可以用来增强物品的外观。 在唐代丝绸之路的金属制品生产中，动物和藤蔓图案是很受欢迎的图案，颗粒技术也经常在银制品上执行。 在这面八叶铜镜中，背面布满了精致的浮雕和鏤空银饰。

描述_EN: foreign dwarves such as depicted in this figure were popular as itinerant entertainers and were known to have served as court entertainers as well. the tang dynasty (619-907ad) can be said to have been one of the most liberal periods of chinese contact with the foreign world. such figures accentuate the obvious physiological differences of foreigners, not so much as caricatures, but rather to record and depict their 'foreign-ness'. one of the most vivid visual records of the trade and cultural exchange between the chinese and foreigners is retained in the form of ceramic figurines.
描述_ZN: 此图中所描绘的外国侏儒作为流动艺人很受欢迎，据说也曾担任过宫廷艺人。 唐朝（公元619-907年）可以说是中国与外国世界接触的最自由的时期之一。 这些陶俑强调了外国人明显的生理差异，与其说是漫画，不如说是为了记录和描绘他们的 "外国性"。 中国人和外国人之间的贸易和文化交流的最生动的视觉记录之一是以陶瓷塑像的形式保留下来的。

描述_EN: the presence of this and other similar figurines in tombs establishes that the chinese imperial family had adopted the pursuits of the neighbouring steppe peoples, including hunting with dogs. carvings dating from the sumerian empire (7000-6000 bc) have also been identified as saluqi. the hounds were also known in india from the time of alexander the great and in china from these figurines in 8th-century tombs. some people believe that the saluqi is the earliest domesticated dog. it is known from about 2100 bc in ancient egypt where these revered dogs were sometimes found mummified in royal tombs. this unglazed earthenware figure represents a saluqi, a coursing hound.
描述_ZN: 墓葬中出现的这个和其他类似的雕像证明了中国皇室已经采用了邻近草原民族的追求，包括用狗打猎。 苏美尔帝国（公元前7000-6000年）的雕刻也被认定为萨鲁奇。 印度亚历山大大帝时期的猎犬和中国8世纪古墓中的这些小雕像也是已知的。 有些人认为萨鲁奇是最早的驯化狗。 在公元前2100年左右的古埃及，这些受人尊敬的狗有时会在皇室墓穴中被发现制成木乃伊。 这个无釉陶俑表现的是一只萨鲁奇，一只猎犬。

描述_EN: finely carved head of a buddha with traces of pigments. the face is smoothly carved with a meditative expression, the eyes cast down beneath arched eyebrows. south asian features of the deity, such as the swirled strands of hair, the high-ridged nose and heavy eyelids still appear, yet the gently rounded face points to tang-chinese interests in the human form. the head bears stylistic features from a transitional period of chinese buddhist art at longmen. the hair is carved with triple-spiralled curls. over the course of the period, artisans created buddhist deities with increasing awareness of movements and soft flesh of the human body. a straight nose above curving lips and long, pendulous ears.
描述_ZN: 精雕细琢的菩萨头像，有颜料的痕迹。 面部雕刻流畅，表情沉思，眼睛在弧形的眉毛下投下。 神像的南亚特征，如旋转的发丝、高耸的鼻子和厚重的眼睑仍然出现，但柔和的圆脸表明了唐代人对人形的兴趣。 头部有龙门的中国佛教艺术过渡时期的风格特征。 头发上雕刻着三螺旋的卷发。 在这一时期，工匠们在创作佛教神像时对人体的动作和柔软的肉体有了越来越多的认识。 直的鼻子在弯曲的嘴唇上方，长而下垂的耳朵。

描述_EN: the marbling effect was achieved by twisting a light-coloured clay with a dark-coloured clay, and then using the twisted clays to form the jar. in the tang dynasty (618-907) daily utensils were usually made of stoneware and goods for burial were made of earthenware. this jar was probably a funerary piece, as lead-glazed vessels could poison the user.
描述_ZN: 大理石纹的效果是通过将浅色的粘土与深色的粘土缠绕在一起，然后用缠绕的粘土来形成罐子。 在唐代（618-907），日常用具通常由石器制成，而埋葬物品则由陶器制成。 这个罐子可能是一件殉葬品，因为铅釉器皿会使使用者中毒。

描述_EN: each panel depicts a different episode. although none of these are easily associated with any known chinese story, the theme running through the 8 panels is that of guanyin watching over those who suffer. this set of panels, woven in the kesi tapestry technique, depict guanyin (the goddess of mercy in chinese beliefs) helping humans overcome wordly difficulties.
描述_ZN: 每个板块都描述了一个不同的情节。 虽然这些都不容易与任何已知的中国故事联系起来，但贯穿这8块板子的主题是观世音菩萨保佑着那些受苦的人。 这组壁板是用克西挂毯技术织成的，描绘了观音（中国信仰中的慈悲女神）帮助人类克服文字上的困难。

描述_EN: in this example, the two characters yongji are incised on the base; they are the signature of the artist deng fujia, probably native of fujian in south-east china and active during the yongzheng (1723-1735) and qianlong (1736-1795) reigns. his works of art are particularly rare since he produced mainly luxury goods for the imperial household. this bamboo box was carved in the shape of a section of a pine tree trunk and shows pine tree branches in relief on the surface. carvings from materials of vegetable origin, like wood, bamboo or gourd, represent one of the most elaborate and refined crafts in china, and often bear the signature of the artist.
描述_ZN: in this example, the two characters yongji are incised on the base; they are the signature of the artist deng fujia, probably native of fujian in south-east china and active during the yongzheng (1723-1735) and qianlong (1736-1795) reigns. 他的艺术作品特别罕见，因为他主要为皇室制作奢侈品。 这个竹盒是按照松树树干的部分形状雕刻的，表面有松树枝的浮雕。 植物性材料的雕刻，如木头、竹子或葫芦，代表了中国最精细和精致的工艺之一，并经常带有艺术家的签名。

描述_EN: the group is divided into four pairs, each characterised by a different hairstyle; in this case the hair is coiled on top of the head and rise diagonally to one side. the body is decorated with yellow-brown, green and colourless lead glazes, from which comes the name sancai or 'three colours' given to this kind of ware. head and neck are left unglazed, sometimes with traces of unfired red painting on lips and cheeks, and of black colour on the eyes or hair. funerary objects, either figures or vessels and daily tools, were placed in the burial to recreate a familiar environment and to accompany the deceased in the afterlife. this earthenware figure is part of a group of eight female attendants or dancers, wearing high-waisted dresses and long shawls typical of the early tang period (ad 618-906). the use of tomb figures was a widespread practice in china since the han dynasty (208 bc-ad 220).
描述_ZN: the group is divided into four pairs, each characterised by a different hairstyle; in this case the hair is coiled on top of the head and rise diagonally to one side. 器身用黄褐色、绿色和无色的铅釉装饰，由此而来的名称是sancai或 "三色 "赋予这种器物。 头部和颈部没有上釉，有时在嘴唇和脸颊上有未烧制的红色绘画痕迹，眼睛或头发上有黑色的颜色。 有趣的物品，无论是人物还是器皿和日常工具，都被放置在墓葬中，以重塑一个熟悉的环境，并在来世陪伴死者。 这个陶俑是一组八名女性侍者或舞者的一部分，她们穿着高腰的衣服和长披肩，是唐代早期（公元618-906年）的典型代表。 自汉代（公元前208年-公元220年）以来，墓葬人物的使用在中国是一种广泛的做法。

描述_EN: the wreck is now commonly referred to as the ca mau wreck. the wreck was discovered off the southern coast of vietnam in 1998 near ca mau. this date corresponds to the reign of the yongzheng emperor (1723-35). this object was salvaged from the wreck of a trade ship thought to be a chinese junk, dating to approximately 1725. this object is one of a group of 182 pieces of porcelain acquired by the v&a from this wreck. the ship was loaded with chinese porcelain of various designs for export to south asia and europe.
描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_EN: the wreck is now commonly referred to as the ca mau wreck. the wreck was discovered off the southern coast of vietnam in 1998 near ca mau. this date corresponds to the reign of the yongzheng emperor (1723-35). this object was salvaged from the wreck of a trade ship thought to be a chinese junk, dating to approximately 1725. this object is one of a group of 182 pieces of porcelain acquired by the v&a from this wreck. the ship was loaded with chinese porcelain of various designs for export to south asia and europe.
描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_ZN: 该沉船现在通常被称为CA MAU沉船。 该沉船于1998年在越南南部海岸附近的CA MAU被发现。 这个日期对应于雍正皇帝的统治时期（1723-35）。 这个物品是从一艘贸易船的残骸中打捞出来的，它被认为是一艘中国货船，可以追溯到大约1725年。 这件物品是V&A从这艘沉船上获得的182件瓷器中的一件。 这艘船装载了出口到南亚和欧洲的各种设计的中国瓷器。

描述_EN: the central red panel is decorated with a four-clawed dragon rising above roaring sea waves and surrounded by clousd; at the corners are four daoist emblems (clockwise from top right): castanets, a gourd, a sheng musical instrument, and a fan; framed by a green border decorated with wavy floral stem. the top is edged with a band of dark blue cotton; the back is lined with red cotton. a slightly wider piece of the same material has been stitched across the top. it is decorated with two buddhist lions playing with a brocade ball, and surrouned by a green border of wavy floral stem. altar table frontal of cut voided satin velvet with red and green silk pile, brocaded in gilt paper strips.

描述_EN: in the tang dynasty (618-907) grave goods included replicas of men and women engaged in work or leisurely recreations, made from pottery but in reduced size. this figure of a plump woman reveals that it was not fashionable to be slim in the 8th century, because the favourite concubine of the emperor was a woman of considerable proportion.
描述_ZN: 在唐代（618-907）的墓葬物品中包括从事工作或休闲娱乐的男人和女人的复制品，由陶器制成但尺寸缩小。 这个丰满女人的形象表明，在8世纪，苗条并不是一种时尚，因为皇帝最喜欢的妃子是一个有相当比例的女人。

描述_EN: preissler was originally from bohemia (now the czech republic) but may have trained in nuremburg where this type of enamelling in black was a speciality. although the porcelain was made in china, the black enamelling and gilding was done by ignaz preissler in 1720-30. he is also known to have worked in breslau in germany and to have returned to bohemia (kronstadt) in later life to continue his work, probably with his son, daniel. the refined decoration on this chocolate beaker would have been specially commissioned by an aristocratic patron, either as a flattering gift for someone important, or as a cabinet piece which would have advertised the owner's educated tastes.
描述_ZN: Preissler最初来自波西米亚（现在的捷克共和国），但可能在纽伦堡接受过培训，在那里这种黑色的珐琅是一种专长。 虽然瓷器是在中国制造的，但黑色的珐琅和镀金是由伊尼亚兹-普雷斯勒在1720-30年完成的。 他也曾在德国的布雷斯劳工作，并在晚年回到波西米亚（喀琅施塔得）继续工作，可能与他的儿子丹尼尔一起。 这个巧克力烧杯上的精致装饰应该是由贵族赞助人特别委托制作的，要么是作为对重要人物的奉承礼物，要么是作为宣传主人有教养的品味的橱柜作品。

描述_EN: the group is divided into four pairs, each characterised by a different hairstyle; in this case the hair is combed in a large v-shaped chignon on the top of the head. neck and head are left unglazed, sometimes with traces of unfired red painting on lips and cheeks, and of black colour on the eyes or hair. the body is decorated with yellow-brown, green and colourless lead glazes, from which comes the name sancai or 'three colours' given to this kind of ware. funerary objects, either figures or vessels and daily tools, were placed in the burial to recreate a familiar environment and to accompany the deceased in the afterlife. this earthenware figure is part of a group of eight female attendants or dancers, wearing high-waisted dresses and long shawls typical of the early tang period (ad 608-907). the use of tomb figures was a widespread practice in china since the han dynasty (208 bc-ad 220).
描述_ZN: the group is divided into four pairs, each characterised by a different hairstyle; in this case the hair is combed in a large v-shaped chignon on the top of the head. 颈部和头部没有上釉，有时嘴唇和脸颊上有未烧制的红色绘画痕迹，眼睛或头发上有黑色的颜色。 器身用黄褐色、绿色和无色的铅釉装饰，由此而来的名称是sancai或 "三色 "赋予这种器物。 有趣的物品，无论是人物还是器皿和日常工具，都被放置在墓葬中，以重塑一个熟悉的环境，并在来世陪伴死者。 这个陶俑是一组八名女侍者或舞者的一部分，她们穿着高腰的衣服和长披肩，是唐代早期（公元608-907年）的典型代表。 自汉代（公元前208年-公元220年）以来，墓葬人物的使用在中国是一种广泛的做法。

描述_EN: the object was probably created by a wealthy hobbyist; on one side a mark reads: 'beautiful object made for enjoyment in the qianlong era (1736-95)'. eight small peaches are moulded on the surface, making a total of nine, an auspicious number associated with long life. the gourd is mounted on a hardwood stand decorated with silver inlays, almost certainly contemporary. the emperor's mark of qianlong, shanwan, is moulded in low relief on one shoulder. the marks made by the five sections of the mould are still visible. it was used as a display piece. its peach shape was obtained by using a mould which would have restricted its growth. this moulded gourd is the largest and most elaborate gourd in the collection.

描述_ZN: 除了五爪龙之外，皇帝的袍子也很可能带有十二个帝国的标志：包括火焰、斧头、酒杯等符号都巧妙地融入了袍子中。 皇帝穿的御用长袍通常被称为龙袍，部分原因是突出的龙形图案，这件长袍是为皇帝制作的，看起来是明亮的黄色，但它完全是在蓝色丝绸上绣的。 某些色调的黄色被限制为皇帝和他的直系亲属专用。

描述_EN: the intelligent and alert turn of the horse's head and the energy of its well-muscled body is testament to the immense skill of the tang potter. emperors of the tang dynasty (618-907) kept their horses in special stables and parks that occupied large tracts of land around the tang capital chang'an (present-day xian in shaanxi province). this magnificent tomb figure is proof of the passion the chinese have for beautiful pure-bred horses from the west. important tombs held models of these desirable animals.
描述_ZN: 马的头部聪明而警觉的转动，以及它肌肉发达的身体的能量，证明了唐代陶工的巨大技巧。 唐朝（618-907）的皇帝们把他们的马养在特殊的马厩和公园里，这些马厩和公园占据了唐朝首都长安（今陕西省西安市）周围的大片土地。 这个宏伟的墓像证明了中国人对来自西方的美丽纯种马的热情。 重要的墓葬里有这些理想动物的模型。

描述_EN: it was part of a series entitled "the elements", and including "air", "earth", "fire" and "water". during the first quarter of the eighteenth century, allegorical scenes of gallant encounters became very popular with french painters and engravers as they reflected the free spirit of the age. this scene may have been taken from a french print engraved by nataniel parr after a drawing by nicholas lancret entitled "la terre" , and published by thomas and john bowles in london in 1752. the plaque depicts the flirtatious advances of two young men, one of them up a ladder picking an apple and offering it to a young woman, the other enjoying pleasantries with a second woman.
描述_ZN: 它是题为 "元素 "系列的一部分，包括 "空气"、"地球"、"火 "和 "水"。 在十八世纪的前四分之一，寓言式的英勇邂逅场景在法国画家和雕刻家中非常流行，因为它们反映了那个时代的自由精神。 这个场景可能取自Nataniel Parr根据Nicholas Lancret的画作雕刻的法国版画，名为 "la terre"，由Thomas and John Bowles于1752年在伦敦出版。 这块牌子描绘了两个年轻人的调情，其中一个在梯子上摘了一个苹果送给一个年轻的女人，另一个在和另一个女人寒暄。

描述_ZN: 当它们在几个世纪后被意外地挖掘出来时，它们成了古董学者和收藏家的珍品。 该器皿和盖子上都有一个由两个象形文字组成的铭文。 古代中国的金属工匠用青铜制作了大量的食物和酒的容器，供祭祀使用。 每个容器根据其形状和功能都有一个特定的名字。 它有一个盖子，这表明它是用来储存酒的。 这个青铜酒器在中国被称为扇形器。 这些刻画的图画是该器皿主人的宗族标志。 这些器皿与死者埋在一起。

藏品名称_EN: perspective print depicting wan-nian qiao bridge in suzhou
描述_EN: european jesuit artists working at the chinese imperial court in the 17th and 18th centuries played an important role in introducing western painting styles to china. when a viewer looks at it through a mignifying lens of the peepbox, he or she will see the image in the right direction. interest in european perspective techniques spread to suzhou in eastern china, a centre for the production of woodblock prints to celebrate new year. images such as this, of suzhou’s wan-nian qiao bridge, were widely seen and brought western pictorial conventions to a large and varied audience. for this reason, the prints like this are printed in reverse and the inscriptions appear in back front. these perspective prints were made to be viewed through an optical device such as a peepbox incorporating a mirror.
描述_ZN: 17、18世纪在中国宫廷工作的欧洲耶稣会艺术家在向中国介绍西方绘画风格方面发挥了重要作用。 当观看者通过窥视盒的模拟镜头观看时，他或她会看到图像的正确方向。 对欧洲透视技术的兴趣传到了中国东部的苏州，那里是生产庆祝新年的木版画的中心。 像这样的苏州万年桥的图片被广泛看到，并把西方的绘画惯例带给了大量不同的观众。 由于这个原因，像这样的版画是反向印刷的，题词出现在后面的前面。 这些透视版画是为了通过光学设备，如带有镜子的窥视盒来观看。

描述_EN: marking the transition from childhood to adulthood, girls began to style their hair in buns with a pair of hairpins from the age of fifteen. this is also when the earliest form of chinese writing developed, and silk use was widely distributed throughout china. although men and women wore hairpins, its original owner was probably a woman. hairpins crafted from animal bones such as cattle, pig and deer were luxury items produced by local workshops for elite use. in ancient china, such hairpins symbolised an important rite of passage for young women, indicating they were ready to marry. numerous similar hairpins have been found in the tombs of aristocratic women in anyang, the capital city of the shang dynasty (1600-1046 bc), the earliest recorded dynasty in china's history. this bone hairpin (ji), carved with the figure of a stylised bird, is one of the oldest hair ornaments in the v&a.
描述_ZN: 标志着从童年到成年的过渡，女孩从15岁起就开始用一对发簪为自己的头发做发髻。 年，这也是最早的中国文字发展的时候，丝绸的使用在中国各地广泛分布。 虽然男人和女人都戴着簪子，但它的原主人可能是个女人。 用牛、猪、鹿等动物骨骼制作的发簪是由当地工场生产的供精英使用的奢侈品。 在古代中国，这种发簪象征着年轻女性的一种重要的成年仪式，表明她们已经准备好结婚。 在中国历史上最早的王朝--商朝（公元前1600-1046年）的首都安阳的贵族妇女的墓中发现了许多类似的发簪。 这个骨质发簪（ji），雕刻着一只造型鸟的形象，是V&a中最古老的发饰之一。

描述_EN: the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, their whiteness and fine texture. some kilns in the hebei province that produced xing ware came under this control, but were left to continue in their ceramic traditions, producing wares such as this ewer. it shares the xing ware characteristics of a hard, white porcelain body and glaze. xing ware was the earliest true porcelain made in china, and the world. this ewer (left) was made during the liao dynasty, a period when the khitan tribes-people took control of parts of northern china.
描述_ZN: 瓷器一词适用于由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做petuntse的白色石头混合制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、白色和精细的纹理。 河北省的一些生产邢器的窑场被控制了，但却被留在了他们的陶瓷传统中，生产出了像这个陶器这样的器物。 它具有邢器的特点，即硬而白的瓷体和釉面。 兴器是中国和世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 这个陶器（左）是在辽代制造的，当时契丹人控制了中国北方的部分地区。

描述_EN: while the wares produced at the yaozhou kiln complex enjoyed popularity from the end of the tang dynasty (618-906) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368), these bowls exhibit the olive green glaze and dense surface designs common to the yaozhou wares of the northern song period. carving was an important design method in yaozhou wares. angled tools were used to carve out the stylised waves and duck motif in sloping grooves, and comb-like tools provided the linear accents visible in the waves. the celadon glaze was then applied to the bowl, pooling in the crevices and laying thinly on raised areas. through firing, the pooled areas grew darker in colour, and the thinly glazed areas more transparent, creating the illusion of light and shadows in the surface design. these bowls are examples of the yaozhou wares typical of the northern song dynasty (960-1127). the dish on the far right would have began with a smooth body, partially dried (or ‘leather hard’).
描述_ZN: 从唐朝末年（618-906）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州窑群生产的瓷器都很受欢迎，这些碗表现出北宋时期耀州瓷器常见的橄榄绿釉和密集的表面图案。 雕花是耀州器物的重要设计方法。 角形工具被用来在倾斜的凹槽中雕刻出风格化的波浪和鸭子图案，而梳状工具则提供了波浪中可见的线性点缀。 然后将青瓷釉涂在碗上，在缝隙中积聚，在凸起的地方薄薄地铺上。 通过烧制，汇集的区域颜色越来越深，薄薄的釉面区域越来越透明，在表面设计中创造了光和影的幻觉。 这些碗是北宋时期（960-1127）典型的耀州器物的例子。 最右边的盘子开始时应该是光滑的器身，部分干燥（或 "皮革硬"）。

描述_EN: the artisans had to first make outer moulds composed of several sections around a prototype of the finished bronze and then reproduce the patterns in reverse on the surface of the sections. the cost, craftsmanship and labor required to produce these items further emphasises their value. they would then assemble the moulds around a core leaving a space between the outer and inner parts into which melted bronze would be poured. it was probably used as a communal drinking goblet or libation cup during the traditional rites for the ancestors celebrated by members of the royal family. it was made at the end of the shang dynasty, about 1150-1050 bc, probably in the capital anyang. bronze vessels like this were kept in temples for ceremonies or buried in graves to denote status and prestige. once the bronze had solidified, the outer moulds and the inner core were removed. the ownership and use of this and other ritual vessels were essential components of the ruling system under the shang kings, and contributed to their power and authority. this vessel, called a gu in chinese, is an exquisite example of bronze craftsmanship.
描述_ZN: 工匠们必须首先在成品青铜器的原型周围制作由几个部分组成的外模，然后在这些部分的表面反向复制图案。 生产这些物品所需的成本、工艺和劳动力进一步强调了其价值。 他们会把模具组装在一个核心部分周围，在外部和内部之间留出一个空间，把融化的青铜倒进去。 它可能是在皇室成员庆祝祖先的传统仪式上作为公共饮酒的高脚杯或奠酒杯。 它是在商朝末期，大约公元前1150-1050年制造的，可能是在首都安阳。 像这样的青铜器被保存在寺庙里进行仪式，或埋在坟墓里以表示地位和声望。 一旦青铜凝固，外部模具和内部核心就会被移除。 这个和其他礼器的拥有和使用是商王统治体系的重要组成部分，有助于他们的权力和权威。 这个容器在中国被称为古，是青铜工艺的一个精致的例子。

描述_EN: xing and ding wares were both made in kilns in the hebei province of china during the northern song dynasty (960-1127). porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, their whiteness and fine texture. the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture containing a of clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. although they look very similar, subtle differences in the glaze and the body of these dishes can link them to the wares produced in their respective places of origin, the cities of xing yao and ding yao. xing and ding wares were of the earliest true porcelains made in china, and the world. these two dishes are examples of xing ware (left) and ding ware (right).
描述_ZN: 北宋时期（960-1127年），中国河北的窑厂都在生产兴和鼎的器物。 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、白色和精细的纹理。 瓷器这一术语适用于由含有一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 虽然它们看起来非常相似，但这些餐具的釉面和器身的细微差别可以将它们与它们各自的产地--兴耀和定耀--生产的器物联系起来。 邢、定二器是中国乃至世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 这两个盘子是邢器（左）和鼎器（右）的例子。

描述_EN: vessels with green lead glaze are typical liao products. liao ceramics are generally plainer than their song counterparts. south china continued to be ruled by the song dynasty emperors. this ewer was made in a northern kiln, at a time when two chinese dynastic rulers co-existed. north china came under the rule of a nomadic people called the qidan, who established the liao dynasty.
描述_ZN: 带有绿色铅釉的容器是典型的辽代产品。 辽代的陶瓷一般比宋代的陶瓷更朴素。 南中国继续由宋朝的皇帝统治。 这个陶器是在北方的窑炉中制造的，当时有两个中国王朝的统治者并存。 中国北方被称为契丹的游牧民族统治，他们建立了辽朝。

描述_EN: inlaid bronzes were treasured by later collectors, since it was considered that they were a speciality of the perhaps mythical xia dynasty (believed by the chinese to be their earliest ruling dynasty, with traditional dates of 2205-1818 bc). it is a song dynasty copy of the flamboyant style of decoration that was at its height many centuries earlier in the late zhou period. this ewer shaped like a goose displays an elaborate inlaying technique, in which gold and silver wires and gold and silver sheets were inserted into pre-chiselled depressions on the surface of the bronze.
描述_ZN: 后来的收藏家们都很珍惜这些青铜器，因为他们认为这些青铜器是也许是神话中的夏朝的特产（中国人认为这是他们最早的统治王朝，传统日期为公元前2205-1818年）。 它是宋代仿制的浮夸的装饰风格，这种风格在许多世纪前的晚周时期达到顶峰。 这个形状像鹅的陶器展示了一种精致的镶嵌技术，其中金银丝和金银片被插入青铜器表面的预凿凹陷中。

描述_ZN: 尽管如此，这些花纹纺织品从18世纪末到1900年左右一直是人们的最爱。 像这样的彩绘丝绸并不是很耐用，因为颜料很容易从纺织品的表面擦掉。 这种丝绸纱布材料在中国被涂上了颜色，然后进口到欧洲被做成了被子。

描述_EN: and applied with a narrow yellow ground figured ribbon. the main part of the embroidery is located on the back side of the sleeves. informal wear. pink silk satin ground embroidered with multi coloured floss silks in satin and pekin knot stitch. han chinese woman's coat. the butterflies which are embroidered in pekin knot stitch are also outlined with white twisted thread in couched work. neck, cuffs, hem and side slits are trimmed with decorative borders made of a narrow black satin bias-cut band, a wider black silk band embroidered in shades of blue and white in satin stitches, and gold threads in couched work and an applied blue ground ribbon. blue silk plain weave lining. slit at sides. front fastening coat (three black silk loop and knot buttons), long and wide sleeves, straight folded-back cuffs. the sleeve bands are of blue silk satin embroidered in coloured silk with flowers, vases etc. the main body is embroidered with large butterflies, bats and scattered design of flowers ( peonies, orchid, magnolia, prunus).
描述_ZN: 并以窄的黄底花纹丝带进行装饰。 刺绣的主要部分位于袖子的背面。 非正式的磨损。 粉色真丝缎面地，用缎面和佩金结缝制的多色绒线丝绣。 汉族妇女的外套。 蝴蝶是用皮金结绣的，也是用白捻线勾勒出的耦合工作。 颈部、袖口、下摆和侧缝都有装饰性的边框，由一条窄的黑缎斜切带，一条较宽的黑丝带，用缎线绣出蓝色和白色的色调，还有金线的耦合工作和一条应用的蓝地丝带组成。 蓝色丝绸平纹衬里。 两侧开衩。 前扣大衣（三个黑丝圈和结扣），长而宽的袖子，直折袖口。 袖带是蓝色丝缎的，用彩色丝线绣有花朵、花瓶等。 主体绣有大蝴蝶、蝙蝠和散落的花朵图案（牡丹、兰花、玉兰、梅花）。

描述_EN: imperial robe of silk tapestry (kesi), woven in shades of blue and white, on a ground of gold thread and yellow silk; some of the details have been executed with the brush. the decoration consists of five-clawed dragons pursuing flaming jewels amid clouds, the interspaces being filled in with shou (longevity) characters, bats, and the eight buddhist emblems (bajixiang). the lower border and sleeves are encircled with a striped pattern culminating in waves on which are floating symbols of rank and riches, including the ruyi-sceptre with jewels and cash, and emblems of the four liberal arts: calligraphy, painting, music and chess, all bound with fillets.
描述_ZN: imperial robe of silk tapestry (kesi), woven in shades of blue and white, on a ground of gold thread and yellow silk; some of the details have been executed with the brush. 的装饰是由五爪龙在云中追逐火焰的珠宝组成的，中间的空间被填上了寿字、蝙蝠和佛教的八个标志（八吉祥）。 下边框和袖子上环绕着条纹图案，最终形成波浪，上面漂浮着等级和财富的象征，包括带有珠宝和现金的如意宝杖，以及书法、绘画、音乐和象棋这四种艺术的标志，全部用丝线捆绑。

描述_EN: while the wares produced at the yaozhou kiln complex enjoyed popularity from the end of the tang dynasty (618-906) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368), these bowls exhibit the olive green glaze and dense surface designs common to the yaozhou wares of the northern song period. moulded designs were an important feature of youzhou ware. the celadon glaze was then applied to the dish, pooling in the crevices and laying thinly on raised areas. multiple dishes could then be made by forming clay to this mould and pressing the walls to the appropriate thickness. a mould was then made of the dish and fired, creating a convex ‘hump-mould’. through firing, the pooled areas grew darker in colour and the thinly glazed areas more transparent, creating the illusion of light and shadows in the surface design. the process began with a master dish, which would have been carved by hand and fired. these bowls are examples of the yaozhou wares typical of the northern song dynasty (960-1127). the dish in the centre is an example of the this technique, which made detailed designs much more efficient to produce.
描述_ZN: 从唐朝末年（618-906）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州窑群生产的瓷器都很受欢迎，这些碗表现出北宋时期耀州瓷器常见的橄榄绿釉和密集的表面图案。 模塑设计是幽州器物的一个重要特征。 然后将青瓷釉涂在盘子上，在缝隙中积聚，在凸起的地方薄薄地铺上。 然后可以通过在这个模具上形成粘土并将壁压到适当的厚度来制作多个盘子。 然后在盘子上做一个模具并烧制，形成一个凸起的 "驼峰模具"。 通过烧制，汇集的区域颜色越来越深，薄釉的区域越来越透明，在表面设计中创造出光和影的幻觉。 这个过程是从一个主盘开始的，它将被手工雕刻和烧制。 这些碗是北宋时期（960-1127）典型的耀州器物的例子。 中间的盘子是这种技术的一个例子，它使详细的设计更有效地生产。

描述_ZN: 当他们在几个世纪后被意外发掘出来时，他们成为了古董学者和收藏家的珍品。 古代中国的金属工匠用青铜制作了大量的食物和酒的容器，供祭祀使用。 每个容器根据其形状和功能都有一个特定的名字。 这些器皿与死者埋在一起。 这种装粮食的容器在中国被称为 "圭"。

描述_EN: the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture of a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, their whiteness and fine texture. xing wares like the dish on the left were very popular both domestically and abroad, and were exported as far away as north africa during the years between 800-1000ad. xing and ding wares were of the earliest true porcelains made in china, and the world. these two dishes are examples of xing ware (left) and ding ware (right). chinese porcelains later achieved great popularity in western europe, although it was not until the early eighteenth century that european makers accurately duplicated true porcelain.
描述_ZN: 瓷器一词适用于由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做Petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、白色和精细的纹理。 像左边的盘子这样的兴器在国内外都非常流行，在公元800-1000年期间，被出口到遥远的非洲北部。 邢、定二器是中国乃至世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 这两个盘子是邢器（左）和鼎器（右）的例子。 中国的瓷器后来在西欧大受欢迎，尽管直到18世纪初，欧洲的制造商才准确地复制了真正的瓷器。

描述_EN: later european collectors gave these wares the fanciful name of ‘celadon’. resembling jade, they were admired for their tranquil beauty. green-glazed vessels were exported in large quantities to south-east asia and the middle east. the yaozhou kilns in shaanxi province excelled in the production of objects with bold carved or moulded designs under a green olive glaze. they were often used in buddhist tea ceremonies and meditation rituals. china produced many types of green-glazed wares, in shades ranging from olive to grass to grey-blue. the most popular examples were made in the south, at the yue and longquan kilns in zhejiang province, but some kilns in the north also specialised in green-glazed wares.
描述_ZN: 后来的欧洲收藏家给这些器物起了一个奇怪的名字 "青瓷"。 类似于玉石，它们因其静谧的美感而受到推崇。 绿釉器皿被大量出口到东南亚和中东地区。 陕西省耀州窑擅长生产绿橄榄釉下的大胆雕刻或模制图案的物品。 它们经常被用于佛教的茶道和冥想仪式中。 中国生产了许多类型的绿釉器皿，色调从橄榄到草到灰蓝不等。 最流行的例子是在南方，在浙江的越窑和龙泉窑，但北方的一些窑场也专门生产绿釉器皿。

描述_EN: this offering jar has a simple carved pattern of lotus petals and buds. this was a common burial ritual in song china, particularly in south china, and funerary jars containing rice were buried in pairs. such jars would have been filled with offerings of rice for the souls of the dead, and then buried in the tombs of the wealthy. this decoration may be significant, for it is linked with buddhist beliefs about rebirth in the western paradise.
描述_ZN: 这个供奉罐有一个简单的莲花花瓣和花蕾的雕刻图案。 这是宋代中国常见的葬仪，尤其是在中国南方，装米的陪葬品罐子是成对埋葬的。 这种罐子会装满供奉给死者灵魂的米，然后埋在富人的坟墓里。 这种装饰可能是重要的，因为它与佛教关于在西方极乐世界重生的信仰有关。

描述_EN: this dish is an example of the yaozhou wares typical of the northern song dynasty (960-1127). while the wares produced at the yaozhou kiln complex enjoyed popularity from the end of the tang dynasty (618-906) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368), these dishes exhibit the olive green glaze and dense surface designs common to the yaozhou wares of the northern song period. carving was an important method of surface decoration in yaozhou ware. angled tools were used to carve out the stylised waves and duck in sloping grooves, and comb-like tools provided the linear accents visible in the waves. the celadon glaze was then applied to the dish, pooling in the crevices and laying thinly on raised areas. through firing, the pooled areas grew darker in colour and the thinly glazed areas more transparent, creating the illusion of light and shadows in the surface design. the dish on the far left would have begun with a smooth clay body, partially dried (or ‘leather hard’).
描述_ZN: 此盘是北宋时期典型的耀州器皿的一个例子（960-1127）。 从唐朝末年（618-906）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州窑群生产的器物一直很受欢迎，这些盘子展示了北宋时期耀州器物常见的橄榄绿釉和密集的表面图案。 雕刻是耀州器物表面装饰的一种重要方法。 角形工具被用来在倾斜的凹槽中雕刻出风格化的波浪和鸭子，而梳状工具则提供了波浪中可见的线性点缀。 然后将青瓷釉涂在盘子上，在缝隙中积聚，在凸起的地方薄薄地铺上。 通过烧制，汇集的区域颜色越来越深，薄釉的区域越来越透明，在表面设计中创造出光和影的幻觉。 最左边的盘子开始时应该是光滑的泥体，部分干燥（或 "皮革硬"）。

描述_EN: the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture of a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, their whiteness and fine texture. xing wares were very popular both domestically and abroad, and were exported as far away as north africa during the years between 800-1000ad. this lion figure is an example of xing ware, the earliest true porcelain made in china, and the world. chinese porcelains later achieved great popularity in western europe, although it was not until the early eighteenth century that european makers accurately duplicated true porcelain.
描述_ZN: 瓷器一词适用于由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做Petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、白色和精细的纹理。 兴器在国内和国外都非常流行，在公元800-1000年期间被出口到遥远的非洲北部。 这个狮子图是邢器的一个例子，是中国和世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 中国的瓷器后来在西欧大受欢迎，尽管直到18世纪初，欧洲的制造商才准确地复制了真正的瓷器。

描述_EN: this dish is a splendid example of craftsmanship from the period of the song dynasty (960-1279), and shows the luxury and prosperity enjoyed by a certain sector of society. gold was used only in the imperial courts or in the homes of the wealthiest urban residents. we do not know what was served in or eaten from this dish, but the small size suggests that it might have been used as a serving dish for sweetmeats, pickles, or for an individual helping of a meal, in which case it was likely to have been part of a large service. the lotus design in the centre is unlikely to have any link to the food served in it even though both lotus roots and seeds were common ingredients.
描述_ZN: 此盘是宋代（960-1279）时期工艺的杰出范例，显示了社会中某一阶层所享有的奢侈和繁荣。 黄金只在朝廷或最富有的城市居民家中使用。 我们不知道这个盘子里装的是什么或吃的是什么，但它的小尺寸表明它可能被用作盛放甜食、腌制食品的盘子，或用于单独的饭菜，在这种情况下，它可能是大型服务的一部分。 中间的莲花图案不太可能与盛放的食物有任何联系，尽管莲藕和种子都是常见的原料。

描述_EN: the term porcelain refers to ceramics made from a mixture containing a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, whiteness after firing and fine texture. ding wares were among the earliest true porcelains to be made made in china, and indeed in the world. it would have been kept well away from the kitchen in order to protect the salt from absorbing any cooking odours or fumes. this lidded jar is an example of ding ware, made in hebei province in china during the northern song dynasty (960-1127). the shape of this jar suggests that it was used in a practical way, for storing salt needed for the preparation of brick tea.
描述_ZN: 瓷器一词是指由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，这种混合物在高温下烧制。 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、烧制后的白度和精细的纹理。 丁器是中国乃至世界上最早的真正的瓷器之一。 它应该被放在远离厨房的地方，以保护盐不吸收任何烹饪的气味或烟雾。 这个盖子是中国北宋时期河北制造的鼎器的一个例子（960-1127）。 这个罐子的形状表明它是以一种实用的方式使用的，用于储存制备砖茶所需的盐。

描述_EN: this bowl began with a smooth body, partially dried (or ‘leather hard’). while the wares produced at the yaozhou kiln complex enjoyed popularity from the end of the tang dynasty (618-906) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368), this bowl exhibits the olive green glaze and dense floral designs common to the yaozhou wares of the northern song period. carving was an important method of surface decoration in yaozhou wares. the glaze was then applied, pooling in the crevices and laying thinly on raised areas. using an angled tool, the floral pattern was carved out of the surface in sloping grooves. through firing, the pooled areas grew darker in colour and the thinly glazed areas more transparent, thus creating illusion of light and shadows in the surface design. this bowl is an example of the yaozhou wares typical of the northern song dynasty (960-1127).
描述_ZN: 此碗开始是光滑的身体，部分干燥（或 "皮革硬"）。 从唐朝末年（618-906）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州窑群生产的器物都很受欢迎，这只碗展示了北宋时期耀州器物常见的橄榄绿釉和密集的花卉图案。 雕刻是耀州器物表面装饰的一种重要方法。 然后施釉，在缝隙中积聚，在凸起的地方薄薄地铺上。 使用倾斜的工具，将花纹刻在表面的倾斜的沟槽中。 通过烧制，汇集的区域颜色越来越深，薄釉的区域越来越透明，从而在表面设计中创造了光和影的幻觉。 这只碗是北宋时期典型的耀州器皿的例子（960-1127）。

描述_EN: while the wares produced at the yaozhou kiln complex enjoyed popularity from the end of the tang dynasty (618-906) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368), this bowl exhibits the olive green glaze and dense floral designs common to the yaozhou wares of the northern song period. carved pieces began with a smooth body, partially dried (or ‘leather hard’). moulds were often used to avoid the time consumption and labour intensity of this process, as is demonstrated by this bowl. the glaze was then applied, pooling in the crevices and laying thinly on raised areas. using an angled tool, the floral pattern was carved out of the surface in sloping grooves. through firing, the pooled areas grew darker in colour and the thinly glazed areas more transparent, thus creating illusion of light and shadows in the surface design. surface patterns of yaozhou wares were either carved or moulded onto the body before firing. a master dish would have been carved and fired, from which convex ‘hump-mould’ was taken. this mould then acted as the template for multiple dishes to be formed. this bowl is an example of the yaozhou wares typical of the northern song dynasty (960-1127).
描述_ZN: 从唐朝末年（618-906）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州窑群生产的器物都很受欢迎，这只碗展示了北宋时期耀州器物常见的橄榄绿釉和密集的花卉图案。 雕刻的作品开始时是光滑的器身，部分干燥（或 "皮革硬化"）。 经常使用模具来避免这一过程的时间消耗和劳动强度，这一点在这个碗上得到了证明。 然后施釉，在缝隙中积聚，在凸起的地方薄薄地铺上。 使用倾斜的工具，将花纹刻在表面的倾斜的沟槽中。 通过烧制，汇集的区域颜色越来越深，薄釉的区域越来越透明，从而在表面设计中创造了光和影的幻觉。 耀州器物的表面图案在烧制前被雕刻或模塑在器物上。 一个主盘将被雕刻和烧制，从它上面取下凸起的 "驼峰模具"。 这个模子然后作为模板，用于形成多个盘子。 这只碗是北宋时期典型的耀州器皿的例子（960-1127）。

描述_EN: porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, whiteness and fine texture. the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture containing a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. this bowl is an example of ding ware, made in the hebei province of china during the northern song dynasty (960-1127). this bowl is typical of ding wares in its ivory-white hue and incised decoration. ding wares were of the earliest true porcelains made in china, and the world. the use of coal instead of firewood in the ding kilns also created a higher firing temperature and an ideal oxidising atmosphere, perfect for the production of ivory white ding porcelain. the lotus was strongly associated with buddhism, and was a popular motif in this period. the exterior is carved with an abstract lotus leaf pattern, and the inside with lotus flowers. it is possible the bowl, due to its size and decoration, was utilised in buddhist rituals.
描述_ZN: 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、白色和精细的纹理。 瓷器这一术语适用于由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 此碗是北宋时期中国河北制造的鼎器的一个例子。 此碗在象牙白的色调和刻画的装饰上是典型的鼎器。 丁器是中国乃至世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 鼎窑使用煤而不是木柴，也创造了更高的烧制温度和理想的氧化气氛，非常适合生产象牙白的鼎瓷。 荷花与佛教有着密切的联系，是这一时期的流行图案。 外部刻有抽象的荷叶图案，内部刻有荷花。 由于其尺寸和装饰，这只碗有可能被用于佛教仪式。

描述_EN: porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, whiteness after firing and fine texture. the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture containing a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. this bowl and stand are examples of ding ware, made in the hebei province of china during the northern song dynasty (960-1127). the aubergine-brown colour of this bowl and its stand is known as ‘purple ding’, and a rare find. ding wares were of the earliest true porcelains made in china, and the world. despite having such a different appearance in colour, they are still characteristic of ding ware in their bright white bodies and burnished glaze. while most ding wares are characterised by their ivory-white tone, a few examples have black, brown and green glazes.
描述_ZN: 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、烧制后的白度和精细的纹理。 瓷器这一术语适用于由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 此碗和支架是北宋时期中国河北制造的鼎器的例子。 此碗及其支架的青褐色被称为 "紫丁"，是一种罕见的发现。 丁器是中国乃至世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 尽管在颜色上有如此不同的外观，但它们在亮白的器身和烧制的釉面上仍然具有鼎器的特征。 虽然大多数的鼎器的特点是象牙白的色调，但也有少数例子有黑色、棕色和绿色的釉面。

描述_EN: large hanging with a central vertical seam. the ground of the textile is red satin waeve silk and this is weft-patterned in various colours. the main field of the textile consists of large flower and foliage bands, while across the bottom is a narrow border of key-fret and small dragon bands. the hanging is lined with beige plain weave cotton. across the top is a broad border consisting of bands of key frets, small dragons and dragons with phoenixes. the pattern is arranged in three sections. there is a supplementary warp to bind the pattern wefts. there is a small handwritten paper label stuck on one corner of the lining. next to the paper label are two red characters stamped straight onto the lining
描述_ZN: 大挂，中央有竖缝。 纺织物的地面是红色的缎面海丝，这是由各种颜色的纬线图案组成的。 纺织物的主场由大的花和叶带组成，而横跨底部的是一个由钥匙扣和小龙带组成的窄边。 该挂毯以米色平纹棉布为衬。 横跨顶部的是一个宽阔的边框，由关键的雀斑、小龙和龙凤呈祥的带子组成。 图案分三部分排列。 有一个补充经线来绑定图案的纬线。 有一个小的手写纸标签贴在里子的一角。 在纸质标签的旁边有两个红色的字直接印在里子上。

描述_EN: this plate is a good example of the ware. although cizhou wares were made in a number of kilns in different regions, they are linked by shared design characteristics. its stoneware body is decorated with a white slip (a diluted white clay which gives a consistent ground colour) over the surface, and the floral design carved through this slip to form a contrasting curvilinear design. this dish is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the song dynasty (960-1279).
描述_ZN: 此盘是该器皿的一个很好的例子。 虽然慈溪器皿是在不同地区的一些窑场生产的，但它们因共同的设计特点而联系在一起。 它的石器主体表面用白滑（一种稀释的白泥，使地面颜色一致）进行装饰，并通过这种滑液雕刻出花卉图案，形成一种对比强烈的曲线设计。 这个盘子是慈航器的一个例子，慈航器是宋朝（960-1279）时期中国北方的一种陶瓷。
