描述_EN: known as suzhou numerals, they were used by traders to display the price of goods. but, as s. the number '9' is written in black ink, in cursive script, on the sole of the shoe. wells williams notes in the chinese commerical guide (1863), the waves of migration from around china in the 1850s, including guangdong and fujian provinces, where many were facing destitution caused by famine and civil war, had vastly increased the export of neatly crafted straw slippers and other footwear. the upper has a green paper interlining and double ridges to hold its shape. prior to the gold rushes in california in 1849 and australia in 1851, chinese shoes had rarely been exported. in the 19th century, well-to-do men wore backless, square-toed slippers like these tuo xie at home as a type of relaxed footwear during the summer. this pair, made from finely plaited rushes, is decorated with a lozenge pattern in basketweave on the insoles, with leather soles for durability. this type of numerical symbol appeared at the turn of the 20th century. eventually, many chinese settled abroad and engaged in a variety of businesses.
描述_ZN: 被称为苏州数字，它们被商人用来显示货物的价格。 但是，正如S. 数字'9'是用黑色墨水写在鞋底的草书上。 威尔斯-威廉斯在《中国商业指南》（1863年）中指出，19世纪50年代来自中国各地的移民潮，包括广东和福建两省，其中许多人面临着饥荒和内战造成的贫困，这大大增加了整齐的草鞋和其他鞋子的出口。 鞋面有绿色的纸质衬里和双脊来保持其形状。 在1849年加利福尼亚和1851年澳大利亚的淘金热之前，中国的鞋子很少被出口。 在19世纪，富裕的男人在家里穿露背的方头拖鞋，像这样的拖鞋在夏天是一种休闲的鞋类。 这双拖鞋是用细密的芦苇编成的，鞋垫上有菱形图案的花篮，皮鞋底很耐用。 这种类型的数字符号出现在20世纪初。 最终，许多中国人在国外定居并从事各种商业活动。

描述_EN: grass slippers (cao xie) are among the oldest and simplest forms of outdoor footwear in china, with soles made from woven rice straw and uppers of plaited rush. traditionally, family members of the deceased would wear undyed coarse hemp clothing and headbands, along with straw sandals, at a funeral to express filial piety, putting aside personal appearance and comfort to grieve for the passing of loved ones. peasants wore straw shoes such as these while working in the fields, gathering firewood and herbs, or hunting in the mountains, regardless of the weather. although the shoes look uncomfortable to wear, their coarse soles grip efficiently to slippery surfaces. by displaying useful and commercial goods from across the world made from discarded materials, the museum aimed to promote corporate awareness of environmental sustainability and drive innovative uses from scraps or surplus materials. sandals made from straw were even fitted to the hooves of cattle and pigs to wear while being led along muddy roads. in china, straw shoes are also associated with mourning. these close-toe slippers were originally acquired for the v&a’s bethnal green branch, which opened in 1872, to illustrate the use of waste products.
描述_ZN: 草鞋是中国最古老和最简单的户外鞋类形式之一，鞋底由稻草编织而成，鞋面由草编而成。 传统上，死者的家人会在葬礼上穿上未染色的粗麻衣和头巾，再加上草鞋，以表达孝心，抛开个人的外表和舒适感，为亲人的离去而悲伤。 农民穿着这样的草鞋在田间劳作，收集柴火和草药，或在山上打猎，无论天气如何。 虽然这种鞋看起来不舒服，但它们的粗鞋底能有效地抓紧湿滑的表面。 通过展示来自世界各地的由废弃材料制成的有用和商业商品，该博物馆旨在促进企业对环境可持续性的认识，并推动对废品或剩余材料的创新利用。 用稻草做的鞋甚至被装在牛和猪的蹄子上，以便在泥泞的道路上被牵着走。 在中国，草鞋也与丧事有关。 这些贴脚拖鞋最初是为1872年开业的V&a's bethnal green分店购买的，以说明废品的使用情况。

描述_EN: the top line is edged with buttonhole stitches in twisted magenta yarn, arranged closely together, with flat gilt-paper strips woven in and out of these foundation stitches to form a basket-work pattern. children's shoes were often used to showcase a multitude of embroidery techniques. for this pair, untwisted floss silks worked in satin stitches have been used to depict floral scrolls on the yellow satin uppers. this decorative technique, known as overlock embroidery (suo bian xiu), was frequently used to finish the raw edges of purses or shoe uppers. the toe caps in brown velvet are embroidered with couched gold-wrapped threads and knot stitches, resembling a butterfly with flowers beneath its wings.
描述_ZN: 顶线用扭曲的洋红色纱线的扣眼线镶边，紧密地排列在一起，扁平的鎏金纸条在这些基础针线中交织，形成一个篮子的图案。 儿童的鞋子经常被用来展示大量的刺绣技术。 在这双鞋中，用缎子缝制的无捻线丝绸被用来描绘黄色缎子鞋面上的花纹。 这种装饰技术被称为包边绣（suo bian xiu），经常被用来完成皮包或鞋面的原始边缘。 棕色天鹅绒的脚趾盖用金丝线和结针绣出，就像一只翅膀下有花的蝴蝶。

描述_EN: this bottle is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the song dynasty (960-1279). cizhou wares were utilitarian at their time of production and were made in relatively large numbers. however, some of these 'prunus vases' are inscribed with the chinese words 'fine wine'. although they were not given high praise at the time of production, the bold designs and simple shapes of cizhou wares were later treasured by japanese and western connoisseurs alike. the studio pottery movement in britain found affinity with ceramics like this vase, which bernard leach praised in his seminal publication, a potter’s book, in 1940. this bottle is made in a shape known as meiping (prunus vase), but it was most likely used to store alcohol. the term cizhou encapsulates a range of wares made in several regions of northern china, often consisting of a course stoneware body covered with a white slip (a thin layer of diluted firing clay), and then decorated with a contrasting colour. vessels of this shape have traditionally been referred to as meiping, literally 'prunus vases'.
描述_ZN: 本壺是中國北方宋代(960-1279)製造的一種陶器--慈禧瓷器的例子。 慈溪器皿在生产时是功利性的，而且制作数量相对较多。 然而，这些'梅花瓶'中的一些刻有中文'美酒'二字。 虽然在生产的时候没有得到很高的评价，但是慈禧的大胆设计和简单的造型后来被日本和西方的鉴赏家们所珍视。 英国的工作室陶艺运动发现了像这个花瓶这样的陶瓷的亲和力，伯纳德-利奇在1940年的开创性出版物《陶艺家之书》中称赞了这个花瓶。 这个瓶子的形状被称为梅瓶，但它很可能是用来储存酒精的。 这个术语概括了中国北方几个地区制造的一系列器物，通常由白滑（一层薄薄的稀释的烧制粘土）覆盖的石器主体组成，然后用对比的颜色进行装饰。 这种形状的器皿传统上被称为梅瓶，字面意思是 "梅花瓶"。

描述_EN: shadow puppetry has been immensely popular in china, but due to its universal appeal was forbidden in china between 1796 to 1800, for fear of spreading peasant uprising. its chinese name 'pi ying' means 'shadow of hides' since the puppets were traditionally made from the donkey or ox hide. one operates the puppets, one plays a suo-na horn, and a yu-kin, one plays banhu fiddle, one is in charge of percussion instruments, and one sings. a chinese shadow puppet troupe is made up of five people. chinese shadow puppetry is said to be over 2000 years old.

描述_EN: the the top centre, against a red sky, is the emblem of the peoples' republic of china surrounded by doves. there is a yellow macramé fringe at each end. wall carpet, knotted pile of coloured silks and flat metallic thread worked in the weft-wrapping weave known as pinjin in chinese or soumak in the west. the corners show, from top left clockwise, a bucket of molten steel, a wheatsheaf, cotton bolls and a truck of coal. the pictorial design is one commensurate with the movement known as the great leap forward. below this, dancing on a green sward and encircled by a garland of flowers, grapes and peaches, are representatives of the national minority peoples of china. a soldier from the peoples' liberation army plays the accordion.
描述_ZN: 顶部中心，在红色的天空下，是中国人民共和国的标志，周围有鸽子。 两端有一个黄色的macramé流苏。 墙毯，由彩色丝绸和扁平金属线组成的结堆，在中国称为pinjin或西方称为soumak的纬线包裹编织。 四角显示，从左上角顺时针方向，一桶熔化的钢，一个麦穗，棉花棒和一车煤。 图画设计是与被称为大跃进的运动相称的。 下面是中国少数民族的代表，他们在绿色的草地上跳舞，被鲜花、葡萄和桃子的花环所包围。 一位人民解放军战士在拉手风琴。

描述_EN: the pockets have been tailored to ensure there is no break in this design. sleeveless jackets like this were usually worn over long robes and the slits at the sides allowed for expansion. this waistcoat is made from closely woven black ribbed silk and it has a subdued pattern of lattice roundels woven into it. this waistcoat has shoulder seams and the back is cut from one piece of cloth, which, like the pockets, are a sign of twentieth-century tailoring. the garment is versatile enough to be worn with western clothes and this may well have been how it was used. it was part of the bequest left too the v&a by sir john addis and, as a diplomat in china, he seems to have had several chinese-style garments made especially for him. this was a time when chinese men started wearing western three-piece suits or a mix of chinese and western modes. the match across the sewing lines is meticulous as is that across the fold-line at the top of the pocket. chinese garments did not originally have pockets like these but, by the beginning of the twentieth century, they were being added to traditional styles.
描述_ZN: 口袋是量身定做的，以确保在这个设计中没有断裂。 像这样的无袖夹克通常穿在长袍外面，两侧的缝隙允许扩张。 这件马甲是由紧密编织的黑色罗纹丝制成的，它有一个低调的格子圆形图案编织而成。 这件马甲有肩缝，背部是由一块布裁剪而成的，这和口袋一样，是二十世纪裁缝的标志。 这件衣服的用途很广，可以和西方的衣服一起穿，这很可能就是它的用途。 这是John Addis先生留给V&A的遗产的一部分，作为一名驻中国的外交官，他似乎特别为他制作了几件中国风格的服装。 这是个中国男人开始穿西方三件套或中西方混合模式的时期。 整个缝制线的匹配是一丝不苟的，就像口袋顶部的折线一样。 中国服装最初没有这样的口袋，但到了20世纪初，传统的服装款式中开始有了口袋。

描述_EN: he looks down, with a detached air, expressing a state of meditation. the large mark between his eyebrows, the long earlobes and the headdress are all signs of his high standing and spiritual advancement. like other depictions of guanyin, he wears a diadem featuring the buddha amitabha. this figure sits in a posture of relaxation, often called 'royal ease', deemed fitting for buddhas, bodhisattvas and royalty.
描述_ZN: 他俯视着，带着一种超然的气质，表达了一种冥想的状态。 他眉间的大印，长长的耳垂和头饰都是他地位高和精神进步的标志。 与其他观音菩萨的描述一样，他戴着以阿弥陀佛为主题的头饰。 这个人物以一种放松的姿势坐着，通常被称为 "皇家的轻松"，被认为适合于佛陀、菩萨和皇家。

描述_EN: the term cizhou encapsulates a range of wares made in several regions of northern china, often consisting of a stoneware body decorated with a bold design. ceramic pillows were an important item in the kilns producing cizhou wares, and were made for both funerary use and as a neck support for the living. this pillow is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the stoneware body of this piece has been glazed in a modified version of the sancai three-colour scheme of the tang dynasty, known as song sancai.
描述_ZN: 术语 "Cizhou "概括了中国北方几个地区制造的一系列器物，通常由一个石器主体装饰着大胆的设计。 陶瓷枕头是窑厂生产的重要物品，既可用于葬礼，也可作为生活中的颈部支撑。 这个枕头是贵州器的一个例子，贵州器是中国北方地区在金代（1115-1234）时制造的一种陶瓷。 这件作品的石器主体已经在唐代三彩的改良版中上了釉，被称为宋三彩。

描述_EN: the lines of the peony were then carved out, revealing the buff colour of the body as the background to this striking design. to achieve its effect, a cream slip (a thinned firing clay) was first applied over the body. contrary to the imperial wares of the time, which were prized for their perfection of form and glaze, cizhou wares were made for everyday use and so were more free-spirited in form and design. cizhou is a term used to describe a variety of ceramics made in northern china during the song dynasty (960-1279). this octagonal ceramic pillow is an example of cizhou ware. this pillow is typical of cizhou ware in its bold surface decoration over a stoneware body.
描述_ZN: 然后雕刻出牡丹的线条，揭示了作为这个引人注目的设计的背景的身体的水色。 为了达到其效果，首先在器身上涂抹了奶油滑液（一种稀薄的烧制粘土）。 与当时的御用器物不同，御用器物以其完美的形式和釉面而受到推崇，而慈禧的器物是为日常使用而制作的，因此在形式和设计上更加自由奔放。 在中国北方的宋代（960-1279年）的陶瓷中，"Cizhou "是一个用来描述各种陶瓷的术语。 这个八角形的陶瓷枕头是一个贵州器皿的例子。 这个枕头是典型的贵州器物，它在石器上有大胆的表面装饰。

描述_EN: the central scene depicted is one of four women playing a game of dominoes, with all 32 tiles laid out in a specific formation. the cross in the centre of the embroidery is made up of inverted chinese characters: happiness (‘fu’), prosperity (‘lu’) and longevity (‘shou’). it is also unusual that cotton is used in place of the more commonly used material, silk. the inversion of the characters symbolises ‘the arrival of the three stars of happiness, prosperity and longevity’, as the chinese word for inversion is a homonym for the word for arrival (‘dao’). the patterns that appear on this textile are not often featured on other kinds of textiles. this cotton embroidery may provide some evidence of a folk design that had currency before imperial and aristocratic tastes overtook the visual culture of china. chinese cross-stitch embroideries were made by women at home in preparation for weddings.
描述_ZN: 描绘的中心场景是四个女人在玩多米诺骨牌游戏，所有的32张牌都以特定的队形摆放。 绣品中央的十字架是由倒置的汉字组成的：幸福（'福'）、繁荣（'禄'）和长寿（'寿'）。 用棉布代替更常用的材料丝绸，也是不寻常的。 这些字的倒置象征着 "幸福、繁荣和长寿三星的到来"，因为倒置的中文词与到来的中文词同音（"道"）。 这种纺织品上出现的图案在其他种类的纺织品上不常出现。 这种棉布刺绣可能提供了一些民间设计的证据，这种设计在帝国和贵族的口味笼罩中国的视觉文化之前就已经流行了。 中国的十字绣是妇女在家里为婚礼做的准备。

描述_EN: other symbols contributing to the theme of longevity are the peach, and the butterfly which is the symbol of a person who has attained seventy to eighty years of age. it may have been made to be used as a decorative cover for the surface of a side table. the symbols on the roundel indicate that this would have been used on in interiors for an older person, perhaps even in celebration of a birthday. the previous owner of this piece, bernard vuilleumier, collected chinese textiles such as this one out of an interest in chinese symbols. this is a decorative roundel made of embroidery on panels of woven silk. the central figure is that of the god of longevity, accompanied by a deer (which is also a longevity symbol).
描述_ZN: 其他有助于长寿主题的符号是桃子和蝴蝶，蝴蝶是年满七八十岁的人的象征。 它可能是用来作为边桌表面的装饰性封面的。 圆盘上的符号表明，这应该是用于老年人的室内装饰，甚至可能是为了庆祝生日。 这件作品的前主人Bernard Vuilleumier出于对中国符号的兴趣而收集了像这样的中国纺织品。 这是在编织的丝绸面板上用刺绣做的装饰性圆盘。 中心人物是长寿之神，旁边有一只鹿（这也是长寿的象征）。

描述_EN: in 1126 the hebei province experienced great change as the northern song dynasty ended and the jin dynasty established power. porcelains differ from other ceramics in their impermeability, whiteness after firing and fine texture. the term porcelain is applied to ceramics made from a mixture containing a clay called kaolin and a white stone called petuntse, which was fired at high temperatures. this bowl is an example of ding ware, made in the hebei province of china during the northern song dynasty (960-1127) and jin dynastsy (1115-1127). from the beginning of the jin dynasty, the characteristics of ding wares changed slightly. ding wares were of the earliest true porcelains made in china, and the world. despite such upheaval, ding wares continued to be produced after a short interval as an ‘official ware’, meaning it was selected to supply ceramics to the royal household and the most elite officials in china. instead of the hand-incised decorations which previously adorned its surfaces, its designs began to mimic that of the metal wares of the period through the use of moulded design. the elaborate scene on this dish, portraying two spotted deer amongst swirling clouds and flowers, would have been slow and expensive to achieve without the precision afforded by the mould technique. this was achieved by shaping the clay over domed moulds, which gave the form of the object and impressed the inside pattern onto the clay in one step.
描述_ZN: 1126年，随着北宋王朝的结束和金朝政权的建立，河北经历了巨大的变化。 瓷器与其他陶瓷的不同之处在于其不渗透性、烧制后的白度和精细的纹理。 瓷器这一术语适用于由一种叫做高岭土的粘土和一种叫做petuntse的白色石头的混合物制成的陶瓷，在高温下烧制。 此碗是一个鼎器的例子，在北宋（960-1127）和金代（1115-1127）期间在中国的河北制造。 从金代开始，鼎器的特征发生了微小的变化。 丁器是中国乃至世界上最早的真正的瓷器。 尽管发生了这样的动荡，但在短暂的间隔之后，鼎器作为 "官器 "继续生产，这意味着它被选中为皇家和中国最精英的官员提供陶瓷。 取代了以前装饰在其表面的手工刻画的装饰，其设计开始通过使用模制设计来模仿当时的金属器皿。 这个盘子上精心设计的场景，描绘了两只斑点鹿在旋转的云彩和花朵中，如果没有模具技术提供的精确性，那么实现起来就会很慢而且很昂贵。 这是通过在圆顶模具上塑造粘土来实现的，它赋予了物品的形式，并将里面的图案一步步地印在粘土上。

描述_EN: support for confucian values was important to ruling groups not themselves han chinese, striving to cement their legitimacy as holders of the mandate of heaven. this state was established by a different ethnic group from the majority han chinese. this marble slab probably came from north china, to judge from the costumes of the figures and the tent that is similar to a mongol yurt. these, together with the evidence of a complete tomb lined with such slabs excavated in the north-western province of gansu, show that the slab probably originated in jin dynasty territory. the complete set of slabs probably depicted popular confucian tales later known as the 'twenty four exemplars of filial piety'. it was during this period that this set of tales was being structured, and it often inspired tomb decoration.
描述_ZN: 对儒家价值观的支持对非汉族的统治集团很重要，他们努力巩固自己作为天命持有者的合法性。 这个国家是由一个不同于大多数汉族人的民族建立的。 这块大理石板可能来自中国北方，从人物的服装和类似于蒙古蒙古包的帐篷来判断。 这些，再加上在甘肃省西北部发掘的一个完整的墓葬内有这种石板的证据，表明这块石板可能来自金朝的领土。 整套石板可能描绘了流行的儒家故事，后来被称为 "二十四孝的典范"。 正是在这一时期，这套故事被结构化了，而且它经常激发墓葬的装饰。

描述_EN: this candlestick is an example of yaozhou wares typical of the northern song dynasty (960-1127). while the wares produced at the yaozhou kiln complex enjoyed popularity from the end of the tang dynasty (960-1127) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368), this candlestick is typical of the yaozhou wares of the northern song period in its stoneware body and olive green glaze. when applied to the formed surface of the candlestick, the glaze pooled into the crevices of the clay and ran thin over any raised areas and at the edges. after firing, areas where the glaze ran thick were an opaque olive green and thin areas emerged a paler hue, heightening effect of the actual relief. glaze was an important tool in the design of yaozhou wares.
描述_ZN: 此烛台是北宋时期典型的耀州器皿的一个例子（960-1127）。 从唐朝末年（960-1127）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州窑群生产的器物都很受欢迎，这个烛台是北宋时期耀州器物的典型，它的石器身和橄榄绿釉。 当应用于烛台的成型表面时，釉料积聚在泥土的缝隙中，并在任何凸起的地方和边缘处流淌着薄薄的釉。 烧制后，釉面厚的地方是不透明的橄榄绿，薄的地方出现了较淡的色调，加强了实际的浮雕效果。 釉料是耀州器物设计中的重要工具。

描述_EN: the two dishes pictured here are examples of ceramics probably made at linru, in the henan province of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). a convex ‘hump-mould’ was then made from the master, from which multiple dishes could then be made, saving time and resources. the craftspeople of both yaozhou and linru used moulds to achieve their intricate surface designs some of the time, avoiding the time consumption and labour intensity of hand carving. yaozhou wares were popular for their olive green glazes and their detailed surface designs. during this period, the kilns at linru produced wares that imitated those made at the yaozhou kilns in the neighbouring shaanxi province. this process began with one master dish carved by hand and fired. these wares appear to be very similar to their yaozhou contemporaries, but their glazes have very slight differences in colour and shine that reveal they were probably fired slightly differently.
描述_ZN: 此图中的两个盘子可能是金代（1115-1234）期间在中国河南省临汝制作的陶瓷的例子。 然后用母盘制作一个凸形的 "驼峰模具"，然后用它来制作多个盘子，节省时间和资源。 姚州和临汝的工匠们在某些时候使用模具来实现其复杂的表面设计，避免了手工雕刻的时间消耗和劳动强度。 耀州器物因其橄榄绿的釉面和细致的表面设计而受到欢迎。 在这一时期，林汝窑生产的器物模仿了邻近的陕西省耀州窑的器物。 这个过程从一个手工雕刻和烧制的主盘开始。 这些器物看起来与同时代的耀州器非常相似，但它们的釉面在颜色和光泽上有非常细微的差别，显示出它们的烧制方式可能略有不同。

描述_EN: it may have been made for use in a tomb, or for the neck support of a living owner. the term cizhou encapsulates a range of wares made in several regions of northern china, often consisting of a course stoneware body covered with a white slip (a thin layer of wet clay), and then decorated with a bold design in a contrasting colour. this pillow is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). this technique is used to striking effect in creating the features of this ceramic pillow in the shape of a tiger.
描述_ZN: 它可能是为在墓中使用而制作的，也可能是为活着的主人的颈部提供支撑。 这个术语囊括了中国北方几个地区的一系列器物，通常由白色滑液（一层薄薄的湿粘土）覆盖的石器主体组成，然后用对比色的大胆设计进行装饰。 这个枕头是贵州器的一个例子，贵州器是中国北方地区在金代（1115-1234）时制造的一种陶瓷。 这种技术在创造这个老虎形状的陶瓷枕头的特征中被使用到了惊人的效果。

描述_EN: the wares produced at the yaozhou kiln complex enjoyed popularity from the end of the tang dynasty (618-906) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368), however, this incense burner exhibits the green glaze and stoneware body produced there during the northern song (960-1127) and jin (1115-1234) dynasties. when applied, the glaze pooled into any crevices and ran thin over the raised areas and at the edges. the glaze that gives the green hue and shiny texture to this object is known as a celadon. celadons are feldspathic glazes which derive their colour from the presence of iron oxide when fired in a reduction atmosphere (one with very little oxygen). after firing, areas where the glaze ran thick were an opaque olive green and the thinly covered surfaces emerged a paler hue. in this case, the glaze is crazed slightly, meaning that during firing, the body expanded further than the glaze, giving an underlying crackled texture to the shiny surface of the glaze. this incense burner is an example of yaozhou wares.
描述_ZN: 从唐朝末年（618-906）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州窑群生产的器物一直很受欢迎，然而，这个香炉展示了北宋（960-1127）和金朝（1115-1234）时期生产的绿釉和石器身。 当应用时，釉料汇集到任何缝隙中，并在凸起的地方和边缘处变薄。 赋予该器物绿色色调和光泽纹理的釉料被称为青瓷。 青瓷是一种长石质的釉料，当在还原气氛（含氧量极少）中烧制时，其颜色来自于氧化铁的存在。 烧制后，釉面厚的地方是不透明的橄榄绿，而薄的表面则出现了较淡的色调。 在这种情况下，釉面出现了轻微的裂纹，这意味着在烧制过程中，器身比釉面进一步膨胀，使釉面的光亮表面出现了潜在的裂纹纹理。 这个香炉是耀州器物的一个例子。

描述_EN: a close examination of the object and scientific tests have revealed that the lid is an original production dated about 500-400 bc, while the bottom half of the vessel and the lid handle were made in the 14th century or slightly earlier. this elegant example from the later eastern zhou dynasty (771-221 bc) uses gold inlays to produce a delicate pattern of stylised interlacing dragons. this evidence supports the theory that this piece was conceived for an antiquarian or collector of the song (960-1279) or yuan (1279-1368) dynasty, following the taste for archaic objects developed during the song period. this type of vessel, called a dou in chinese, was routinely cast during the western zhou dynasty (1050-771 bc) for use in ceremonies and death rituals.
描述_ZN: 通过对该物品的仔细检查和科学测试发现，盖子是公元前500-400年的原始产品，而容器的下半部分和盖子的把手是在14世纪或稍早的时候制作的。 这个来自东周晚期（公元前771-221年）的优雅的例子使用黄金镶嵌来产生一个精致的风格化交错的龙的图案。 这一证据支持了这一理论，即这一作品是为宋朝（960-1279）或元朝（1279-1368）的古董商或收藏家构思的，遵循了宋朝时期形成的对古物的品味。 这种类型的容器，在中国被称为斗，在西周时期（公元前1050-771年）经常被铸造，用于仪式和死亡仪式。

描述_EN: the term cizhou encapsulates a range of wares made in several regions of northern china, often consisting of a stoneware body decorated with a bold design. ceramic pillows were an important item in the kilns producing cizhou wares, and were made for both funerary use and as a neck support for the living. this pillow is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the stoneware body of this piece has been glazed in a modified version of the sancai three-colour scheme of the tang dynasty, known as song sancai.
描述_ZN: 术语 "Cizhou "概括了中国北方几个地区制造的一系列器物，通常由一个石器主体装饰着大胆的设计。 陶瓷枕头是窑厂生产的重要物品，既可用于葬礼，也可作为生活中的颈部支撑。 这个枕头是贵州器的一个例子，贵州器是中国北方地区在金代（1115-1234）时制造的一种陶瓷。 这件作品的石器主体已经在唐代三彩的改良版中上了釉，被称为宋三彩。

描述_EN: by the 1950s, it was thriving, making nearly every type of footwear - including leather shoes, casual and formal, bespoke and mass-produced - to cater to the latest fashions in the local and overseas markets. red is the primary colour for traditional chinese wedding ceremonies. today, white wedding dresses are popular, but traditional bridal ensembles are still worn for the performing of rituals in front of parents and ancestors, and during the wedding banquets. the hong kong footwear industry began in the mid-1920s, producing mostly rubber and canvas shoes, and expanded rapidly in the 1930s to meet the growing demands of the export market. this pair of red court shoes would have been worn by the bride to complete an ensemble of a matching jacket and skirt, known as hong gua or ‘red gown.’ the uppers are richly embroidered with a dragon and a phoenix chasing a pearl, worked in highly padded metallic couching on red satin, so that the design stands out in relief. these shoes were handmade by the sun sun shoes factory, located at 32 lyndhurst avenue, hong kong.

描述_EN: this hu was probably one of the great numbers of bronzes cast as altar vessels for buddhist and daoist temples. the inscription tells us that the vessel was made at the city of zhenjiang. the form of the bronze and the style of both decoration and inscription are consistent with a song date. it is both an important documentary piece and an example of average quality song bronzework. it is covered with bands of delicate and intricate patterns that show the influence of both ancient and contemporary design. this vase, of a form known in chinese as hu, has a punched inscription running round its lower body dating it to a time - about 1173 - in the song period.
描述_ZN: 此胡可能是为佛教和道教寺庙铸造的大量青铜器中的一件。 铭文告诉我们，该器皿是在镇江市制造的。 青铜器的形式、装饰和铭文的风格都与宋代一致。 它既是一件重要的文献资料，也是一件质量一般的宋代青铜器的例子。 它上面布满了精致而复杂的花纹，显示了古代和现代设计的影响。 这个花瓶，在中国被称为 "胡"，它的下半身有一个冲孔的铭文，可以追溯到宋代的某个时期--大约1173年。

描述_EN: the term cizhou encapsulates a range of popular wares made in several regions of northern china. ceramic pillows were an important item in the kilns producing cizhou wares, and were made for both funerary use and as a neck support for the living. this pillow would have had special meaning for its owner, as lions were sacred animals to buddhists. this pillow is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the stoneware body of this piece has taken on the shape of a lion through clever use of moulding techniques and its amber glaze.
描述_ZN: 术语 "Cizhou "概括了在中国北部几个地区制造的一系列流行的器物。 陶瓷枕头是窑厂生产的重要物品，既可用于葬礼，也可作为生活中的颈部支撑。 这个枕头对它的主人有特殊的意义，因为狮子是佛教徒的神圣动物。 这个枕头是贵州器的一个例子，贵州器是中国北方地区在金代（1115-1234）时制造的一种陶瓷。 这件作品的石器主体通过巧妙地使用铸模技术和琥珀色的釉面而呈现出狮子的形状。

描述_EN: then, the colourful enamels were painted onto the surface and the whole piece was re-fired to the lower firing temperature of the enamels. as colourful glazes became more popular, potters were limited by the fact that many glazes ran together during firing, blurring their design. around 1200, at various kilns, potters began to initially cover the body with a transparent glaze and fire it to the very high temperatures required for the clay to harden fully. prior to the 13th century, chinese potters created their wares by forming the body of the piece, glazing and then firing it in a kiln. the result of this experiment was to evolve into the elaborate and colourful 'overglaze enamel' designs of later centuries. this bowl is a good example of one of the crucial innovations of the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the history of chinese ceramics is a fascinating story of innovation and discovery.
描述_ZN: 然后，彩色的珐琅彩被涂在表面，整个作品被重新烧到珐琅彩的较低烧制温度。 随着彩色釉料的流行，陶工们受到了限制，因为许多釉料在烧制过程中会跑到一起，模糊了他们的设计。 在1200年左右，在不同的窑场，陶工们开始最初用透明的釉料覆盖器身，并将其烧至粘土完全硬化所需的极高温度。 在13世纪之前，中国的陶艺家通过形成作品的主体，上釉，然后在窑中烧制来创造他们的作品。 这个实验的结果就是演变成了后来几个世纪的精心设计和色彩斑斓的 "釉上彩 "设计。 这个碗是金代（1115-1234）关键创新之一的一个好例子。 中国陶瓷的历史是一个迷人的创新和发现的故事。

描述_EN: lions were sacred animals to buddhists, so this pillow would have had a special meaning for its owner. the term cizhou encapsulates a range of wares made in several regions of northern china, often consisting of a stoneware body decorated with a bold design. ceramic pillows were an important item in the kilns producing cizhou wares, and were made for both funerary use and as a neck support for the living. this pillow is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the jin dynasty (1115-1234). the stoneware body of this piece has taken on the shape of a lion through clever use of moulding and incising techniques, and brightly coloured glazes.
描述_ZN: 狮子是佛教徒的圣物，所以这个枕头对它的主人有特殊的意义。 术语 "Cizhou "概括了中国北方几个地区制造的一系列器物，通常由一个石器主体装饰着大胆的设计。 陶瓷枕头是窑厂生产的重要物品，既可用于葬礼，也可作为生活中的颈部支撑。 这个枕头是贵州器的一个例子，贵州器是中国北方地区在金代（1115-1234）时制造的一种陶瓷。 这件作品的石器主体通过巧妙地使用模压和刻画技术，以及明亮的彩色釉面，呈现出狮子的形状。

描述_EN: when this sculpture arrived at the museum, it contained a lacquer box with offerings of silks, gauze, grain and a bronze mirror. earlier, like all other bodhisattvas, guanyin was depicted in male form. this figure is one of the most popular figures of worship in buddhism – the bodhisattva guanyin, called avalokitesvara in sanskrit. these confirm that the figure was once worshipped in a temple. as the deity of compassion, guanyin was usually shown from the 10th century onwards as a female figure.
描述_ZN: 当这个雕塑到达博物馆时，它包含了一个漆盒，里面有丝绸、纱布、谷物和一面铜镜等供品。 早些时候，像其他所有的菩萨一样，观音是以男性的形式被描绘的。 这个人物是佛教中最受欢迎的崇拜人物之一--观世音菩萨，在梵文中称为阿瓦罗基斯瓦罗。 这些都证实了这尊雕塑曾经在寺庙中被供奉过。 作为慈悲之神，观世音菩萨从10世纪起通常以女性形象出现。

描述_EN: yaozhou wares were widely popular from the end of the tang dynasty (618-906) through to the beginning of the yuan dynasty (1279-1368). the glaze that gives the opaque green hue to this object is known as a celadon. celadons are feldspathic glazes which derive their colour from the presence of iron oxide when fired in a reduction atmosphere (one with very little oxygen). while yaozhou wares are more commonly a translucent green, this jar’s lengthy firing period allowed for faint crystals to form in the glaze, giving it a waxy appearance. this jar is an example of yaozhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the shaanxi province of china.
描述_ZN: 从唐朝末年（618-906）到元朝初年（1279-1368），耀州器广泛流行。 该器物的釉面呈现不透明的绿色，被称为青花瓷。 青瓷是一种长石质的釉料，当在还原气氛（含氧量极少）中烧制时，其颜色来自于氧化铁的存在。 虽然耀州器物通常是半透明的绿色，但这个罐子的漫长烧制时间使得釉面上形成了微弱的晶体，使它呈现出蜡质的外观。 这个罐子是耀州器的一个例子，耀州器是中国陕西省制造的一种陶瓷类型。

描述_EN: it takes the form of a mythical one-horned beast called 'xiniu'. many mirrors had links with the chinese mystical philosophy of taoism. the meaning of the allusion being that miracles can be brought into being by mental activity alone. this beautiful mirror stand seems to combine a practical use perhaps for a lady of leisure, with taoist symbolism. this form of mirror stand represents the classical allusion 'the xiniu longs for the moon', with the mirror being the moon. mirrors in china are associated with ceremonial rites and magic and mysticism, as well as with ordinary cosmetic purposes.
描述_ZN: 它采用了神话中的独角兽的形式，称为 "西牛"。 许多镜子都与中国的神秘主义哲学--道教有联系。 这个典故的意思是，奇迹可以仅仅通过精神活动来实现。 这个美丽的镜架似乎结合了一个实用的用途，也许是一个休闲的女士，和道教的象征意义。 这种形式的镜架代表了经典的典故'西牛贺岁'，镜子就是月亮。 中国的镜子与仪式、魔法和神秘主义有关，也与普通的化妆用途有关。

描述_EN: the roughness of the construction, decoration and glazing suggests that it contained the ashes of a humble person. when associated with the reign name of an emperor the date is unambiguous, but when it is used alone, as in this case, it gives a range of alternative dates. for this object the style and manufacturing techniques suggest three possible dates: 1206, 1266 or 1326 ad. the inscription also contains a date in chinese lunar dating system. the front side of the coffin is incised with the image of a door surrounded by the names of the 'guardian spirits of the four directions': the green dragon of the east, the red bird of the south, the white tiger of the west and the dark warrior of the north, who were meant to protect the deceased in the grave. cremation was not a native chinese tradition, but was introduced to china with the coming of buddhism after the 4th century ad. confucian officials, however, openly rejected cremation, considering the destruction of the body as an evil act against the confucian, and traditionally chinese, value of filial piety. this piece is a ceramic container in the form of a coffin with lid, used to hold the ashes of the deceased. this new practice was first adopted by buddhist monks in monasteries and then gradually extended to lay believers, particularly during the song period (960-1279).
描述_ZN: 从结构、装饰和釉面的粗糙程度来看，它装的是一个卑微的人的骨灰。 当与一个皇帝的名字联系在一起时，日期是明确的，但当它单独使用时，如在本例中，它提供了一个可供选择的日期范围。 对于这件物品，其风格和制造技术表明了三种可能的日期： 1206年、1266年或公元1326年。 该碑文还包含了中国农历年代系统中的一个日期。 棺材的正面刻有一个门的图像，周围有 "四方守护神 "的名字：东方的青龙、南方的红鸟、西方的白虎和北方的黑武士，他们要在坟墓里保护死者。 火葬不是中国本土的传统，而是在公元4世纪后随着佛教的传入而传入中国。 然而，儒家官员公开反对火葬，认为销毁尸体是违反儒家和中国传统的孝道价值观的邪恶行为。 这件作品是一个带盖的棺材形式的陶瓷容器，用来装死者的骨灰。 这种新的做法首先被寺院里的佛教僧侣采用，然后逐渐扩展到非宗教人士，特别是在宋代（960-1279）。

描述_EN: still it demonstrates that the qipao became a classic staple in women's wardrobe, and is a versatile dress that may be adapted to different styles and tastes. by the 1940s, under the influence of western tailoring, the dress had become tailored to be much more form-fitting (and fashionable). on its own, the qipao is itself a modernised form of the dress worn by manchu and han women of the qing dynasty (1644-1911). during the republican period (1911-1949), the qipao was promoted as the dress of modern china, identifiably 'chinese' on the one hand, and moving away from 'feudal' associations with the imperial past. in its earlier form, the modern qipao was relatively loose and comfortable, a symbol of simplicity and frugality. this example, made in the 1960s, retains the loose, comfortable cut of the qipao's earlier style, and may not have been considered fashionable for younger audiences. the dress is made in warm thick rayon, and may have been intended to be worn in cooler seasons.
描述_ZN: 但它表明旗袍已经成为女性衣橱里的经典主食，是一种可以适应不同风格和品味的多功能礼服。 到了1940年代，在西方裁缝的影响下，这种衣服变得更加合身（和时尚）。 就其本身而言，旗袍本身是清朝（1644-1911年）满汉妇女所穿服装的一种现代形式。 在共和国时期（1911-1949），旗袍被宣传为现代中国的服装，一方面可以识别为 "中国人"，另一方面也摆脱了与帝国时代的 "封建 "联系。 在其早期形式中，现代旗袍是相对宽松和舒适的，是简单和节俭的象征。 这个例子是在20世纪60年代制作的，保留了旗袍早期风格的宽松、舒适的剪裁，对于年轻的观众来说可能不被认为是时尚的。 这件衣服是由温暖的厚人造纤维制成的，可能是为了在凉爽的季节穿着。

描述_EN: the shape of the vessel, characterised by a hemispherical bowl on a high stem, was extensively reproduced during the song dynasty (960-1279) when a taste for archaic objects was shared by the imperial court and wealthy élites. the tiny interlaced snake-like creatures, which decorate many eastern zhou bronzes, are used on this example as background to a pattern of small protruding beads distributed symmetrically on the surface. during the western zhou dynasty (1050-771 bc) it became routine to cast these vessels in bronze and use them in various ceremonies and death rituals. this traditional vessel, called a dou in chinese, was produced between 525-475 bc during the eastern zhou period (771-221 bc). vessels of this sort had been produced since the neolithic period (5000-1700 bc), but were typically made of ceramic in many regions of china.
描述_ZN: 此器形状的特点是高柄半球形碗，在宋朝（960-1279）期间被广泛复制，当时朝廷和富有的贵族们都喜欢古物。 小的交错的蛇形生物，装饰了许多东周的青铜器，在这个例子中，作为背景，小的突出的珠子图案对称地分布在表面上。 在西周时期（公元前1050-771年），用青铜铸造这些器皿并将其用于各种仪式和死亡仪式成为惯例。 这种传统的器皿，在中国被称为斗，是在公元前525-475年的东周时期（公元前771-221年）生产的。 这种容器从新石器时代（公元前5000-1700年）就开始生产了，但在中国的许多地区通常是由陶瓷制成的。

描述_EN: in addition to bolts of cloth, court robes were often sent from china to tibet in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries where they were refitted into a style of dress worn by lay aristocrats. close examination of the dragons on the upper part of this robe reveals that parts of their bodies do not match precisely, which suggests that this garment was either made from a larger one or pieced together from different robes. such reworking illustrates the value awarded to chinese textiles in tibet at the time.
描述_ZN: 除了布疋，宫廷长袍在十八和十九世纪经常从中国被送到西藏，在那里它们被改装成非专业贵族穿的衣服样式。 仔细观察这件袍子上部的龙，发现它们的部分身体并不完全吻合，这表明这件衣服要么是由一个更大的袍子制成，要么是由不同的袍子拼接而成。 这种再加工说明了当时西藏对中国纺织品的重视。

描述_EN: the ensemble was doubled in orange-yellow satin. the mantle of the four officers who administered the order-chancellor, provost master of ceremonies, grand treasurer, clerk-secretary-was similar to that of the knights except that it was not embroidered with the order's collar all around. black silk velvet, embroidered with gold and silver: flame pattern all over. upper part hidden by a large collar or mantelet (or epitoge) of green silver cloth (or green velvet?) embroidered with the same motifs.
描述_ZN: 的合奏是用橙黄色的缎子加倍的。 管理骑士团的四位官员--大法官、司仪长、大司库、书记员--的斗篷与骑士团的斗篷相似，只是没有在四周绣上骑士团的领子。 黑色丝绒，绣有金色和银色的图案：全身都是火焰图案。 上半部分被一个绣有相同图案的绿色银布（或绿色天鹅绒）的大项圈或曼特莱（或表记）所掩盖。

The center of the square is decorated with a small, plain dark blue border, followed by a regular network of small, adjacent rhombuses, created with a shuttle. 描述_EN: eg.cpt.223 a: this fragment comprises a large part of the upper half of the original square. eg.cpt.223 b: this piece of tapestry comes from the right-hand side of the square's border. the highly stylized figure is probably a nereid seated on a fabulous aquatic animal. A small part of two medallions remain, but their iconography is no longer legible, as well as a fine frieze forming a final border is formed by the repetition of small outward-pointing triangles. il is composed of the remains of a framing border decorated with plants, animals and an offering-bearing putto inscribed in medallions, and the central scene enclosed within a circle, a large part of which remains. two fragments belonging to the same tapestry square are listed under inventory no. eg.cpt.223.
描述_ZN: eg.cpt.223 a: 这块碎片包括原广场上半部分的一大部分。 eg.cpt.223 b: 这块挂毯来自广场边框的右侧。 高度风格化的人物可能是一个坐在神话般的水生动物上的Nereid。 两个奖章的一小部分被保留下来，但它们的图案已无法辨认，还有一个形成最后边界的精美门楣，是由重复的小的外向三角形形成的。 年，它由一个边框的遗迹组成，边框上装饰着植物、动物和一个带着铭文的祭品的普陀，中心场景被围在一个圆圈中，其中很大一部分被保存下来。 属于同一挂毯广场的两块碎片被列在库存号eg.cpt.223下。

描述_EN: according to the inventory amn/ *10 dd 14, "before the date, the name of the Fatimid caliph mustansir (427-487)". above and below, two lines of a kufic inscription. above and below, two lines of a kufic inscription; on one side, bismillah ("in the name of god"), on the other, the date 448 (of the hegira = 1056). horizontal band, multicolored silks and linen, decorated with three medallions, two with red backgrounds and one with blue, each containing a griffin. fragment of tiraz, embroidery that adorned the robes of honor offered by the sovereign. in the spandrels, a double scroll motif appears on a blue background. at center, horizontal band decorated with three medallions each containing a winged quadruped.
描述_ZN: 根据库存amn/ *10 dd 14，"在日期之前，法蒂玛王朝哈里发mustansir（427-487）的名字"。 上下，两行库法铭文。 上下两行Kufic铭文；一边是bismillah（"以上帝的名义"），另一边是448年（hegira=1056）的日期。 水平带，用多色丝绸和亚麻布装饰，有三个奖章，两个红底，一个蓝底，每个都有一个狮鹫。 提拉兹碎片，装饰君主给予的荣誉袍的刺绣。 在翼板上，蓝色背景上勾勒出一个双卷轴图案。 在中心位置，横带装饰有三个奖章，每个奖章都有一个带翅膀的四足动物。

描述_EN: large linen fragment, one side of which is made using the bouclé technique, adorned with a monochrome tapestry medallion. This wine-red yoke features a stylized plant motif created with a shuttle: several geometrical leaf-like motifs on stems surround a central medallion, also featuring a similar motif. One of the original short sides of this fragmentary canvas remains; it is decorated across its entire width with a strip of linen canvas, then an openwork strip, a second strip of linen canvas, and ends with bangs.
描述_ZN: 大块的亚麻布碎片，其中一面是用bouclé技术制作的，装饰着单色的挂毯徽章。 这个酒红色的轭状物上有一个用梭子制作的风格化的植物图案：几个几何形状的茎叶状图案围绕着一个中央奖章，也有一个类似的图案。 这块残缺不全的画布的一个原始短边保存了下来；它的整个宽度上都有一条亚麻布条的装饰，然后是一个镂空条，第二个亚麻布条，最后是流苏的装饰。

描述_EN: eg.cpt.223 a: this fragment comprises a large part of the upper half of the original square. eg.cpt.223 b: this piece of tapestry comes from the right-hand side of the square's border. the highly stylized figure is probably a nereid seated on a fabulous aquatic animal. A small part of two medallions remain, but their iconography is no longer legible, as well as a fine frieze forming a final border is formed by the repetition of small outward-pointing triangles. il is composed of the remains of a framing border decorated with plants, animals and an offering-bearing putto inscribed in medallions, and the central scene enclosed within a circle, a large part of which remains. two fragments belonging to the same tapestry square are listed under inventory no. eg.cpt.223.
描述_ZN: eg.cpt.223 a: 这块碎片包括原广场上半部分的一大部分。 eg.cpt.223 b: 这块挂毯来自广场边框的右侧。 高度风格化的人物可能是一个坐在神话般的水生动物上的Nereid。 两个奖章的一小部分被保留下来，但它们的图案已无法辨认，还有一个形成最后边界的精美门楣，是由重复的小的外向三角形形成的。 年，它由一个边框的遗迹组成，边框上装饰着植物、动物和一个带着铭文的祭品的普陀，中心场景被围在一个圆圈中，其中很大一部分被保存下来。 属于同一挂毯广场的两块碎片被列在库存号eg.cpt.223下。

描述_EN: the buckle, large and oval, has a hinged and chased pin. Germany, 15th century. the decoration is inlaid with seventeen blue stones. The other part of the trim features the ferret with the charity on it and two lion's heads holding a chain with a small ball hanging from its end. golden brass belt buckle and ferret, fitted to a red velvet belt with small gold braid. each is decorated with two flamboyant-style windows, edged with acanthus leaves joined by blue stones. the trim comprises two parts, one longer than the other and fitted with the buckle. elle is decorated with justice in the middle of an openwork frieze of foliage. on one side, the figures of faith and prudence; on the other, those of temperance and strength. the cartouche of the long piece bears an inscription in Gothic characters: georg denabach.
描述_ZN: 大的、椭圆形的扣子有一个铰链式的、凹陷的针。 德国，15世纪。 的装饰上镶嵌了17颗蓝宝石。 另一部分修饰包括上面有慈善机构的雪貂和两个狮子头拿着一条链子，链子的末端挂着一个小球。 鎏金铜扣和皮带箍，装在有小金辫的红色天鹅绒皮带上。 每一个都有两个浮夸风格的窗户，边缘是由蓝色石头连接的刺桐叶。 饰带由两部分组成，一部分比另一部分长，并配有带扣。 他在一个镂空的叶子楣中间装饰着正义。 一边是信仰和谨慎的形象；另一边是节制和力量的形象。 长条形图案上有一个哥特式字体的铭文：Georg Denabach。

描述_EN: the buckle, large and oval, has a hinged and chased pin. Germany, 15th century. the decoration is inlaid with seventeen blue stones. The other part of the trim features the ferret with the charity on it and two lion's heads holding a chain with a small ball hanging from its end. golden brass belt buckle and ferret, fitted to a red velvet belt with small gold braid. each is decorated with two flamboyant-style windows, edged with acanthus leaves joined by blue stones. the trim comprises two parts, one longer than the other and fitted with the buckle. elle is decorated with justice in the middle of an openwork frieze of foliage. on one side, the figures of faith and prudence; on the other, those of temperance and strength. the cartouche of the long piece bears an inscription in Gothic characters: georg denabach.
描述_ZN: 大的、椭圆形的扣子有一个铰链式的、凹陷的针。 德国，15世纪。 的装饰上镶嵌了17颗蓝宝石。 另一部分修饰包括上面有慈善机构的雪貂和两个狮子头拿着一条链子，链子的末端挂着一个小球。 鎏金铜扣和皮带箍，装在有小金辫的红色天鹅绒皮带上。 每一个都有两个浮夸风格的窗户，边缘是由蓝色石头连接的刺桐叶。 饰带由两部分组成，一部分比另一部分长，并配有带扣。 他在一个镂空的叶子楣中间装饰着正义。 一边是信仰和谨慎的形象；另一边是节制和力量的形象。 长条形图案上有一个哥特式字体的铭文：Georg Denabach。
